question: During the reigns of which four kings of Judah did Isaiah the son of Amoz receive his prophetic visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in Isaiah 1:1?
opt1: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
opt2: Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, and Jehoshaphat
opt3: Amaziah, Joash, Manasseh, and Amon
opt4: Josiah, Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah
correct: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
explanation: Isaiah's prophetic ministry spanned four consecutive Judahite monarchs from the late eighth century BC down to the Assyrian crisis under Hezekiah. Isaiah 1:1 (KJV) - "The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah."

question: What domestic animals are contrasted with Israel's unthinking rebellion against God in Isaiah 1:3?
opt1: The sheep followeth the shepherd, and the camel his keeper: but Judah hath gone astray
opt2: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider
opt3: The horse obeyeth the bridle, and the mule his driver: but Ephraim hath broken the yoke
opt4: The goat recognizeth the fold, and the dog his feeder: but Zion hath forgotten her maker
correct: The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider
explanation: Dumb domestic draft beasts possess an instinctive recognition of their masters, yet Israel fails to discern or acknowledge its divine provider. Isaiah 1:3 (KJV) - "The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider."

question: What medical metaphor portrays the systemic spiritual corruption and moral decay of Judah in Isaiah 1:5-6?
opt1: A leprous hand that cannot be cleansed, and blind eyes that cannot behold the daylight
opt2: A broken bone that will not knit, and a fever that consumeth the marrow of the joints
opt3: The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint; from the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores
opt4: A poisoned fountain drying up the veins, and a gangrene eating the flesh of the body
correct: The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint; from the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores
explanation: The nation is depicted as a battered body covered in unbandaged, suppurating wounds from head to foot, illustrating total depravity. Isaiah 1:5-6 (KJV) - "Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment."

question: To what fragile agricultural shelters is the desolate, besieged 'daughter of Zion' compared in Isaiah 1:8?
opt1: As a broken watchtower in an olive orchard, as a threshing floor swept by the whirlwind
opt2: As a shepherd's tent in the barren wilderness, as a cistern cracked by the summer heat
opt3: As an abandoned sheepfold on the rocky hills, as a desolate sheepcote near the Dead Sea
opt4: As a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city
correct: As a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city
explanation: Zion sits isolated and defenseless amidst devastation, resembling a flimsy temporary hut left abandoned in a harvested melon or cucumber patch. Isaiah 1:8 (KJV) - "And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city."

question: What theological doctrine preserves Judah from suffering the absolute annihilation of Sodom and Gomorrah in Isaiah 1:9?
opt1: Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah
opt2: Because of the covenant of circumcision and the perpetual bloodline of King David
opt3: Because of the golden vessels preserved within the holy sanctuary of Solomon
opt4: Because of the intercession of the priests offering evening sacrifices upon the altar
correct: Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah
explanation: Only the sovereign grace of Yahweh Sabaoth in preserving an election of grace ('a very small remnant') spared Judah from the total extinction of Sodom. Isaiah 1:9 (KJV) - "Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah."

question: Why does the LORD declare His abhorrence of Judah's elaborate liturgical sacrifices, new moons, and assemblies in Isaiah 1:13-15?
opt1: Because they sacrificed unblemished rams without sprinkling salt upon the grain offering
opt2: Because it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting; their hands are full of blood, and He cannot endure vain oblations combined with wickedness
opt3: Because they failed to remit the temple tithes to the sons of Zadok during the exile
opt4: Because they offered incense upon foreign altars on the high places of Samaria
correct: Because it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting; their hands are full of blood, and He cannot endure vain oblations combined with wickedness
explanation: Hypocritical ritualism devoid of moral justice is repulsive to God; their outstretched hands of prayer are stained with social oppression and blood. Isaiah 1:13-15 (KJV) - "Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting ... And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood."

question: What famous divine invitation offers total redemptive cleansing from deeply ingrained sin in Isaiah 1:18?
opt1: Offer unto God the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay thy vows unto the Most High in righteousness
opt2: Turn ye unto me with fasting and weeping, and rend your garments before the holy veil
opt3: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool
opt4: Bring your silver into the storehouse, and prove me now herewith if I will not open the heavens
correct: Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool
explanation: Yahweh invites Judah into legal-covenantal dialogue ('let us reason together'), promising that deep indelible stains of bloodguilt can be transformed into snow-like purity. Isaiah 1:18 (KJV) - "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool."

question: What metallurgical and viticultural metaphors describe Jerusalem's moral debasement in Isaiah 1:22?
opt1: Thy gold is covered with rust, thy oil contaminated with clay
opt2: Thy bronze is decayed into iron, thy honey turned to vinegar
opt3: Thy jewels are swallowed by dust, thy vineyards trampled by swine
opt4: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water
correct: Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water
explanation: The city's noble character has deteriorated into useless scum (dross) and diluted, adulterated wine, signaling compromised integrity. Isaiah 1:22 (KJV) - "Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water:"

question: What restorative titles will be bestowed upon Jerusalem after God purges her dross in Isaiah 1:25-26?
opt1: The city of righteousness, the faithful city
opt2: The throne of the Great King, the perfection of beauty
opt3: The joy of the whole earth, the inviolable sanctuary
opt4: The fortress of peace, the fountain of living waters
correct: The city of righteousness, the faithful city
explanation: Following divine refinement and the restoration of righteous judges, Jerusalem will regain her lost titles of integrity: the city of righteousness and the faithful city. Isaiah 1:26 (KJV) - "And I will restore thy judges as at the first, and thy counsellors as at the beginning: afterward thou shalt be called, The city of righteousness, the faithful city."

question: In what idolatrous cultic groves will the apostate rebels be ashamed and confounded in Isaiah 1:29-30?
opt1: The high cedars of Lebanon and the terraces of Mount Hermon
opt2: The oaks which ye have desired, and the gardens that ye have chosen: for ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water
opt3: The caves of En-gedi and the palm groves of Jericho
opt4: The standing stones of Bethel and the altars of Dan
correct: The oaks which ye have desired, and the gardens that ye have chosen: for ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water
explanation: Pagan nature cults celebrated under sacred terebinths and lush gardens will yield spiritual barrenness, with the worshippers becoming withered like dry gardens. Isaiah 1:29-30 (KJV) - "For they shall be ashamed of the oaks which ye have desired, and ye shall be confounded for the gardens that ye have chosen. For ye shall be as an oak whose leaf fadeth, and as a garden that hath no water."

question: In the eschatological vision of Isaiah 2:2, what supreme prominence will the mountain of the LORD's house attain in the last days?
opt1: It shall be surrounded by twelve golden ramparts, and all kings shall send tributes of cedar
opt2: It shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it
opt3: It shall split the Mount of Olives into a great valley, and a river of life shall issue forth
opt4: It shall burn with perpetual unconsumed fire, and the tribes of Jacob shall encamp around it
correct: It shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it
explanation: Mount Zion is elevated as the cosmic and spiritual zenith of the earth, drawing all gentile nations in an upward pilgrimage to worship Yahweh. Isaiah 2:2 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD's house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it."

question: What divine revelation will emanate globally from Jerusalem to instruct the gathering nations in Isaiah 2:3?
opt1: For from the altar shall issue the sacrificial fire, and the holy anointing oil from the sanctuary
opt2: For out of the palace of David shall proceed imperial decrees, and royal tax collectors to all borders
opt3: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem
opt4: For from the temple court shall blow the silver trumpets, and the Levitical choir shall instruct the earth
correct: For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem
explanation: Zion serves as the global source for divine covenant instruction (Torah) and the prophetic word of the LORD. Isaiah 2:3 (KJV) - "And many people shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem."

question: What universal disarmament and pacification of warfare is prophesied under the Lord's international arbitration in Isaiah 2:4?
opt1: They shall burn their shields in the fire for seven years, and melt their chariots into temple vessels
opt2: They shall cast their bows into the sea, and convert their fortresses into royal granaries
opt3: They shall surrender their armories to the high priest, and pledge eternal treaties of non-aggression
opt4: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more
correct: They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more
explanation: Weapons of violence are converted into agricultural tools, inaugurating an era of permanent international peace under divine rule. Isaiah 2:4 (KJV) - "And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more."

question: What foreign occult and religious syncretism brought divine judgment upon the house of Jacob in Isaiah 2:6?
opt1: They be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers
opt2: They imported the astrological tables of Babylon, and set up shrines of Chemosh in the Kidron valley
opt3: They adopted the hieroglyphic mysteries of Egypt, and worshipped the golden calf at Gilgal
opt4: They embraced the human sacrifices of the Ammonites, and burned incense upon Mount Gerizim
correct: They be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers
explanation: Judah compromised her covenantal purity by absorbing eastern divination, Philistine occult arts, and foreign pagan alliances. Isaiah 2:6 (KJV) - "Therefore thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east, and are soothsayers like the Philistines, and they please themselves in the children of strangers."

question: What material and military self-sufficiency seduced Judah into idolatrous security in Isaiah 2:7-8?
opt1: Their storehouses overflow with grain from the Nile, and their garrisons are filled with foreign mercenaries
opt2: Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots: their land also is full of idols
opt3: Their harbors are packed with merchant vessels from Tyre, and their palace is overlaid with ivory
opt4: Their cities are fortified with double walls of stone, and their towers reach unto the clouds
correct: Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots: their land also is full of idols
explanation: Material wealth, excessive cavalry, and manufactured idols directly violated Deuteronomy 17:16-17, leading Judah into proud apostasy. Isaiah 2:7-8 (KJV) - "Their land also is full of silver and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures; their land is also full of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots: Their land also is full of idols; they worship the work of their own hands, that which their own fingers have made:"

question: What will happen to human arrogance when the LORD alone is exalted in that day according to Isaiah 2:11?
opt1: The wise of the earth shall hide their faces, and the princes of the nations shall fall by the sword
opt2: The kings of Tarshish shall cast off their crowns, and the priests shall weep between the porch and altar
opt3: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day
opt4: The rich shall surrender their silver, and the mighty warriors shall flee without their weapons
correct: The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day
explanation: Every expression of human pride will be cast down so that Yahweh's majesty alone reigns preeminent. Isaiah 2:11 (KJV) - "The lofty looks of man shall be humbled, and the haughtiness of men shall be bowed down, and the LORD alone shall be exalted in that day."

question: Against what natural grandeur and maritime achievements will the day of the LORD of hosts be unleashed in Isaiah 2:13-16?
opt1: Upon the vineyards of En-gedi, the olive trees of Carmel, the fortresses of Lachish, and the fleet of Ezion-geber
opt2: Upon the forests of Gilead, the plains of Sharon, the towers of Hebron, and the merchant caravans of Sheba
opt3: Upon the palms of Jericho, the hills of Samaria, the gates of Damascus, and the trading barges of the Euphrates
opt4: Upon all the cedars of Lebanon that are high and lifted up, upon all the oaks of Bashan, upon all high mountains, upon every high tower, and upon all the ships of Tarshish
correct: Upon all the cedars of Lebanon that are high and lifted up, upon all the oaks of Bashan, upon all high mountains, upon every high tower, and upon all the ships of Tarshish
explanation: God's judgment levels everything exalted in nature (cedars, oaks, mountains) and human technological pride (towers, fortified walls, magnificent ships). Isaiah 2:13-16 (KJV) - "And upon all the cedars of Lebanon, that are high and lifted up, and upon all the oaks of Bashan, And upon all the high mountains, and upon all the hills that are lifted up, And upon every high tower, and upon every fenced wall, And upon all the ships of Tarshish, and upon all pleasant pictures."

question: Where will terrified humanity seek refuge from the glory of the LORD's majesty when He ariseth to shake terribly the earth in Isaiah 2:19?
opt1: Into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth
opt2: Into the inner chambers of their palaces, and into the deep cellars of their towers
opt3: Across the great sea to distant islands, and behind the thick walls of Babylon
opt4: Beneath the altars of their idols, and into the dense thickets of the desert
correct: Into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth
explanation: Humanity's desperate attempt to escape divine judgment drives them into subterrene crevices and mountain caverns. Isaiah 2:19 (KJV) - "And they shall go into the holes of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, for fear of the LORD, and for the glory of his majesty, when he ariseth to shake terribly the earth."

question: To what repulsive subterranean creatures will men cast their useless idols of silver and gold in Isaiah 2:20?
opt1: To the scorpions and to the serpents
opt2: To the moles and to the bats
opt3: To the worms and to the jackals
opt4: To the ravens and to the vultures
correct: To the moles and to the bats
explanation: The manufactured gods of precious metal are discarded as worthless refuse into dark caverns inhabited by moles and bats. Isaiah 2:20 (KJV) - "In that day a man shall cast his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which they made each one for himself to worship, to the moles and to the bats;"

question: What sobering anthropological warning concludes the judgment oracle of Isaiah 2:22?
opt1: Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help
opt2: For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass
opt3: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?
opt4: Trust ye in the LORD forever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength
correct: Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?
explanation: Mankind is finite, fragile, and wholly dependent on the temporary breath in his nostrils; trusting in human power is folly. Isaiah 2:22 (KJV) - "Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?"

question: What fundamental physical and civil supports does the Lord, the LORD of hosts, strip away from Jerusalem and Judah in Isaiah 3:1?
opt1: The walls and the ramparts, the royal treasury of silver, and the armory of bronze
opt2: The temple choir, the altar of burnt offerings, and the morning incense
opt3: The stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water
opt4: The trade routes of the north, the olive presses of the south, and the vineyards of the valley
correct: The stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water
explanation: God dismantles the essential pillars of life, depriving the nation of basic physical sustenance: all bread and water. Isaiah 3:1 (KJV) - "For, behold, the Lord, the LORD of hosts, doth take away from Jerusalem and from Judah the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water,"

opt1: The high priest, the Levites of the sanctuary, the royal scribes, and the keepers of the gate

explanation: The entire leadership infrastructure - military, legal, prophetic, intellectual, and technical - is systematically eliminated. question: What sociological inversion and collapse of order occurs when mature leadership vanishes in Isaiah 3:4-5?
opt1: I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them; the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable

correct: I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them; the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable

Isaiah 3:4-5 (KJV) - "And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them. And the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour: the child shall behave himself proudly against the ancient, and the base against the honourable."

explanation: The societal breakdown is so acute that merely owning an extra cloak makes a man eligible for high office, yet even he refuses the burden. Isaiah 3:6-7 (KJV) - "When a man shall take hold of his brother of the house of his father, saying, Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand: In that day shall he swear, saying, I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people."

question: What primary theological cause explains why Jerusalem is ruined and Judah is fallen in Isaiah 3:8?
opt1: Because the Assyrian army possessed superior iron chariots and siege engines

correct: Because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory
explanation: National collapse is the direct consequence of rebellious speech and unrighteous actions that blatantly defy God's glorious presence. Isaiah 3:8 (KJV) - "For Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen: because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory."

question: Like what infamous ancient city do the unrepentant people of Judah shamelessly flaunt their open sin in Isaiah 3:9?

Isaiah 3:9 (KJV) - "The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves."

question: What dual moral antithesis establishes the contrasting eternal destinies of the righteous and the wicked in Isaiah 3:10-11?
opt1: Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings. Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him

explanation: God's unchanging moral law guarantees retribution: the righteous will enjoy the fruit of righteousness, while the wicked reap ruin. Isaiah 3:10-11 (KJV) - "Say ye to the righteous, that it shall be well with him: for they shall eat the fruit of their doings. Woe unto the wicked! it shall be ill with him: for the reward of his hands shall be given him."

question: What indictments does Yahweh bring against the elders and princes concerning the exploitation of the poor in Isaiah 3:14-15?

explanation: Judah's aristocratic elite devoured the nation's resources ('eaten up the vineyard') and ruthlessly crushed the vulnerable poor. What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith the Lord GOD of hosts."

question: What haughty mannerisms and flirtatious vanity characterize the daughters of Zion in Isaiah 3:16?
opt1: They adorn their garments with Tyrian purple, and dance before the shrines of Ashtoreth
opt2: They wear crowns of beaten gold, and pour costly perfumes upon their hair
opt3: They are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet
opt4: They refuse the spinning of wool, and recline upon couches of ivory in the palace
correct: They are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet
explanation: Isaiah condemns the aristocratic women for their haughty postures, seductive glances, affected gait, and noisy ankle ornaments. Isaiah 3:16 (KJV) - "Moreover the LORD saith, Because the daughters of Zion are haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes, walking and mincing as they go, and making a tinkling with their feet:"

question: What five dramatic reversals of luxury and beauty will replace the vanity of the daughters of Zion in Isaiah 3:24?
opt1: Instead of fine linen rags; instead of gold chains iron fetters; instead of wine bitter gall; instead of mirth weeping; and shame instead of glory
opt2: Instead of perfume ashes; instead of bracelets thorns; instead of silk haircloth; instead of singing lamentation; and leprosy instead of honor
opt3: Instead of royal sandals barefoot exile; instead of mirrors blindness; instead of jewels stones; instead of dancing mourning; and dust instead of grace
opt4: Instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; instead of a girdle a rent; instead of well set hair baldness; instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty
correct: Instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; instead of a girdle a rent; instead of well set hair baldness; instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty
explanation: Five catastrophic reversals illustrate war's humiliation: stench for perfume, torn ropes for belts, baldness for ornate hair, sackcloth for luxury robes, and captive branding for beauty. Isaiah 3:24 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass, that instead of sweet smell there shall be stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness; and instead of a stomacher a girding of sackcloth; and burning instead of beauty."

question: What desperate appeal do seven women make to a single surviving man due to the catastrophic wartime slaughter of men in Isaiah 4:1?
opt1: We will give thee our silver and our inheritance: only defend our gates from the foreign conqueror
opt2: We will serve thee as handmaids in thy house: only deliver our sons from captivity in Babylon
opt3: We will build thee a fortress of cedar: only offer prayers for our households at the altar
opt4: We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach
correct: We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach
explanation: Because war decimated Judah's male population, women wave all customary marital financial support, pleading only for marriage to remove the social stigma of being childless and unmarried. Isaiah 4:1 (KJV) - "And in that day seven women shall take hold of one man, saying, We will eat our own bread, and wear our own apparel: only let us be called by thy name, to take away our reproach."

question: What Messianic title and earthly restoration are heralded as beautiful, glorious, excellent, and comely in Isaiah 4:2?
opt1: The branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel
opt2: The scepter of David shall arise in triumph, and the vineyards of Judah shall produce vintage wine
opt3: The horn of salvation shall be lifted on Mount Zion, and the holy temple shall be rebuilt with onyx
opt4: The rod of Jesse shall smite the oppressor, and the wilderness shall blossom like the lily
correct: The branch of the LORD shall be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel
explanation: The Messianic 'Branch of the LORD' (Tzemach Yahweh) represents divine restoration and glorious fruitfulness for the surviving remnant of Israel. Isaiah 4:2 (KJV) - "In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel."

question: What holy status and divine registration will characterize the surviving remnant in Zion and Jerusalem in Isaiah 4:3?
opt1: They shall be anointed as royal priests, and their names shall be engraved upon the twelve breastplate stones
opt2: He that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem
opt3: They shall be called the pillars of truth, and their generations shall never be moved from the holy soil
opt4: They shall be designated the redeemed of Jacob, and shall inherit the double portion of the land
correct: He that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem
explanation: The preserved remnant is consecrated as 'holy' (kadosh), recorded in the heavenly book of life among the living in Jerusalem. Isaiah 4:3 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy, even every one that is written among the living in Jerusalem:"

question: By what twin supernatural agents will the Lord wash away the moral filth and bloodguilt of Jerusalem in Isaiah 4:4?
opt1: By the blood of bulls, and by the ashes of an heifer sprinkled upon the altar
opt2: By the river of living water, and by the wind of the desert sweeping the sanctuary
opt3: By the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning
opt4: By the word of the prophets, and by the sharp two-edged sword of the cherubim
correct: By the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning
explanation: Divine cleansing requires radical moral purge through God's penetrating judicial discernment ('spirit of judgment') and refining fire ('spirit of burning'). Isaiah 4:4 (KJV) - "When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning."

question: What Exodus-like divine manifestations will be created over every dwelling place and assembly of Mount Zion in Isaiah 4:5?
opt1: A pillar of alabaster by day, and twelve golden lamps by night
opt2: A rainbow of covenant mercy by day, and the bright morning star by night
opt3: A canopy of woven purple by day, and the sound of silver harps by night
opt4: A cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence
correct: A cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence
explanation: The wilderness pillar of cloud and fire is renewed over every home and gathering in Zion, forming a protective bridal canopy (chuppah) over God's glory. Isaiah 4:5 (KJV) - "And the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence."

question: What three environmental and climatic protections does the heavenly tabernacle provide in Isaiah 4:6?
opt1: A shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain
opt2: A shield from the locust, a barrier against drought, and a wall against foreign armies
opt3: A shelter from the pestilence, an hiding place from the sword, and safety from the famine
opt4: A defence from the arrow by day, a terror against wild beasts, and deliverance from midnight fear
correct: A shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain
explanation: God's tabernacle serves as a complete sanctuary from searing heat, violent tempests, and torrential rains. Isaiah 4:6 (KJV) - "And there shall be a tabernacle for a shadow in the daytime from the heat, and for a place of refuge, and for a covert from storm and from rain."

question: To whom does the promised fruitfulness of the earth exclusively belong in Isaiah 4:2?
opt1: For all the inhabitants of the Mediterranean coastlands
opt2: For them that are escaped of Israel
opt3: For the mighty warriors who defend the gates of Jerusalem
opt4: For the wealthy merchants who offer gifts in the temple
correct: For them that are escaped of Israel
explanation: The blessing of Messianic renewal is reserved strictly for the purified remnant - those who have escaped the purifying judgments of God. Isaiah 4:2 (KJV) - "In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the earth shall be excellent and comely for them that are escaped of Israel."

question: What specific civic and moral stain is explicitly named alongside the 'filth of the daughters of Zion' in Isaiah 4:4?
opt1: The silver of oppression from the marketplace
opt2: The idols of wood from the high places
opt3: The blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof
opt4: The false oaths of the corrupt judges
correct: The blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof
explanation: The Lord purges both sexual/moral corruption ('filth of the daughters of Zion') and violent civic injustice and murder ('the blood of Jerusalem'). Isaiah 4:4 (KJV) - "When the Lord shall have washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion, and shall have purged the blood of Jerusalem from the midst thereof by the spirit of judgment, and by the spirit of burning."

question: What Hebrew architectural and covenantal concept is implied by the phrase 'upon all the glory shall be a defence' in Isaiah 4:5?
opt1: A high battlement of cut granite surrounding the outer courts
opt2: An iron gate guarded by the captains of the heavenly host
opt3: A bronze shield suspended above the ark of the covenant
opt4: A protective bridal canopy or canopy of divine glory shielding the sanctified community
correct: A protective bridal canopy or canopy of divine glory shielding the sanctified community
explanation: The Hebrew word chuppah indicates a protective royal and marital canopy spread over the redeemed city to guard God's glorious presence. Isaiah 4:5 (KJV) - "And the LORD will create upon every dwelling place of mount Zion, and upon her assemblies, a cloud and smoke by day, and the shining of a flaming fire by night: for upon all the glory shall be a defence."

question: In the structural flow of Isaiah's early oracles, what dramatic role does Chapter 4 play following the devastating collapse of Chapter 3?
opt1: It transitions from the humiliation and stripping of pride to the glorious Messianic restoration of a holy remnant
opt2: It records the historical accession of King Ahaz and the arrival of the Syrian ambassadors
opt3: It outlines the architectural blueprints for rebuilding the temple walls destroyed by Babylon
opt4: It pronounces seven woes against the surrounding pagan nations of Philistia and Moab
correct: It transitions from the humiliation and stripping of pride to the glorious Messianic restoration of a holy remnant
explanation: Isaiah 4 provides the glorious theological climax to the judgment oracle of Isaiah 2-3, revealing the purified Messianic community that emerges beyond judgment. Isaiah 4:2-3 (KJV) - "In that day shall the branch of the LORD be beautiful and glorious ... And it shall come to pass, that he that is left in Zion, and he that remaineth in Jerusalem, shall be called holy:"

question: What extensive agrarian preparation did the Wellbeloved undertake for His vineyard on a fruitful hill in Isaiah 5:1-2?
opt1: He fenced it, gathered out the stones thereof, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein
opt2: He terraced the mountainside, dug irrigation canals from the Jordan, and hired Egyptian vinedressers
opt3: He burned the thorns with fire, planted wild figs around the borders, and erected an altar of stone
opt4: He manured the soil with salt, hedged it with cedar posts, and imported slips from Lebanon
correct: He fenced it, gathered out the stones thereof, planted it with the choicest vine, built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein
explanation: The parabolic owner provided every conceivable benefit: protective fencing, soil clearing, superior stock (soreq vine), watchtower security, and a winepress for expected harvest. Isaiah 5:1-2 (KJV) - "Now will I sing to my wellbeloved a song of my beloved touching his vineyard. My wellbeloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill: And he fenced it, and gathered out the stones thereof, and planted it with the choicest vine, and built a tower in the midst of it, and also made a winepress therein: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes."

question: What disappointing and bitter harvest did the vineyard yield despite all divine labor in Isaiah 5:2?
opt1: It brought forth sour figs and withered branches
opt2: He looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes
opt3: It yielded thorns, thistles, and dry leaves
opt4: It produced bitter olives and wormwood
correct: He looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes
explanation: Instead of luscious, cultivated fruit, the vineyard yielded 'wild grapes' (be'ushim, foul-smelling, poisonous berries). Isaiah 5:2 (KJV) - "And he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes."

question: What destructive judgment does the Owner decree against His unfruitful vineyard in Isaiah 5:5-6?
opt1: I will sell it to the kings of Assyria, and burn the tower with sulfur from heaven
opt2: I will uproot the vines and cast them into the Kidron valley to be consumed by fire
opt3: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it
opt4: I will plow the fruitful hill into a salt pit, and make it a den for jackals and owls
correct: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it
explanation: God removes all divine protection and nurture, leaving the vineyard vulnerable to grazing, trampling, drought, and overgrowth of thorns. Isaiah 5:5-6 (KJV) - "And now go to; I will tell you what I will do to my vineyard: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down: And I will lay it waste: it shall not be pruned, nor digged; but there shall come up briers and thorns: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it."

question: What famous prophetic wordplay summarizes the tragic moral failure of Israel and Judah in Isaiah 5:7?
opt1: He looked for faith, but behold apostasy; for obedience, but behold rebellion
opt2: He looked for worship, but behold idols; for truth, but behold falsehood
opt3: He looked for mercy, but behold murder; for peace, but behold violence
opt4: He looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry
correct: He looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry
explanation: Isaiah uses poignant Hebrew assonance: God looked for mishpat (justice) but found mispach (bloodshed/oppression); for tzedakah (righteousness) but heard tze'akah (cry of the oppressed). Isaiah 5:7 (KJV) - "For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry."

question: What first woe is pronounced against greedy real-estate monopolists in Isaiah 5:8?
opt1: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!
opt2: Woe unto them that build their palaces with unrighteous timber and oppress the day-labourer!
opt3: Woe unto them that foreclose upon the widows and seize the vineyards of the fatherless!
opt4: Woe unto them that buy the inheritance of the poor for a pair of bronze sandals!
correct: Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!
explanation: The first woe condemns ruthless agrarian greed and land monopoly that disenfranchised peasant landholders in violation of Jubilee laws. Isaiah 5:8 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!"

question: What second woe condemns elite hedonism, perpetual intoxication, and neglect of God's sovereign work in Isaiah 5:11-12?
opt1: Woe unto them that feast upon fatted calves in ivory pavilions while the nation perisheth!
opt2: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them! And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD
opt3: Woe unto them that drink wine from golden bowls and anoint themselves with chief ointments!
opt4: Woe unto them that sing wanton songs to the sound of the viol and invent instruments of music!
correct: Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them! And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD
explanation: Self-indulgent partygoers pursue alcohol from dawn to dusk with music, completely oblivious to God's historical judgment. Isaiah 5:11-12 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink; that continue until night, till wine inflame them! And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine, are in their feasts: but they regard not the work of the LORD, neither consider the operation of his hands."

question: What audacious metaphor depicts shameless sinners dragging their transgression behind them in Isaiah 5:18?
opt1: Woe unto them that carry their idols upon their shoulders like a beast of burden
opt2: Woe unto them that weave spider webs of deceit to ensnare the innocent
opt3: Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope
opt4: Woe unto them that bind heavy yokes of bronze upon the necks of their brethren
correct: Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope
explanation: Apostates are tethered to their wicked lifestyles like draft animals harnessed to a heavy freight cart with thick ropes. Isaiah 5:18 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope:"

question: What memorable woe denounces the complete inversion of objective moral truth and ethical standards in Isaiah 5:20?
opt1: Woe unto them that pervert judgment in the gates and take bribes against the innocent!
opt2: Woe unto them that teach false doctrines and lead my people into outer darkness!
opt3: Woe unto them that exchange the truth of God for a lie and worship the creature!
opt4: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
correct: Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
explanation: Isaiah delivers a classic denunciation of ethical nihilism and moral relativism that interchanges good/evil, light/darkness, and sweet/bitter. Isaiah 5:20 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!"

question: What woe condemns intellectual hubris and self-sufficient arrogance in Isaiah 5:21?
opt1: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
opt2: Woe unto the scribes that boast of their learning and despise the unlearned!
opt3: Woe unto the counsellors that hide their counsel deep from the Holy One of Israel!
opt4: Woe unto the philosophers that trust in Egyptian mysteries and reject the law!
correct: Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!
explanation: Pride in one's own intellect blinds leaders to divine wisdom and brings inevitable judgment. Isaiah 5:21 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!"

question: How does Isaiah describe the rapid, unstoppable advance of the invading foreign army summoned by the Lord's ensign in Isaiah 5:26-28?
opt1: They march like locusts over the hills: their chariots shake the valleys, their bronze spears darken the sun, and their captains shout with thunder
opt2: They shall come with speed swiftly: none shall be weary nor stumble among them; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind
opt3: They cross the Euphrates without boats: their footmen outrun horses, their swords break iron gates, and their banners strike terror into all kings
opt4: They encamp around Zion like the sand of the sea: their battering rams demolish towers, their slingers cast fire, and their archers never miss
correct: They shall come with speed swiftly: none shall be weary nor stumble among them; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken: whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind
explanation: The Assyrian invasion force is portrayed as a disciplined, tireless, lightning-swift instrument of divine wrath. Isaiah 5:26-28 (KJV) - "And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far, and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth: and, behold, they shall come with speed swiftly: None shall be weary nor stumble among them; none shall slumber nor sleep; neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken: Whose arrows are sharp, and all their bows bent, their horses' hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind:"

question: In what pivotal historical year did Isaiah see his foundational throne-room vision of the sovereign Lord in Isaiah 6:1?
opt1: In the year that king Ahaz made an alliance with Assyria
opt2: In the year that king Uzziah died
opt3: In the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah when Sennacherib invaded
opt4: In the year that Pekah king of Israel was assassinated
correct: In the year that king Uzziah died
explanation: Around 740 BC, with the death of Judah's prosperous King Uzziah, Isaiah was given a vision of the true, immortal King reigning on the celestial throne. Isaiah 6:1 (KJV) - "In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple."

question: What celestial beings attended the Lord's throne, and how did they employ their six wings in Isaiah 6:2?
opt1: Cherubims with four wings: with two they covered their bodies, and with two they guarded the mercy seat
opt2: Archangels with golden wings: with two they held trumpets, and with four they ministered before the altar
opt3: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly
opt4: Living creatures with six wings: full of eyes before and behind, bearing the crystal chariot of the Almighty
correct: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly
explanation: The burning seraphim model supreme reverence before unapproachable holiness: covering faces (reverence), feet (humility/creatureliness), and flying (readiness to serve). Isaiah 6:2 (KJV) - "Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly."

question: What threefold praise (the Trisagion) did the seraphim proclaim antiphonally in Isaiah 6:3?
opt1: Great, great, great, is the King of kings: heaven and earth are filled with his power
opt2: Righteous, righteous, righteous, is the God of Jacob: let all the nations bow before him
opt3: Worthy, worthy, worthy, is the Lamb on the throne: dominion and honor belong unto our God
opt4: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory
correct: Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory
explanation: The seraphic Trisagion emphasizes the absolute, superlative holiness of Yahweh Sabaoth, whose glory fills the entire created order. Isaiah 6:3 (KJV) - "And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory."

question: What physical phenomena accompanied the seraphic worship within the temple in Isaiah 6:4?
opt1: The posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke
opt2: The golden veil was rent in twain, and lightning flashed from between the cherubim
opt3: A mighty earthquake shook Mount Moriah, and the bronze altar melted with fervent heat
opt4: The foundation stones split into two, and living water gushed forth from beneath the threshold
correct: The posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke
explanation: The architectural threshold vibrated at the angel's voice and the sanctuary was shrouded in the smoke of divine majesty. Isaiah 6:4 (KJV) - "And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke."

question: What cry of personal devastation and confessed unworthiness did Isaiah utter when beholding the King in Isaiah 6:5?
opt1: Depart from me, O Lord, for I am a sinful man, and unworthy to stand in thy holy presence!
opt2: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts
opt3: Lord, have mercy upon me, for my knees tremble, and my tongue cleaveth to the roof of my mouth!
opt4: Hide me beneath thy wings, O God, lest the fierce brightness of thy glory consume my flesh!
correct: Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts
explanation: Gazing upon absolute holiness brought profound conviction of moral ruin ('I am undone') and verbal sinfulness. Isaiah 6:5 (KJV) - "Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the LORD of hosts."

question: How was Isaiah's guilt purged and his speech consecrated for prophetic service in Isaiah 6:6-7?
opt1: An angel poured holy anointing oil from a golden horn upon his head and consecrated his lips
opt2: The high priest sprinkled the blood of the sin offering upon his tongue before the veil
opt3: A seraph flew with a live coal taken with tongs from off the altar, touched his mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged
opt4: A river of living water washed his mouth, and a scroll of prophecy was given him to eat
correct: A seraph flew with a live coal taken with tongs from off the altar, touched his mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged
explanation: A blazing coal from the sacrificial altar touched Isaiah's lips, supernaturally expiating his guilt and purifying his speech. Isaiah 6:6-7 (KJV) - "Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged."

question: What divine council inquiry did Isaiah hear, and what was his immediate, unreserved response in Isaiah 6:8?
opt1: Who will warn this rebellious generation? Then said I, Lord, let thy servant speak
opt2: Who shall declare my counsel unto Judah? Then said I, Speak, LORD, for thy servant heareth
opt3: Who will stand in the gap for my people? Then said I, O Lord GOD, behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child
opt4: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me
correct: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me
explanation: Purged by grace, Isaiah willingly responds to the Trinitarian plural ('who will go for us?'), offering himself without condition: 'Here am I; send me.' Isaiah 6:8 (KJV) - "Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me."

question: What paradoxical judicial blinding and judicial hardening commission was Isaiah commanded to proclaim in Isaiah 6:9-10?
opt1: Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed
opt2: Repent and turn from your idols, lest the wrath of the LORD consume your cities with unquenchable fire
opt3: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression and their sins
opt4: Go unto the king of Judah and declare that his days are numbered, and his kingdom shall be delivered unto strangers
correct: Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed
explanation: The preaching of the holy word would judicially harden an already rebellious people, dulling their spiritual perception as divine judgment. Isaiah 6:9-10 (KJV) - "And he said, Go, and tell this people, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes; lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert, and be healed."

question: When Isaiah agonized, 'Lord, how long?', what devastating duration of judgment did the Lord disclose in Isaiah 6:11-12?
opt1: For seventy years in the land of the Chaldeans until the decree of the Persian monarch
opt2: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate, and the LORD have removed men far away
opt3: Until three generations have passed away and the temple walls be leveled to the ground
opt4: For forty days of mourning until the pestilence hath consumed the mighty men of war
correct: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate, and the LORD have removed men far away
explanation: The hardening and judgment would persist until complete demographic collapse, severe depopulation, and imperial exile occurred. Isaiah 6:11-12 (KJV) - "Then said I, Lord, how long? And he answered, Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate, And the LORD have removed men far away, and there be a great forsaking in the midst of the land."

question: What botanical metaphor of the felled stump guarantees the survival of the remnant in Isaiah 6:13?
opt1: As an olive tree whose root remaineth green beneath the rocks, so shall the branch of David revive
opt2: As a cedar of Lebanon that sprouteth fresh shoots from the stump, so shall Zion flourish again
opt3: As a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof
opt4: As a vine planted by running streams that endureth the drought, so shall the sons of Jacob endure
correct: As a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof
explanation: Though the nation is repeatedly cut down until only a tenth remains, vital life persists in the stump: the 'holy seed' (Messianic remnant) is its enduring substance. Isaiah 6:13 (KJV) - "But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof."

question: What military coalition marched against Jerusalem in the days of Ahaz king of Judah, terrifying the royal house in Isaiah 7:1-2?
opt1: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and the princes of the Philistines
opt2: Sennacherib king of Assyria, and Tirhakah king of Ethiopia
opt3: Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel
opt4: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and the governors of Ammon and Moab
correct: Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel
explanation: The Syro-Ephraimite alliance between Rezin of Damascus and Pekah of Samaria besieged Jerusalem, causing the hearts of Ahaz and his people to shake like trees in the wind. Isaiah 7:1-2 (KJV) - "And it came to pass in the days of Ahaz the son of Jotham, the son of Uzziah, king of Judah, that Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it. And it was told the house of David, saying, Syria is confederate with Ephraim. And his heart was moved, and the heart of his people, as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind."

question: Whom was Isaiah commanded to take with him when meeting King Ahaz at the conduit of the upper pool in Isaiah 7:3?
opt1: Maher-shalal-hash-baz his son
opt2: Uriah the high priest
opt3: Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah
opt4: Shear-jashub his son

explanation: Isaiah took his son Shear-jashub (whose prophetic name means 'A remnant shall return') to confront King Ahaz with a message of divine assurance. Isaiah 7:3 (KJV) - "Then said the LORD unto Isaiah, Go forth now to meet Ahaz, thou, and Shear-jashub thy son, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field;"

question: What contemptuous metaphor does the LORD use to describe the threatening allied kings Rezin and Pekah in Isaiah 7:4?
opt1: Two tails of these smoking firebrands

explanation: God dismisses the two invading kings as nearly burnt-out, harmless torches producing only lingering smoke. Isaiah 7:4 (KJV) - "And say unto him, Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, for the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria, and of the son of Remaliah."

question: What puppet ruler did Syria and Ephraim plot to enthrone over Judah in Isaiah 7:6?
opt1: Hadad the Edomite

opt4: Gedaliah the son of Ahikam

Isaiah 7:6 (KJV) - "Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and let us make a breach therein for us, and set a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeal:"

question: Within how many years did Isaiah prophesy that the northern kingdom of Ephraim would be broken so that it should not be a people in Isaiah 7:8?
opt1: Within forty years
opt2: Within seventy years
opt3: Within threescore and five years
opt4: Within one hundred and twenty years

explanation: Within 65 years (culminating in Esarhaddon's foreign resettlement of Samaria around 669 BC), Ephraim's national identity would be completely shattered. Isaiah 7:8 (KJV) - "For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin; and within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people."

question: What momentous Messianic sign did the Lord promise to the house of David after Ahaz hypocritically refused to ask for a sign in Isaiah 7:14?
opt1: Behold, the sun shall return ten degrees backward upon the dial of Ahaz
opt2: Behold, a star shall arise out of Jacob and a scepter out of Israel
opt3: Behold, the angel of the LORD shall smite an hundred fourscore and five thousand in a night

correct: Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel

Isaiah 7:14 (KJV) - "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

question: What pastoral dietary fare will the child Immanuel eat before knowing to refuse evil and choose good in Isaiah 7:15?
opt1: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good

opt4: Dates from Jericho and sweet wine from En-gedi
correct: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good
explanation: Curds (butter) and wild honey signify both sustenance in a devastated, uncultivated pastoral land and the simplicity of royal infancy. Isaiah 7:15 (KJV) - "Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good."

question: What invasive insect metaphors depict the foreign armies of Egypt and Assyria summoned by Yahweh's hiss in Isaiah 7:18?
opt1: The locust that devoureth the field of Egypt, and the hornet that stingeth from Assyria

opt3: The moth that consumeth the garments of Egypt, and the scorpion that creepeth from Assyria

correct: The fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and the bee that is in the land of Assyria
explanation: Egyptian swarms of flies and Assyrian stinging bees represent massive military invasions occupying every desolate ravine and thorn bush. Isaiah 7:18 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall hiss for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria."

question: What humiliating metaphor of bodily shaving portrays Assyria's subjugation of Judah in Isaiah 7:20?
opt1: The Lord shall strip them of their armor and expose their nakedness before the heathen
opt2: The Lord shall brand them with hot irons upon the forehead like captive slaves
opt3: The Lord shall shave with a razor that is hired, namely, by them beyond the river, by the king of Assyria, the head, and the hair of the feet: and it shall also consume the beard
opt4: The Lord shall wash away their ointments with lye and leave their skin withered
correct: The Lord shall shave with a razor that is hired, namely, by them beyond the river, by the king of Assyria, the head, and the hair of the feet: and it shall also consume the beard
explanation: The Assyrian empire, hired by Ahaz's silver, becomes God's razor to inflict total national humiliation, stripping hair from head to foot and beard. Isaiah 7:20 (KJV) - "In the same day shall the Lord shave with a razor that is hired, namely, by them beyond the river, by the king of Assyria, the head, and the hair of the feet: and it shall also consume the beard."

question: What agrarian reversion will transform prized vineyards worth a thousand silver coins into desolate wilderness in Isaiah 7:23-24?
opt1: The terrace walls shall crumble into heaps of chalk, and wild boars shall root out the vines
opt2: The locusts shall eat the tender shoots, and the drought shall turn the hills into salt

correct: Every place shall even be for briers and thorns; with arrows and with bows shall men come thither; because all the land shall become briers and thorns
explanation: Cultivated, valuable vineyards will revert to overgrown thorn thickets where men must carry weapons to hunt game amidst briers. Isaiah 7:23-24 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that every place shall be, where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings, it shall even be for briers and thorns. With arrows and with bows shall men come thither; because all the land shall become briers and thorns."

question: What prophetic name was Isaiah instructed to write upon a great roll with a man's pen concerning the imminent plundering of Damascus and Samaria in Isaiah 8:1-3?
opt1: Shear-jashub
opt2: Immanuel
opt3: Pele-joez-el-gibbor
opt4: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
correct: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
explanation: The symbolic name Maher-shalal-hash-baz means 'Swift to the spoil, quick to the prey,' signifying that Assyria would rapidly plunder Damascus and Samaria. Isaiah 8:1-3 (KJV) - "Moreover the LORD said unto me, Take thee a great roll, and write in it with a man's pen concerning Maher-shalal-hash-baz ... Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Maher-shalal-hash-baz."

question: What two faithful witnesses were summoned to legally record the prophecy in Isaiah 8:2?
opt1: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah

opt3: Shebna the treasurer, and Eliakim the son of Hilkiah
opt4: Baruch the son of Neriah, and Seraiah the chief chamberlain
correct: Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah
explanation: Uriah the high priest and Zechariah served as credible public witnesses to certify the prophetic inscription before its historical fulfillment. Isaiah 8:2 (KJV) - "And I took unto me faithful witnesses to record, Uriah the priest, and Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah."

question: What gentle local water source did the people of Judah despise in favor of foreign imperial power in Isaiah 8:6?

question: What overwhelming river flood will sweep over Judah, reaching even to the neck and filling the land of Immanuel in Isaiah 8:7-8?
opt1: The torrents of the Nile overflowing the delta and drowning the vineyards of the south
opt2: The swelling of the Jordan at harvest time washing away the fenced cities of Benjamin
opt3: The waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel
opt4: The sea rising in tempest and crashing against the high towers of Zion
correct: The waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel
explanation: The Euphrates in flood represents the Assyrian military machine that inundates Judah up to the neck (besieging Jerusalem itself), yet God's land belongs to Immanuel. Isaiah 8:7-8 (KJV) - "Now therefore, behold, the Lord bringeth up upon them the waters of the river, strong and many, even the king of Assyria, and all his glory: and he shall come up over all his channels, and go over all his banks: And he shall pass through Judah; he shall overflow and go over, he shall reach even to the neck; and the stretching out of his wings shall fill the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."

question: Why will all pagan coalitions, international conspiracies, and confederacies ultimately come to nought according to Isaiah 8:9-10?
opt1: Because their gods are carved of stone and their diviners are blind
opt2: Because the angel of the covenant shall scatter them with the north wind

correct: Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us
explanation: No anti-God conspiracy can prevail against the sovereign decree of Yahweh, because 'God is with us' (the Hebrew meaning of Immanuel). Isaiah 8:10 (KJV) - "Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us."

question: Whom alone must God's people sanctify, fear, and dread, rather than joining popular panic over political conspiracies in Isaiah 8:12-13?
opt1: Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread

Isaiah 8:12-13 (KJV) - "Say ye not, A confederacy, to all them to whom this people shall say, A confederacy; neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread."

question: What paradoxical double role does the LORD become to both houses of Israel in Isaiah 8:14?
opt1: He shall be for a shield to the righteous, but for a devouring tempest to the hypocrite
opt2: He shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem

explanation: To the faithful, God is an inviolable sanctuary; but to unbelieving Israel and Judah, He becomes an offensive stumbling stone and trapping snare. Isaiah 8:14 (KJV) - "And he shall be for a sanctuary; but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel, for a gin and for a snare to the inhabitants of Jerusalem."

question: What commission does Isaiah receive regarding the preservation of divine revelation among the faithful remnant in Isaiah 8:16?
opt1: Engrave the covenant upon bronze pillars in the temple gate

explanation: During periods of national apostasy, the prophet must preserve, guard, and seal the written testimony within the circle of genuine disciples. Isaiah 8:16 (KJV) - "Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples."

question: What sign value do Isaiah and his children possess within Israel according to Isaiah 8:18?
opt1: We are appointed as royal priests to minister before the ark of the covenant

explanation: Isaiah ('Yahweh is salvation') and his prophetically named sons (Shear-jashub and Maher-shalal-hash-baz) embodied living sermons and signs to Israel. Isaiah 8:18 (KJV) - "Behold, I and the children whom the LORD hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the LORD of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion."

question: What definitive standard of truth exposes the darkness of necromancers and familiar spirits that peep and mutter in Isaiah 8:19-20?
opt1: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them

opt4: To the council of the priests: if the Urim and Thummim answer not, they shall be put to death

explanation: All spiritual practices and teachings must be tested against God's written revelation ('the law and the testimony'); any deviation reveals spiritual blindness. question: What northern frontier regions of Israel, once lightly afflicted and living in darkness, are promised glorious illumination in Isaiah 9:1-2?

explanation: Zebulun and Naphtali (Galilee of the Gentiles), the first territories ravaged by Assyrian deportation, are promised the initial dawn of Messianic light. Isaiah 9:1-2 (KJV) - "The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined."

question: To what historic victory is the destruction of the oppressor's yoke, staff, and rod compared in Isaiah 9:4?

question: What fivefold royal and divine throne names are bestowed upon the promised royal Child in Isaiah 9:6?
opt1: The King of glory, The Lord of hosts, The Holy One of Israel, The Shepherd of Jacob, The Rock of Ages

opt4: The Scepter of power, The Morning Star, The Horn of salvation, The Shield of truth, The Captain of the host

explanation: The Child born unto us is endowed with absolute deity and cosmic dominion: Wonderful Counsellor, El Gibbor (Mighty God), Eternal Father (Father of Eternity), and Prince of Peace. Isaiah 9:6 (KJV) - "For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace."

question: What guarantees the eternal establishment, perpetual justice, and boundless expansion of David's throne under Messiah in Isaiah 9:7?

opt4: The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this

Isaiah 9:7 (KJV) - "Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the LORD of hosts will perform this."

question: What defiant boast of architectural self-reliance did Ephraim utter in pride and stoutness of heart in Isaiah 9:9-10?
opt1: The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars

opt4: Our king is fallen, but we will crown a mightier prince: our swords are blunted, but we will forge iron spears

explanation: Instead of repenting under divine chastisement, Ephraim arrogantly vowed to rebuild with superior stone and replace cheap sycamore with luxury cedar. Isaiah 9:9-10 (KJV) - "And all the people shall know, even Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria, that say in the pride and stoutness of heart, The bricks are fallen down, but we will build with hewn stones: the sycomores are cut down, but we will change them into cedars."

question: What hostile nations are stirred up on the east and west to devour Israel with open mouth in Isaiah 9:11-12?

question: What tragic refrain echoes four times throughout Isaiah 9 and 10 to demonstrate ongoing, unappeased divine wrath?
opt1: And they repented not of the works of their hands to give him glory

opt3: For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still
opt4: Therefore shall the sword of the enemy devour their young men without mercy
correct: For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still
explanation: This chilling prophetic refrain signals that previous judgments have not exhausted divine justice because national unrepentance persists. Isaiah 9:12 (KJV) - "For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still."

question: What civic and religious categories are described as the 'head and tail, branch and rush' cut off in one day in Isaiah 9:14-15?
opt1: The reigning monarch is the head, and the idolatrous priest is the tail
opt2: The wealthy merchant is the head, and the oppressed beggar is the tail
opt3: The captain of the host is the head, and the foreign mercenary is the tail
opt4: The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail
correct: The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail
explanation: Social elders and noble leaders represent the head, while corrupt false prophets who flatter and deceive the populace constitute the degrading tail. Isaiah 9:14-15 (KJV) - "Therefore the LORD will cut off from Israel head and tail, branch and rush, in one day. The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail."

question: To what raging wildfire is wickedness compared as it consumes the social fabric in Isaiah 9:18?
opt1: For wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forest, and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke
opt2: Like a burning oven heating the baker's dough until all is consumed
opt3: Like molten brimstone flowing down the slopes of a fiery mountain
opt4: Like a spark falling into a threshing floor covered with dry chaff
correct: For wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forest, and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke
explanation: Internal sin acts like an uncontrollable forest fire, consuming society from small briers to massive trees in clouds of smoke. Isaiah 9:18 (KJV) - "For wickedness burneth as the fire: it shall devour the briers and thorns, and shall kindle in the thickets of the forest, and they shall mount up like the lifting up of smoke."

question: What fratricidal tribal civil warfare breaks out among the sons of Joseph in their insatiable moral frenzy in Isaiah 9:20-21?
opt1: Dan against Benjamin, and Benjamin against Simeon

opt4: Zebulun against Issachar, and Asher against the children of Levi
correct: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah

Isaiah 9:20-21 (KJV) - "They shall eat every man the flesh of his own arm: Manasseh, Ephraim; and Ephraim, Manasseh: and they together shall be against Judah. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still."

question: What judicial oppression and legislative tyranny is condemned in the opening woe of Isaiah 10:1-2?
opt1: Woe unto them that build their cities with blood, and establish their ramparts with iniquity!
opt2: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; to turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!
opt3: Woe unto them that demand exorbitant usury from their brethren and seize their ancestral fields!
opt4: Woe unto them that justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous!
correct: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; to turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!
explanation: Corrupt magistrates use legal mechanisms and official decrees to rob widows, orphans, and the poor of their legal rights. Isaiah 10:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless!"

question: What imperial title does God assign to Assyria, establishing its role as an unconscious instrument of divine chastisement in Isaiah 10:5?
opt1: The mighty hammer of the whole earth to shatter the nations
opt2: The razor of wrath to shave the proud kings of the south
opt3: O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation
opt4: The winged lion of the north to tear the heritage of Jacob
