explanation: God strips Shebna of his pomp, bundling him up and tossing him like a ball into the vast, open plains of Assyria to die in obscurity. Isaiah 22:18 (KJV) - "He will surely violently turn and toss thee like a ball into a large country: there shalt thou die, and there the chariots of thy glory shall be the shame of thy lord's house."

question: What Messianic symbol of supreme administrative authority is placed upon the shoulder of Eliakim the son of Hilkiah in Isaiah 22:22?
opt1: The golden scepter of Solomon, that all princes may bow before his judgment seat
opt2: The breastplate of Urim and Thummim, that he may declare the secret counsel of God
opt3: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open
opt4: The royal signet ring of David, that his decrees may never be reversed in the land
correct: And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open
explanation: Quoted in Revelation 3:7 concerning Christ, the 'key of the house of David' signifies absolute, uncontested royal authority over the kingdom: opening and shutting with sovereign finality. Isaiah 22:22 (KJV) - "And the key of the house of David will I lay upon his shoulder; so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open."

question: What maritime merchant fleet is summoned to wail over the complete devastation of their home seaport in Isaiah 23:1?
opt1: Howl, ye navies of Alexandria; for the harbour of the Nile is choked with stones
opt2: Howl, ye galleys of Sidon; for your cedar oars are broken upon the rocks
opt3: The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them
opt4: Howl, ye merchant barges of Ezion-geber; for the southern trade is cut off
correct: The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them
explanation: The long-distance ocean trading fleet returning from Tarshish (Spain) receives the devastating report at Cyprus (Chittim) that the premier Phoenician island-port of Tyre is destroyed. Isaiah 23:1 (KJV) - "The burden of Tyre. Howl, ye ships of Tarshish; for it is laid waste, so that there is no house, no entering in: from the land of Chittim it is revealed to them."

question: What international agricultural grain revenue sustained the commercial empire of Tyre in Isaiah 23:3?
opt1: The vintage of Sibmah and the olive oil of the hills of Galilee
opt2: The barley of the Euphrates and the woven textiles of Babylon
opt3: The frankincense of Sheba and the fine wool of the flocks of Kedar
opt4: And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations
correct: And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations
explanation: Tyre served as the maritime distributor and global broker ('mart of nations') for Egyptian wheat and Nile harvest ('seed of Sihor'). Isaiah 23:3 (KJV) - "And by great waters the seed of Sihor, the harvest of the river, is her revenue; and she is a mart of nations."

question: What aristocratic commercial titles describe the elite merchant princes and global traders of Tyre in Isaiah 23:8?
opt1: Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth
opt2: Whose captains are monarchs, and whose sailors wear robes of fine linen
opt3: Whose governors control the seas, and whose treasurers dictate treaties to all kings
opt4: Whose shipbuilders are renowned in all lands, and whose bankers possess mountains of gold
correct: Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth
explanation: Tyre was the 'crowning city' - an imperial king-maker whose commercial traders wielded wealth, prestige, and influence equal to sovereign princes. Isaiah 23:8 (KJV) - "Who hath taken this counsel against Tyre, the crowning city, whose merchants are princes, whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth?"

question: Why did the LORD of hosts purpose the overthrow of magnificent, wealthy Tyre in Isaiah 23:9?
opt1: To avenge the enslavement of the children of Judah sold unto the Grecians
opt2: The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth
opt3: To break the maritime monopoly over the copper mines of the western islands
opt4: To establish a new port for the kings of Assyria along the Syrian coastline
correct: The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth
explanation: God sovereignly ordained Tyre's humiliation to dismantle human commercial arrogance, staining all pride of glory and humbling the world's commercial elite. Isaiah 23:9 (KJV) - "The LORD of hosts hath purposed it, to stain the pride of all glory, and to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth."

question: What ancient Mesopotamian people, once insignificant, are cited as the instrument that besieged and ruined Tyre's palaces in Isaiah 23:13?
opt1: The mighty horsemen of the Medes who descended from the mountains of the north
opt2: The archers of Elam who crossed the desert with quivers of iron
opt3: Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, till the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin
opt4: The seafaring Philistines who raided the coastal islands with fleets of war
correct: Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, till the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin
explanation: Isaiah points to the Chaldeans/Assyrians: if they could conquer ancient Babylon, they will effortlessly shatter the offshore fortresses of Tyre. Isaiah 23:13 (KJV) - "Behold the land of the Chaldeans; this people was not, till the Assyrian founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness: they set up the towers thereof, they raised up the palaces thereof; and he brought it to ruin."

question: For how long will commercial Tyre be forgotten, according to the days of one king, in Isaiah 23:15?
opt1: Forty years
opt2: Three years
opt3: One hundred and twenty years
opt4: Seventy years
correct: Seventy years
explanation: Tyre will endure a 70-year eclipse of international commerce, paralleling the Babylonian hegemony and Judah's exile. Isaiah 23:15 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years, according to the days of one king: after the end of seventy years shall Tyre sing as an harlot."

question: What metaphor of an aging, forgotten street harlot depicts Tyre's frantic efforts to regain global commerce in Isaiah 23:16?
opt1: Take an harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayest be remembered
opt2: Put on thy purple apparel and stand in the gates of the harbor with golden anklets
opt3: Pour costly ointment upon thy hair and burn sweet incense before foreign sailors
opt4: Adorn thy merchant vessels with scarlet banners and blow the silver trumpets
correct: Take an harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayest be remembered
explanation: Tyre is satirized as an aged, forgotten courtesan wandering the streets with a musical harp, singing songs to lure back former commercial clients. Isaiah 23:16 (KJV) - "Take an harp, go about the city, thou harlot that hast been forgotten; make sweet melody, sing many songs, that thou mayest be remembered."

question: What ultimate, holy consecration of Tyre's commercial wealth is prophesied at the end of her seventy-year restoration in Isaiah 23:18?
opt1: Her gold shall be melted to cast the two cherubim in the holy of holies
opt2: Her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the LORD: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing
opt3: Her merchant ships shall be dedicated to transport the exiles across the Great Sea
opt4: Her palace treasures shall be burned with holy fire as a whole burnt offering
correct: Her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the LORD: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing
explanation: Instead of hoarding wealth in selfish greed, Tyre's commercial profits will be consecrated ('holiness to the LORD') to sustain God's worshippers with abundant food and fine garments. Isaiah 23:18 (KJV) - "And her merchandise and her hire shall be holiness to the LORD: it shall not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise shall be for them that dwell before the LORD, to eat sufficiently, and for durable clothing."

question: What panic seizes the Egyptian marketplace when news of the destruction of maritime Tyre arrives in Isaiah 23:5?
opt1: The merchants of Memphis shall close their gates and refuse foreign silver
opt2: The price of wheat shall fall by half and the ships shall rot in the harbor
opt3: As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre
opt4: The kings of Egypt shall assemble their chariots to defend the delta
correct: As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre
explanation: Egypt trembles with deep economic and geopolitical dread, knowing that Tyre's fall leaves her own coastlands completely vulnerable. Isaiah 23:5 (KJV) - "As at the report concerning Egypt, so shall they be sorely pained at the report of Tyre."

question: To what distant Phoenician mining colony are the dispossessed citizens of Tyre advised to flee in exile in Isaiah 23:6?
opt1: Flee unto the mountains of Lebanon; hide in the caves of the cedars
opt2: Cross the sea unto the islands of Greece; seek shelter in Corinth
opt3: Escape unto the ports of Carthage; build new fortresses in Africa
opt4: Pass ye over to Tarshish; howl, ye inhabitants of the isle
correct: Pass ye over to Tarshish; howl, ye inhabitants of the isle
explanation: With their island citadel ruined, refugees are told to sail to their westernmost colony, Tarshish in southern Spain. Isaiah 23:6 (KJV) - "Pass ye over to Tarshish; howl, ye inhabitants of the isle."

question: What cosmic de-creation and universal desolation opens the 'Isaiah Apocalypse' (Chapters 24-27) in Isaiah 24:1?
opt1: The heavens shall melt with fervent heat, and the stars shall fall into the deep
opt2: The four winds shall strive upon the great sea, and four beasts shall arise
opt3: The angel of wrath shall sound the seventh trumpet, and the abyss shall open
opt4: Behold, the LORD maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof
correct: Behold, the LORD maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof
explanation: Isaiah 24 expands beyond regional oracles into cosmic eschatology: Yahweh empties, devastates, upends, and depopulates the entire globe. Isaiah 24:1 (KJV) - "Behold, the LORD maketh the earth empty, and maketh it waste, and turneth it upside down, and scattereth abroad the inhabitants thereof."

question: What radical egalitarian leveler dissolves all social, religious, and economic distinctions under divine judgment in Isaiah 24:2?
opt1: As with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him
opt2: The king and the beggar shall share the same grave, and the wise man shall perish like the fool
opt3: The warrior shall drop his spear beside the infant, and the rich shall starve with the pauper
opt4: Neither gold nor silver shall deliver any man, and all crowns shall be trampled in the mud
correct: As with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him
explanation: Judgment strikes indiscriminately across six social pairs: religious, domestic, commercial, and financial hierarchies are leveled before God. Isaiah 24:2 (KJV) - "And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest; as with the servant, so with his master; as with the maid, so with her mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller; as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the taker of usury, so with the giver of usury to him."

question: What threefold moral rebellion polluted the earth and broke God's cosmic covenant in Isaiah 24:5?
opt1: Because they worshipped the host of heaven, shed innocent blood, and oppressed the stranger
opt2: Because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant
opt3: Because they perverted judgment in the gates, followed strong drink, and mocked the prophets
opt4: Because they built towers of pride, multiplied horses from Egypt, and worshipped idols
correct: Because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant
explanation: The earth itself is defiled by its dwellers because of universal moral treason: violating divine laws, altering ordinances, and fracturing the perpetual covenant (the Noahic/creation covenant). Isaiah 24:5 (KJV) - "The earth also is defiled under the inhabitants thereof; because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant."

question: What demographic depletion and global burning is caused by the divine curse consuming the earth in Isaiah 24:6?
opt1: The pestilence hath consumed nine parts of mankind, and only a tenth remaineth in the caves
opt2: The rivers of brimstone have overflowed the valleys, and the cities are turned into white ash
opt3: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are desolate: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left
opt4: The famine hath devoured all flesh, and the wild beasts outnumber the sons of men
correct: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are desolate: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left
explanation: Covenantal curse scorches the earth's population, leaving behind only a tiny fraction of humanity ('few men left'). Isaiah 24:6 (KJV) - "Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth, and they that dwell therein are desolate: therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned, and few men left."

question: What cultural silence and cessation of festivity overtakes urban society in Isaiah 24:8-9?
opt1: The bells upon the horses are silenced, and the singing in the marketplaces hath ceased
opt2: The bridal procession walketh in tears, and the flute player layeth down his instrument
opt3: The trumpets of the sanctuary are broken, and the dancing of the maidens is forgotten
opt4: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, the noise of them that rejoice endeth, the joy of the harp ceaseth. They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it
correct: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, the noise of them that rejoice endeth, the joy of the harp ceaseth. They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it
explanation: All worldly entertainment, musical joy, and banqueting are extinguished; alcohol itself turns unpalatably bitter to depressed drinkers. Isaiah 24:8-9 (KJV) - "The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, the noise of them that rejoice endeth, the joy of the harp ceaseth. They shall not drink wine with a song; strong drink shall be bitter to them that drink it."

question: What universal architectural chaos title is given to the ruined metropolis of human pride in Isaiah 24:10?
opt1: The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in
opt2: The city of blood is overthrown: her towers are level with the dust
opt3: The city of pride is plundered: her gates are burned with unquenchable fire
opt4: The city of oppression is leveled: her foundations are swallowed by the earth
correct: The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in
explanation: The archetypal world city is branded 'the city of confusion' (qiryat tohu, evoking Genesis 1:2 chaos and Babel's confusion), barricaded in fearful ruins. Isaiah 24:10 (KJV) - "The city of confusion is broken down: every house is shut up, that no man may come in."

question: What unexpected song of eschatological praise erupts from the righteous scattered in the distant maritime west and islands in Isaiah 24:14-16?
opt1: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts, heaven and earth are full of thy glory
opt2: They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing for the majesty of the LORD, they shall cry aloud from the sea. Wherefore glorify ye the LORD in the fires, even the name of the LORD God of Israel in the isles of the sea. From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, even Glory to the righteous
opt3: Great and marvellous are thy works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are thy ways
opt4: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ
correct: They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing for the majesty of the LORD, they shall cry aloud from the sea. Wherefore glorify ye the LORD in the fires, even the name of the LORD God of Israel in the isles of the sea. From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, even Glory to the righteous
explanation: Amidst global ruin, a redeemed remnant surviving on islands and across the seas lifts triumphant voices, singing 'Glory to the righteous!' in praise of Yahweh. Isaiah 24:14-16 (KJV) - "They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing for the majesty of the LORD, they shall cry aloud from the sea. Wherefore glorify ye the LORD in the fires, even the name of the LORD God of Israel in the isles of the sea. From the uttermost part of the earth have we heard songs, even Glory to the righteous."

question: What inescapable three-part alliterative trap confronts the ungodly inhabitants of the earth in Isaiah 24:17-18?
opt1: The sword, and the famine, and the pestilence, shall pursue thee into the wilderness
opt2: The tempest, and the earthquake, and the flame of fire, shall devour thy fortresses
opt3: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth. And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare
opt4: The darkness, and the serpent, and the scorpion, shall torment the sons of men
correct: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth. And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare
explanation: Isaiah uses gripping Hebrew alliteration (pachad, pachath, pach): escaping psychological panic only lands a person in a pit; escaping the pit springs a deadly snare. Isaiah 24:17-18 (KJV) - "Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of the earth. And it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the noise of the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that cometh up out of the midst of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for the windows from on high are open, and the foundations of the earth do shake."

question: To what intoxicated individual and fragile shelter is the convulsing, reeling earth compared under its heavy guilt in Isaiah 24:19-20?
opt1: The earth shall tremble like a ship tossed in a typhoon, and shall sink like lead in the mighty waters
opt2: The earth shall wander like a blind man in darkness, and shall melt like wax before the furnace
opt3: The earth shall shatter like a potter's vessel, and its dust shall be carried away by the whirlwind
opt4: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again
correct: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again
explanation: Under the crushing weight of its accumulated sin, the planet staggers like a reeling drunkard and sways like a flimsy temporary shack ('cottage') in a hurricane, collapsing permanently. Isaiah 24:19-20 (KJV) - "The earth is utterly broken down, the earth is clean dissolved, the earth is moved exceedingly. The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, and shall be removed like a cottage; and the transgression thereof shall be heavy upon it; and it shall fall, and not rise again."

question: What cosmic coronation and planetary incarceration takes place when the LORD of hosts reigns gloriously in Mount Zion in Isaiah 24:21-23?
opt1: The LORD shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth. And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison ... Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the LORD of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously
opt2: The archangel shall bind the dragon with a great chain for a thousand years in the bottomless pit
opt3: The stars shall fall from their orbits, and twelve thrones of judgment shall be set up over all flesh
opt4: The righteous shall be caught up into the clouds, and the wicked shall be cast into outer darkness
correct: The LORD shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth. And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison ... Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the LORD of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously
explanation: Demonic powers ('host of the high ones on high') and earthly tyrants are imprisoned together; both sun and moon hide their faces in shame before the dazzling splendor of Yahweh Sabaoth reigning on Mount Zion. Isaiah 24:21-23 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high, and the kings of the earth upon the earth. And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison, and after many days shall they be visited. Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the LORD of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously."

question: What personal doxology exalting God's ancient, faithful counsels opens the hymn of redemption in Isaiah 25:1?
opt1: O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth
opt2: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness
opt3: I will give thanks unto the LORD with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works
opt4: The LORD reigneth, he is clothed with majesty; the LORD is clothed with strength, wherewith he hath girded himself
correct: O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth
explanation: The prophet bursts into personal adoration, praising Yahweh for executing eternal, unchanging purposes rooted in absolute faithfulness and truth. Isaiah 25:1 (KJV) - "O LORD, thou art my God; I will exalt thee, I will praise thy name; for thou hast done wonderful things; thy counsels of old are faithfulness and truth."

question: What fivefold shelter does the LORD provide for the vulnerable and impoverished against the blast of tyrants in Isaiah 25:4?
opt1: A shield of bronze, a sword of victory, a high tower of granite, a deep cistern of water, and an horn of salvation
opt2: Thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall
opt3: A wall of fire around Zion, a fortress on the hill, an army of cherubim, an unquenchable lamp, and an eternal heritage
opt4: A rock of refuge, a strong habitation, a deliverer from the snare, a guide through the desert, and a pavilion of peace
correct: Thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall
explanation: Yahweh serves as an impenetrable defense for the helpless against the violent onslaught of tyrants, likened to a winter storm lashing a stone wall. Isaiah 25:4 (KJV) - "For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall."

question: What lavish eschatological banquet does the LORD of hosts prepare for all nations on Mount Zion in Isaiah 25:6?
opt1: A feast of unleavened bread, of milk from the flock, of wild honey from the rocks, and pomegranates from En-gedi
opt2: A royal banquet of wheat from the Nile, of oil from the olive groves of Samaria, and vintage from the vineyards of Sibmah
opt3: In this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined
opt4: A sacrificial meal of choice bullocks, of rams of Nebaioth, of fine flour sprinkled with frankincense, and sweet spices
correct: In this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined
explanation: God inaugurates the Messianic banquet for all global peoples, serving rich, exquisite foods ('fat things full of marrow') and aged, aged vintage wine thoroughly settled and clarified. Isaiah 25:6 (KJV) - "And in this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things, a feast of wines on the lees, of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined."

question: What universal shroud of spiritual blindness and sorrow will God permanently destroy on Mount Zion in Isaiah 25:7?
opt1: The heavy iron yoke imposed by the emperors of Assyria and the kings of Babylon
opt2: The curse of the broken law engraved upon tablets of stone in the wilderness
opt3: The darkness of the shadow of death that covered the valley of the shadow of mourning
opt4: He will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations
correct: He will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations
explanation: God removes the funeral pall and spiritual veil of grief, ignorance, and spiritual death that has shrouded all human nations since the Fall. Isaiah 25:7 (KJV) - "And he will destroy in this mountain the face of the covering cast over all people, and the vail that is spread over all nations."

question: What supreme redemptive victory and tender comfort is prophesied in the famous promise of Isaiah 25:8?
opt1: He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth
opt2: He will break the scepter of the grave; and the angels shall gather the elect from the four winds; and sorrow shall flee away
opt3: He will resurrect the dead of Jacob; and the streets of Jerusalem shall be paved with gold; and sickness shall be no more
opt4: He will cast the oppressor into the abyss; and the righteous shall shine as the stars; and mourning shall be turned to joy
correct: He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth
explanation: Quoted in 1 Corinthians 15:54 and Revelation 21:4, God obliterates physical death forever, wiping away every tear with divine tenderness. Isaiah 25:8 (KJV) - "He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it."

question: What triumphant confession of patient, vindicated faith will the redeemed utter in that day in Isaiah 25:9?
opt1: The LORD is our King, he hath conquered our adversaries; let us shout for joy before the ark of his strength
opt2: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the LORD; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation
opt3: Behold our Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; he hath remembered his covenant with David our father
opt4: Worthy is the Lord of hosts who hath delivered Zion; we will offer sacrifices of thanksgiving in his courts
correct: Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the LORD; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation
explanation: Patient endurance is rewarded as believers point to their God with joy: 'Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us!' Isaiah 25:9 (KJV) - "And it shall be said in that day, Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us: this is the LORD; we have waited for him, we will be glad and rejoice in his salvation."

question: To what degrading agricultural refuse is proud Moab compared as she is trampled down under God's hand in Isaiah 25:10?
opt1: As dry chaff swept into the burning furnace of the potter
opt2: As rotten wood consumed by worms in the dark forest
opt3: Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill
opt4: As worthless dross discarded from the silver refining pot
correct: Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill
explanation: Moab (representing persistent, arrogant enemies of God) is utterly debased, trodden down like straw trampled into a manure pit. Isaiah 25:10 (KJV) - "For in this mountain shall the hand of the LORD rest, and Moab shall be trodden down under him, even as straw is trodden down for the dunghill."

question: What swimming metaphor portrays Moab's frantic, futile struggles against divine humiliation in Isaiah 25:11?
opt1: As a drowning man clinging to broken reeds in the swollen waters of the Jordan
opt2: As a bird flapping its wounded wings in the snare of the fowler
opt3: As a wild bull tangled in the net of the hunters upon the mountains
opt4: And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands
correct: And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands
explanation: Moab frantically paddles her arms like a desperate swimmer trying to stay afloat in sewage, but God brings down her pride and ill-gotten gains. Isaiah 25:11 (KJV) - "And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst of them, as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim: and he shall bring down their pride together with the spoils of their hands."

question: What total demolition overtakes the high fortifications and defensive ramparts of the enemy in Isaiah 25:12?
opt1: The fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust
opt2: He shall burn them with sulfur and cast their foundation stones into the sea
opt3: He shall cause them to crumble like sand before the fury of the desert whirlwind
opt4: He shall shatter them with the iron rod of his wrath into ten thousand fragments
correct: The fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust
explanation: Four emphatic verbs detail the irreversible leveling of human military fortifications down to the dust. Isaiah 25:12 (KJV) - "And the fortress of the high fort of thy walls shall he bring down, lay low, and bring to the ground, even to the dust."

question: To what weather condition is the oppression of ruthless tyrants compared, and how does God neutralize it in Isaiah 25:4-5?
opt1: A burning fire in dry thorns; extinguished by torrential rains from heaven
opt2: The heat in a dry place; neutralized as the heat with the shadow of a cloud
opt3: A suffocating sirocco wind; subdued by the cool waters of Mount Hermon
opt4: A scorching drought; broken by the early and latter rains upon the earth
correct: The heat in a dry place; neutralized as the heat with the shadow of a cloud
explanation: God effortlessly quells the fierce heat of foreign oppression just as a passing cloud shadow tempers the blistering desert sun. Isaiah 25:5 (KJV) - "Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers, as the heat in a dry place; even the heat with the shadow of a cloud: the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low."

question: What divine defense replaces traditional stone ramparts in the song of the strong city in Judah in Isaiah 26:1?
opt1: Twelve towers of cut granite and gates of hammered bronze
opt2: We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks
opt3: The horses of David and the chariots of the host of Israel
opt4: An impenetrable trench of water flowing from the springs of Zion
correct: We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks
explanation: The security of the redeemed community rests not in masonry or military fortifications, but in God's salvation serving as walls and bulwarks. Isaiah 26:1 (KJV) - "In that day shall this song be sung in the land of Judah; We have a strong city; salvation will God appoint for walls and bulwarks."

question: What famous promise guarantees unshakeable emotional and spiritual serenity to the steadfast believer in Isaiah 26:3?
opt1: The peace of God which passeth all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds through faith
opt2: Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them or cast them down
opt3: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee
opt4: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you
correct: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee
explanation: In Hebrew, 'shalom shalom' ('perfect peace') is divinely guaranteed to the person whose thoughts and affections are firmly anchored ('stayed') on God. Isaiah 26:3 (KJV) - "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee."

question: What divine title reveals the eternal, rock-solid reliability of the LORD in Isaiah 26:4?
opt1: For in the Almighty God is the fountain of eternal life
opt2: For in the Holy One of Israel is unchangeable covenant mercy
opt3: For in the Lord of hosts is supreme dominion and triumph
opt4: Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength
correct: Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength
explanation: The text calls for perpetual trust because in Yah Yahweh ('the LORD JEHOVAH') is Tsur Olamim - the Rock of Ages or 'everlasting strength.' Isaiah 26:4 (KJV) - "Trust ye in the LORD for ever: for in the LORD JEHOVAH is everlasting strength:"

question: Whose feet are appointed to tread down the leveled lofty city of human pride in Isaiah 26:6?
opt1: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy
opt2: The iron chariots of the captains of Judah and the cavalry of the king
opt3: The mighty angels of heaven bearing swords of flame
opt4: The princes of the Medes and Persians marching in triumph
correct: The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy
explanation: In a glorious reversal of worldly power, the once-oppressed poor and needy literally march over the leveled ruins of the proud oppressor city. Isaiah 26:6 (KJV) - "The foot shall tread it down, even the feet of the poor, and the steps of the needy."

question: What spiritual principle explains how the world's inhabitants learn righteousness in Isaiah 26:9?
opt1: When the law is proclaimed from Mount Zion, all nations will turn from their idols
opt2: When thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness
opt3: When the temple is rebuilt with gold, the kings of the Gentiles will bow in the dust
opt4: When the harvest overfloweth with wine and oil, all flesh will give thanks unto God
correct: When thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness
explanation: Moral instruction is imparted through divine discipline: when God's righteous judgments operate historically in the earth, humanity learns true righteousness. Isaiah 26:9 (KJV) - "With my soul have I desired thee in the night; yea, with my spirit within me will I seek thee early: for when thy judgments are in the earth, the inhabitants of the world will learn righteousness."

question: Why does granting unmerited favor to the wicked fail to bring about genuine repentance in Isaiah 26:10?
opt1: Because his heart is an iron sinew and his conscience is seared with foreign sorceries
opt2: Because his eyes are blinded by the god of this world and he cannot perceive the light
opt3: Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD
opt4: Because he hath made an agreement with hell and sealed a covenant with the grave
correct: Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD
explanation: Grace alone, unaccompanied by moral awakening, is abused by the wicked; even living in a land of uprightness, the unregenerate persist in injustice. Isaiah 26:10 (KJV) - "Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness: in the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly, and will not behold the majesty of the LORD."

question: To what agonizing obstetric metaphor is Israel's human attempt at producing national salvation compared in Isaiah 26:17-18?
opt1: Like a barren woman weeping at the threshold because she hath no child to inherit her house
opt2: Like an heifer writhing under the yoke, bringing forth stillborn calves in the desert
opt3: Like a travailer overwhelmed with midnight labor whose child dieth before the dawn
opt4: Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs ... We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth
correct: Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs ... We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth
explanation: Israel's self-effort produced agonizing labor pains that resulted only in wind - an empty, phantom pregnancy achieving zero national deliverance. Isaiah 26:17-18 (KJV) - "Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery, is in pain, and crieth out in her pangs; so have we been in thy sight, O LORD. We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have as it were brought forth wind; we have not wrought any deliverance in the earth; neither have the inhabitants of the world fallen."

question: What glorious Old Testament affirmation of bodily resurrection shatters the despair of death in Isaiah 26:19?
opt1: Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead
opt2: The spirit shall return unto God who gave it, and the righteous shall dwell in eternal light
opt3: The dry bones shall come together bone to bone, and breath shall enter into them from the four winds
opt4: The trumpet shall sound, and the sons of Abraham shall be gathered from the islands of the sea
correct: Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead
explanation: God answers human failure with physical resurrection: dead bodies will arise from the dust, refreshed by life-giving divine dew like reviving plants. Isaiah 26:19 (KJV) - "Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead."

question: What pastoral shelter instruction is given to God's people while cosmic judgment passes over the earth in Isaiah 26:20?
opt1: Flee unto the mountains of Judah, and pitch thy tents in the secret caves of the rocks
opt2: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast
opt3: Gird on your armor, ye righteous, and stand upon the walls of Jerusalem until the morning
opt4: Assemble yourselves in the courts of the sanctuary, and weep between the porch and the altar
correct: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast
explanation: Echoing the Passover night in Egypt, believers are tenderly told to retreat into their inner chambers and shut doors until God's wrath finishes its course. Isaiah 26:20 (KJV) - "Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee: hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast."

question: What moral exposure will occur when the LORD cometh out of His place to punish global iniquity in Isaiah 26:21?
opt1: The secret idols of darkness shall be cast into the public marketplace
opt2: The foundations of the palaces shall be uncovered, exposing the stolen treasures
opt3: The earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain
opt4: The sea shall give up the dead which are in it, and all crowns shall be dissolved
correct: The earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain
explanation: Earth will no longer conceal hidden murders or unavenged bloodshed; every martyred victim and violent crime will be fully exposed and judged. Isaiah 26:21 (KJV) - "For, behold, the LORD cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their iniquity: the earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain."

question: What monstrous chaotic marine adversaries does the LORD punish with His sore, great, and strong sword in Isaiah 27:1?
opt1: Behemoth the beast of the reed marshes, and the winged griffin of the mountains
opt2: The four-headed lion of the deep, and the horned ram of the northern rivers
opt3: Leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea
opt4: The great scorpion of the desert, and the roaring lion of the thickets of Jordan
correct: Leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea
explanation: God wields His cosmic sword to slay Leviathan (the fleeing, twisting sea monster / dragon), representing both demonic chaos powers and oppressive worldly empires. Isaiah 27:1 (KJV) - "In that day the LORD with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea."

question: What song of perpetual divine cultivation and vigilant protection celebrates God's redeemed people in Isaiah 27:2-3?
opt1: An olive grove of choice oil. I have hedged it with cedar posts, and planted it upon Mount Zion
opt2: A garden of fragrant spices. My hand hath watered the lilies, and no spoiler shall enter its gates
opt3: An orchard of sweet pomegranates. I have gathered out the stones, and the spring thereof is sealed
opt4: A vineyard of red wine. I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day
correct: A vineyard of red wine. I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day
explanation: Reversing the tragic song of the unfruitful vineyard in Chapter 5, God now tenderly cultivates His fruitful vineyard of red wine, watering and guarding it 24/7. Isaiah 27:2-3 (KJV) - "In that day sing ye unto her, A vineyard of red wine. I the LORD do keep it; I will water it every moment: lest any hurt it, I will keep it night and day."

question: What gracious alternative does God offer to adversaries rather than facing His consuming battle fury in Isaiah 27:5?
opt1: Let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me
opt2: Let him bring an hundred rams unto the altar, and confess his iniquity before the priest
opt3: Let him bow his head in sackcloth, and fast forty days in the wilderness of the south
opt4: Let him pay tribute of refined silver, and take an oath of allegiance to the king of Judah
correct: Let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me
explanation: Even opponents are invited to lay hold of God's protective refuge ('take hold of my strength') and establish genuine reconciliation and peace. Isaiah 27:5 (KJV) - "Or let him take hold of my strength, that he may make peace with me; and he shall make peace with me."

question: What global horticultural blessing will result when the root of Jacob buds and blossoms in Isaiah 27:6?
opt1: The vines of Judah shall yield sweet wine to satisfy all the kingdoms of the Gentiles
opt2: He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit
opt3: The cedars of Lebanon shall cover the barren hills from the Euphrates unto the sea
opt4: The desert shall rejoice and blossom like the rose, and living waters shall heal the nations
correct: He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit
explanation: Israel takes permanent root, blossoming and filling the entire globe with spiritual fruitfulness under Messianic restoration. Isaiah 27:6 (KJV) - "He shall cause them that come of Jacob to take root: Israel shall blossom and bud, and fill the face of the world with fruit."

question: What measured difference distinguishes God's chastisement of Israel from His total destruction of her imperial conquerors in Isaiah 27:7-8?
opt1: He smote Israel with a bronze rod, but her enemies were broken with a mighty hammer of iron
opt2: He scattered her people for seventy years, but her conquerors were blotted out under seventy cubits of salt
opt3: In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind
opt4: He burned her gates with fire, but drowned her adversaries in the depths of the sea
correct: In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind
explanation: God chastens Israel with paternal restraint ('in measure'), moderating the harsh east wind of judgment, whereas pagan empires were annihilated without mercy. Isaiah 27:7-8 (KJV) - "Hath he smitten him, as he smote those that smote him? or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that are slain by him? In measure, when it shooteth forth, thou wilt debate with it: he stayeth his rough wind in the day of the east wind."

question: What total demolition of idolatrous paraphernalia demonstrates the authentic purgation of Jacob's sin in Isaiah 27:9?
opt1: When he melteth the golden calves into temple vessels and burneth the books of sorcery
opt2: When he overthroweth the high places of Baal and slayeth the false prophets with the sword
opt3: When he grindeth the images of silver into powder and casteth the dust into the brook Kidron
opt4: When he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up
correct: When he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up
explanation: True repentance pulverizes pagan altars like soft, crushed chalkstones, toppling sacred Asherah poles ('groves') and sun-images forever. Isaiah 27:9 (KJV) - "By this therefore shall the iniquity of Jacob be purged; and this is all the fruit to take away his sin; when he maketh all the stones of the altar as chalkstones that are beaten in sunder, the groves and images shall not stand up."

question: Why does the Creator refuse to show compassion or favor to the ruined, fortified city in Isaiah 27:11?
opt1: For it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will shew them no favour
opt2: Because they sold the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of shoes in the gates
opt3: Because they shed the blood of the righteous prophets and mocked the covenant of the Lord
opt4: Because they allied themselves with the kings of Egypt and rejected the word of the seers
correct: For it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will shew them no favour
explanation: Willful, obstinate spiritual stupidity ('a people of no understanding') cuts sinners off from their Creator's mercy and favor. Isaiah 27:11 (KJV) - "For it is a people of no understanding: therefore he that made them will not have mercy on them, and he that formed them will shew them no favour."

question: What individual threshing and harvesting method will the LORD use to recover the dispersed children of Israel in Isaiah 27:12?
opt1: He shall separate the sheep from the goats by the sound of his voice in the valleys
opt2: The LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel
opt3: He shall weigh them in the balances of righteousness and bring them home by thousands
opt4: He shall transport them in the chariots of the Gentiles across the great rivers
correct: The LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel
explanation: From the Euphrates ('the river') to the Wadi of Egypt, God meticulously gathers His elect individually ('one by one') like grain carefully beaten from the ear. Isaiah 27:12 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the LORD shall beat off from the channel of the river unto the stream of Egypt, and ye shall be gathered one by one, O ye children of Israel."

question: What instrument of international summoning will gather the perishing outcasts from Assyria and Egypt to worship on Mount Zion in Isaiah 27:13?
opt1: The silver horn of the high priest shall be sounded from the pinnacle of the temple
opt2: The voice of the archangel shall shout from the clouds of heaven with a mighty noise
opt3: The great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem
opt4: The royal standard of the house of David shall be lifted up upon the mount of Olives
correct: The great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem
explanation: The blast of the great shofar ('great trumpet') resounds across the ancient world, gathering dying exiles to worship Yahweh on His holy mountain. Isaiah 27:13 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass in that day, that the great trumpet shall be blown, and they shall come which were ready to perish in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts in the land of Egypt, and shall worship the LORD in the holy mount at Jerusalem."

question: What domestic animals browse and bed down among the broken, deserted boughs of the ruined fortress city in Isaiah 27:10?
opt1: The flocks of the nomads shall graze, and wild goats shall leap upon the stones
opt2: The jackals shall lair in the courts, and owls shall nest in the royal chambers
opt3: The foxes shall run over the ramparts, and the wild ass shall quench its thirst
opt4: There shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof
correct: There shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof
explanation: Calves peacefully graze and strip leaves from overgrown vegetation in the abandoned streets of the former imperial metropolis. Isaiah 27:10 (KJV) - "Yet the defenced city shall be desolate, and the habitation forsaken, and left like a wilderness: there shall the calf feed, and there shall he lie down, and consume the branches thereof."

question: What intoxicated leaders are denounced in the opening woe of Isaiah 28:1?
opt1: Woe to the elders of Judah, who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with costly ointments!
opt2: Woe to the princes of Samaria, who feast upon fatted calves and recline upon beds of ivory!
opt3: Woe to the false prophets of Bethel, who stumble in vision and drink strong drink before the altar!
opt4: Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!
correct: Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!
explanation: Isaiah condemns the aristocratic rulers of northern Israel (Ephraim/Samaria) whose decadent alcoholic debauchery blinded them to imminent Assyrian doom. Isaiah 28:1 (KJV) - "Woe to the crown of pride, to the drunkards of Ephraim, whose glorious beauty is a fading flower, which are on the head of the fat valleys of them that are overcome with wine!"

question: To what tempting agricultural delicacy is Samaria's rapidly snatched glorious beauty compared in Isaiah 28:4?
opt1: As the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up
opt2: As an early cluster of grapes in the vineyard, which the traveler plucketh and devoureth
opt3: As a ripe pomegranate fallen from the bough, which is crushed beneath the foot of the reaper
opt4: As an ear of corn roasted in the fire, which the hungry labourer swalloweth without chewing
correct: As the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up
explanation: Samaria is like an early ripe first-crop fig ('hasty fruit before the summer'), greedily spotted and instantly devoured by the Assyrian conqueror. Isaiah 28:4 (KJV) - "And the glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fat valley, shall be a fading flower, and as the hasty fruit before the summer; which when he that looketh upon it seeth, while it is yet in his hand he eateth it up."

question: In contrast to worldly garlands, what glorious regalia will the LORD of hosts become to His remnant in Isaiah 28:5?
opt1: A scepter of gold, and a shield of triumph, unto the twelve tribes of Jacob
opt2: For a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people
opt3: A robe of fine linen, and an breastplate of precious gems, unto the house of Aaron
opt4: A tower of strength, and an horn of salvation, unto the sons of the covenant
correct: For a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people
explanation: Yahweh Sabaoth Himself replaces transient earthly floral wreaths, becoming an unfading crown of glory and radiant diadem for the faithful remnant. Isaiah 28:5 (KJV) - "In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty, unto the residue of his people,"

question: What disgusting state of spiritual and physical contamination defiled the judicial and religious leaders of Jerusalem in Isaiah 28:7-8?
opt1: They took bribes of silver from the hands of the oppressor, and justified the wicked for reward
opt2: They burned incense upon the house tops to the host of heaven, and offered strange fire at the altar
opt3: The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean
opt4: They altered the weights of the sanctuary, and robbed the fatherless of their ancestral vineyards
correct: The priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean
explanation: Judah's priests and prophets were so completely inebriated that their banquet tables were covered in vomit, rendering them incapable of discerning vision or executing justice. Isaiah 28:7-8 (KJV) - "But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink, they are swallowed up of wine, they are out of the way through strong drink; they err in vision, they stumble in judgment. For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean."

question: How did the arrogant Jerusalem leaders mock Isaiah's elementary prophetic instruction in Isaiah 28:9-10?
opt1: Doth he speak in parables to mock the princes? or doth he invent visions out of his own heart?
opt2: Is he not the son of Amoz who knoweth nothing of the politics of Egypt and the treaties of kings?
opt3: Why doth he howl like an owl in the night, and weep like a woman before the gates of the city?
opt4: Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little
correct: Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little
explanation: The cynical leaders sneered that Isaiah treated them like toddlers just weaned from breast milk, mimicking his repetitive teaching as babble (tzav la-tzav, qav la-qav). Isaiah 28:9-10 (KJV) - "Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine? them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts. For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little:"

question: How will God ironically speak to this rebellious nation that refused His gentle message of rest in Isaiah 28:11-12?
opt1: For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear
opt2: With the lightning of heaven and the roar of thunder from Mount Sinai
opt3: Through the mouth of Egyptian sorcerers and the diviners of the Philistines
opt4: By the total silence of the prophets and the withdrawal of the holy presence
correct: For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear
explanation: Because they mocked God's clear word, Yahweh will 'preach' to them through the harsh, guttural, foreign language ('another tongue') of invading Assyrian conquerors (1 Corinthians 14:21). Isaiah 28:11-12 (KJV) - "For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people. To whom he said, This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest; and this is the refreshing: yet they would not hear."

question: What false security and deceptive pact did Jerusalem's cynical rulers boast of in Isaiah 28:15?
opt1: We have sealed an eternal alliance with the pharaoh of Egypt, and his chariots of iron shall protect our gates
opt2: We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves
opt3: We have stored ten thousand talents of silver in the citadel, and no foreign king can breach our ramparts
opt4: The temple of the LORD is in our midst, and the angel of the covenant will destroy all our adversaries
correct: We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves
explanation: The rulers cynically claimed immunity from the Assyrian invasion ('overflowing scourge') by forging a treaty with death and Sheol (their secret Egyptian alliance). Isaiah 28:15 (KJV) - "Because ye have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with hell are we at agreement; when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto us: for we have made lies our refuge, and under falsehood have we hid ourselves:"

question: What divine foundation stone does the Lord GOD lay in Zion as the only secure object of faith in Isaiah 28:16?
opt1: A pillar of granite, a golden altar, an ark of the covenant, a permanent refuge: he that trusteth shall never tremble
opt2: A mountain of brass, a rock of salvation, an eternal fortress, an holy hill: he that hopeth shall overcome
opt3: Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste
opt4: A scepter of righteousness, a horn of power, an imperial throne, a royal crown: he that followeth shall reign
correct: Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste
explanation: Quoted in 1 Peter 2:6 and Romans 9:33, God establishes the Messianic Cornerstone - tested, precious, and sure; whoever trusts in Him will never panic or be confounded. Isaiah 28:16 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation: he that believeth shall not make haste."

question: What uncomfortable folk proverb describes the acute inadequacy of worldly human defenses in Isaiah 28:20?
opt1: The shoes are tighter than that a man can run in them, and the tunic thinner than that it can shield the cold
opt2: The wall is lower than that it can keep out the archers, and the gate weaker than that it can bar the chariot
opt3: The cistern is shallower than that it can hold the rain, and the vessel cracked so that all water leaketh out
opt4: For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it
correct: For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it
explanation: A graphic proverb illustrates total insufficiency: trying to find security in human treaties is like lying on a bed too short to stretch out and wrapping in a blanket too narrow to cover oneself. Isaiah 28:20 (KJV) - "For the bed is shorter than that a man can stretch himself on it: and the covering narrower than that he can wrap himself in it."

question: What agricultural parable illustrates God's diversified, patient, and purposeful wisdom in dealing with His people in Isaiah 28:23-29?
opt1: The farmer plows to prepare the soil, sows varied seeds (dill, cummin, wheat, barley, rye) in appointed order, and threshes each grain with appropriate tools (staff, rod, cartwheel), reflecting the wonderful counsel of the LORD of hosts
opt2: The vinedresser prunes the branches in winter, waters the roots with sweet wine, and harvests only when the moon is full
opt3: The shepherd leads the sheep to quiet pastures, shears the wool in summer, and protects the flock from desert wolves
opt4: The olive farmer shakes the boughs with an iron pole, presses the fruit in stone vats, and pours the oil into cedar jars
correct: The farmer plows to prepare the soil, sows varied seeds (dill, cummin, wheat, barley, rye) in appointed order, and threshes each grain with appropriate tools (staff, rod, cartwheel), reflecting the wonderful counsel of the LORD of hosts
explanation: God acts like a discerning farmer who uses varied techniques tailored for each crop: His varied judgments and disciplines are not mindless destruction, but designed with supreme wisdom. Isaiah 28:27, 29 (KJV) - "For the fitches are not threshed with a threshing instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned about upon the cummin; but the fitches are beaten out with a staff, and the cummin with a rod ... This also cometh forth from the LORD of hosts, which is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in working."

question: What symbolic altar-hearth name is applied to Jerusalem, the city where David dwelt, in Isaiah 29:1-2?
opt1: Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices. Yet I will distress Ariel, and it shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel
opt2: Woe to Moriah, the mountain of sacrifice and the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite!
opt3: Woe to Jebus, the ancient fortress of the valley and the stronghold of the giants!
opt4: Woe to Salem, the city of peace and the sanctuary of Melchizedek the priest of God!
correct: Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices. Yet I will distress Ariel, and it shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel
explanation: Ariel ('Lion of God' or 'Altar-hearth') represents Jerusalem, which will become like a blazing sacrificial altar-hearth filled with slaughter during siege. Isaiah 29:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let them kill sacrifices. Yet I will distress Ariel, and it shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel."

question: To what eerie, subterranean whisper is Jerusalem's humiliated speech compared when brought low by siege in Isaiah 29:4?
opt1: Thy voice shall be like the cry of a fledgling fallen into the dry thorns of the terrace
opt2: Thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust
opt3: Thy words shall be like the groaning of a prisoner in the deep pit of Malchiah
opt4: Thy lamentation shall be like the mourning of doves hidden in the crags of the rocks
correct: Thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust
explanation: Jerusalem is brought down to the dirt, her proud speech reduced to a muffled, ghostly whisper like a necromancer muttering from the ground. Isaiah 29:4 (KJV) - "And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be, as of one that hath a familiar spirit, out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust."

question: With what terrifying meteorological and seismic phenomena will the LORD of hosts suddenly visit the besiegers in Isaiah 29:6?
opt1: With a thick cloud of locusts, a pestilence of biting flies, and the turning of the springs into blood
opt2: With an eclipse of the sun, seven lightning bolts striking the towers, and a shower of brimstone
opt3: Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire
opt4: With the sword of an hundred thousand angels, a fiery whirlwind from the south, and an overflowing morass
correct: Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire
explanation: God intervenes cataclysmically to defend His city with thunder, earthquake, deafening roar, tempest, and devouring fire. Isaiah 29:6 (KJV) - "Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire."

question: To what frustrating psychological dream experiences is the sudden disappearance of the invading coalition compared in Isaiah 29:7-8?
opt1: As when a traveler dreameth of finding gold, but awaketh with empty hands in the wilderness
opt2: As when a warrior dreameth of striking down his foe, but awaketh unarmed before his captain
opt3: As when an exile dreameth of returning to his home, but awaketh in chains in a foreign land
opt4: As when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite
correct: As when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite
explanation: The attackers' confident anticipation of conquering Jerusalem dissolves like an illusory dream of eating and drinking that leaves one hungry and thirsty upon waking. Isaiah 29:7-8 (KJV) - "And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel ... shall be as a dream of a night vision. It shall even be as when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion."

question: What metaphor of a sealed book exposes the universal spiritual illiteracy of both the educated and uneducated in Isaiah 29:11-12?
opt1: The words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed: and the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned
opt2: A scroll eaten by moths, which the priest cannot unfold, and the Levite cannot read because the letters are blotted
opt3: A tablet of bronze buried in the dust, which the scholar cannot decipher, and the soldier cannot lift
opt4: A papyrus written in Egyptian hieroglyphs, which the scribe cannot interpret, and the elder rejecteth
correct: The words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed: and the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned
explanation: Judicial blindness affects all classes: the learned excuse themselves because the revelation is 'sealed,' while the unlearned claim basic illiteracy. Isaiah 29:11-12 (KJV) - "And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed: And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned."

question: What famous divine indictment denounces external lip-service religion divorced from authentic heart devotion in Isaiah 29:13?
opt1: They offer sheep without blemish, but their thoughts are set upon the riches of the uncircumcised
opt2: Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men
opt3: They keep the new moons and sabbaths, but they pervert justice in the gate and oppress the poor
opt4: They wear wide phylacteries and pray in public streets, but their souls are full of extortion and excess
correct: Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men
explanation: Quoted by Jesus in Matthew 15:8-9, God condemns superficial, hypocritical ritualism: honoring God verbally while their hearts remain alienated and guided only by human tradition. Isaiah 29:13 (KJV) - "Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men:"

question: How does God overthrow human intellectual arrogance through His 'marvellous work and a wonder' in Isaiah 29:14?
opt1: For the scribes shall be struck dumb, and the philosophers of Egypt shall be led away in chains
opt2: For the royal counsellors shall wander in darkness, and their treaties shall be burned in the fire
opt3: For the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid
opt4: For the high priest shall forget the statutes, and the kings of the earth shall stumble like children
correct: For the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid
explanation: Quoted in 1 Corinthians 1:19, God's supernatural redemptive wisdom confounds and bankrupts the worldly wisdom of secular intellectuals and politicians. Isaiah 29:14 (KJV) - "Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid."

question: What absurdity of upside-down thinking is exposed by the potter and clay analogy in Isaiah 29:16?
opt1: Shall the clay dictate the price of the vessel in the marketplace of the merchants?
opt2: Shall the broken potsherd boast that it was forged in the royal furnace of the king?
opt3: Shall the vessel of earth claim that it was shaped from the gold of Ophir?
opt4: Shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?
correct: Shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?
explanation: Creaturely pride inverting relationship with the Creator is as ludicrous as a manufactured pot claiming its potter never made it or lacked intelligence. Isaiah 29:16 (KJV) - "Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?"

question: What miraculous sensory and spiritual healing will occur when God's revelation is unsealed in Isaiah 29:18-19?
opt1: And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel
opt2: The lame shall leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb shall sing the songs of the temple
opt3: The lepers shall be cleansed with holy water, and the brokenhearted shall receive crowns of gold
opt4: The dead shall walk out of their sepulchres, and the captives shall return across the river
correct: And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel
explanation: Spiritual deafness and blindness are healed; the humble, downtrodden poor experience exuberant joy in the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 29:18-19 (KJV) - "And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel."

question: What corrupt legal predators and judicial conspirators will be completely eradicated in Isaiah 29:20-21?
opt1: They that take bribes of gold from foreign merchants and sell the inheritance of the fatherless
opt2: All that watch for iniquity are cut off: that make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought
opt3: They that forge false signet rings and alter the royal decrees of the house of David
opt4: They that hire false witnesses in the darkness and justify murder for an hundred talents of silver
correct: All that watch for iniquity are cut off: that make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought
explanation: God eliminates unscrupulous legalists who trap people over a single word, entrap honest whistleblowers in the city gate, and defraud the innocent on trivial pretexts. Isaiah 29:20-21 (KJV) - "For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off: That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought."

question: What rebellious political delegation to Egypt is condemned in the opening woe of Isaiah 30:1-2?
opt1: Woe to the princes of Judah, who send merchant caravans unto Tyre to buy cedar and iron chariots!
opt2: Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: that walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
