opt3: Woe to the royal ambassadors, who march unto Babylon with gifts of gold and silver from the temple treasury!
opt4: Woe to the captains of the host, who hire mercenaries from the Philistines and fortify the passes of Benjamin!
correct: Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: that walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!
explanation: Judah's leaders bypassed God's prophetic guidance, sending a secret diplomatic mission to Egypt to seek military shelter under Pharaoh's shadow. Isaiah 30:1-2 (KJV) - "Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!"

question: What ultimate outcome will result from trusting in Pharaoh's protection and Egyptian military aid in Isaiah 30:3?
opt1: Therefore shall the chariots of Egypt be burned with fire, and their horses drowned in the deep
opt2: Therefore shall Pharaoh demand the temple treasures of gold, and enslave the daughters of Zion
opt3: Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion
opt4: Therefore shall the king of Assyria conquer both Jerusalem and the cities of the delta in one year
correct: Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion
explanation: Worldly alliances deliver only public humiliation and disillusionment: Pharaoh's strength turns to shameful failure. Isaiah 30:3 (KJV) - "Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion."

question: What mocking title does Isaiah bestow upon Egypt, exposing her complete military uselessness, in Isaiah 30:7?
opt1: A bruised reed that pierceth the hand
opt2: A roaring dragon whose teeth are broken
opt3: A painted chariot without horses
opt4: Their strength is to sit still
correct: Their strength is to sit still
explanation: Isaiah calls Egypt Rahab Hem Shevet ('Rahab the Do-Nothing' / 'Their strength is to sit still'): she makes boastful promises like a mythical monster, but sits completely idle when war breaks out. Isaiah 30:7 (KJV) - "For the Egyptians shall help in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I cried concerning this, Their strength is to sit still."

question: What corrupt demands did the rebellious populace make of their seers and prophets in Isaiah 30:9-11?
opt1: Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us
opt2: Declare unto us the victories of our fathers, and tell us that the Assyrian shall flee without striking a blow
opt3: Interpret the signs of the stars, and reveal unto us the day when the silver tribute shall cease
opt4: Bless the covenants of our princes, and swear that the altar of Jerusalem shall stand forever
correct: Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us
explanation: Apostate citizens demanded pleasant delusions ('smooth things') and complete silence regarding the demanding moral holiness of Yahweh. Isaiah 30:10-11 (KJV) - "Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things, speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits: Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us."

question: To what sudden structural collapse of a bulging high wall is the nation's catastrophic ruin compared in Isaiah 30:13?
opt1: As a cedar undermined by floods, which falls crashing into the canyon
opt2: As a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant
opt3: As an iron gate whose bolts are broken, admitting the invading cavalry
opt4: As a ship striking a hidden reef, sinking into the depths of the sea
correct: As a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant
explanation: Sin creates an unstable bulge in a high stone masonry wall that unexpectedly bursts into sudden, violent, total collapse. Isaiah 30:13 (KJV) - "Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant."

question: How complete is the shattering of the nation, illustrated by a smashed clay potter's jar in Isaiah 30:14?
opt1: The fragments shall be ground into dust so that not a grain of clay remaineth
opt2: The broken pieces shall be scattered across seven valleys by the whirlwind
opt3: There shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit
opt4: The shards shall cut the feet of the reapers and be trampled into the mud
correct: There shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit
explanation: The clay pot is shattered so thoroughly that not even a single usable piece remains large enough to scoop an ember from a hearth or water from a puddle. Isaiah 30:14 (KJV) - "And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters' vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit."

question: What definitive formula of salvation, quiet trust, and spiritual strength did Judah tragically reject in Isaiah 30:15?
opt1: In prayer and fasting shall ye conquer; in obedience and sacrifice shall be your victory: and ye refused
opt2: In swords of iron and swift cavalry shall ye prevail; in alliances of silver shall be your hope: and ye failed
opt3: In the temple of the Lord and the songs of Zion shall ye abide; in the law of Moses shall be your glory: and ye wandered
opt4: In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not
correct: In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not
explanation: True spiritual victory comes through repentance, resting in God, calm trust, and faithful confidence - yet rebellious Judah stubbornly refused. Isaiah 30:15 (KJV) - "For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not."

question: Why does the sovereign LORD wait with divine patience despite human rebellion in Isaiah 30:18?
opt1: And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him
opt2: That he may see whether any among the princes of Judah will humble themselves before the altar
opt3: That the iniquity of the Assyrians may reach its full measure before he sendeth his destroying angel
opt4: That the seventy years of captivity may be accomplished according to the word of the prophets
correct: And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him
explanation: God delays immediate judgment so He may display grace and compassionate mercy to all who faithfully wait for Him. Isaiah 30:18 (KJV) - "And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him."

question: What internal spiritual guidance will guide the obedient walker when facing moral or practical crossroads in Isaiah 30:21?
opt1: And a pillar of cloud shall lead thee by day, and a fire shall guide thy footsteps in the night
opt2: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left
opt3: And an angel shall stand at the crossroads with a drawn sword pointing to the path of life
opt4: And the high priest shall declare the judgment of the Urim whenever thou enquirest of the Lord
correct: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left
explanation: Believers are promised intimate, unmistakable divine direction - a quiet voice whispering from behind: 'This is the way, walk ye in it.' Isaiah 30:21 (KJV) - "And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left."

question: What vast, fiery pyre is prepared for the funeral destruction of the Assyrian monarch in Isaiah 30:33?
opt1: A furnace of bronze erected in the valley of Kidron, heated seven times hotter by the priests
opt2: A burning pit in the desert of Edom, fueled with asphalt and sulfur from the Dead Sea
opt3: Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it
opt4: A fiery grave on Mount Moriah, kindled with the cedar timber of the ruined palaces
correct: Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it
explanation: Tophet (the blazing refuse trench in the Hinnom Valley) is prepared on a cosmic scale for the Assyrian emperor, ignited by the brimstone breath of Yahweh Himself. Isaiah 30:33 (KJV) - "For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it."

question: What fundamental ontological contrast between human frailty and divine omnipotence exposes the folly of trusting Egyptian cavalry in Isaiah 31:3?
opt1: The chariots of Pharaoh are made of wood and iron, but the chariots of the Lord are twenty thousand angels of fire
opt2: The horsemen of Egypt are mortals subject to death, but the captains of the host of heaven live forever
opt3: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together
opt4: The horses of Egypt stumble in the stony valleys, but the wings of the cherubim fly above the clouds
correct: Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together
explanation: Isaiah sharply distinguishes the Creator from creation: Egyptian allies are merely finite men and their horses perishable flesh, incapable of withstanding God's Spirit. Isaiah 31:3 (KJV) - "Now the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit. When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together."

question: To what fearless predator refusing to be intimidated by a multitude of shouting shepherds is the LORD compared in Isaiah 31:4?
opt1: Like an eagle guarding its aerie from the fowler upon the rocky cliffs
opt2: Like a wild bull charging through the nets of the hunters in the forest of Lebanon
opt3: Like a mighty leopard leaping from the crags upon the flocks of the wilderness
opt4: Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the LORD of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion
correct: Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the LORD of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion
explanation: Yahweh Sabaoth descends to protect Mount Zion with the unyielding, majestic fearlessness of a roaring lion refusing to be scared off by shouting shepherds. Isaiah 31:4 (KJV) - "For thus hath the LORD spoken unto me, Like as the lion and the young lion roaring on his prey, when a multitude of shepherds is called forth against him, he will not be afraid of their voice, nor abase himself for the noise of them: so shall the LORD of hosts come down to fight for mount Zion, and for the hill thereof."

question: What maternal bird imagery portrays God's protective and preserving deliverance of Jerusalem in Isaiah 31:5?
opt1: As birds flying, so will the LORD of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it
opt2: As an hen gathereth her chickens under her wings in the day of the storm
opt3: As an eagle stirreth up her nest and fluttereth over her young in the desert
opt4: As a dove fluttering over the waters of the sanctuary when the enemy approacheth
correct: As birds flying, so will the LORD of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it
explanation: Echoing Exodus Passover imagery ('passing over'), God hovers over Jerusalem like protective parent birds defending their nest against predators. Isaiah 31:5 (KJV) - "As birds flying, so will the LORD of hosts defend Jerusalem; defending also he will deliver it; and passing over he will preserve it."

question: By what supernatural weapon will the invading Assyrian army fall, excluding human military prowess, in Isaiah 31:8?
opt1: With the iron swords of the valiant men of Judah charging from the gates of Zion
opt2: Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited
opt3: With the spears of the princes of the Medes who surround his royal pavilion
opt4: With the arrows of the archers of Egypt ambushing his host in the valley of Elah
correct: Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited
explanation: Sennacherib's army is destroyed not by human warriors (neither mighty aristocrats nor ordinary soldiers), but by the supernatural sword of the Angel of the LORD. Isaiah 31:8 (KJV) - "Then shall the Assyrian fall with the sword, not of a mighty man; and the sword, not of a mean man, shall devour him: but he shall flee from the sword, and his young men shall be discomfited."

question: Where are the holy fire and consuming furnace of the LORD situated according to Isaiah 31:9?
opt1: In the clouds of Mount Sinai where the law was given
opt2: In the holy of holies between the wings of the cherubim
opt3: Saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem
opt4: In the highest heavens above the constellations of the stars
correct: Saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem
explanation: Jerusalem is the terrestrial seat of God's holy altar-fire and refining furnace, consuming all foreign imperial invaders who dare attack it. Isaiah 31:9 (KJV) - "And he shall pass over to his strong hold for fear, and his princes shall be afraid of the ensign, saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem."

question: What practical repentance must accompany Israel's return to the LORD in Isaiah 31:6-7?
opt1: They shall fast forty days and forty nights in sackcloth and ashes
opt2: They shall bring five hundred talents of silver to rebuild the breaches of the wall
opt3: They shall banish all foreign ambassadors from the gates of Jerusalem
opt4: Every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin
correct: Every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin
explanation: Authentic spiritual renewal demands immediate, radical repudiation of manufactured idols of silver and gold. Isaiah 31:6-7 (KJV) - "Turn ye unto him from whom the children of Israel have deeply revolted. For in that day every man shall cast away his idols of silver, and his idols of gold, which your own hands have made unto you for a sin."

question: Why is relying on Egyptian chariots condemned as spiritual apostasy in Isaiah 31:1?
opt1: Because they stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD!
opt2: Because Egyptian horses were bred from unholy stock forbidden under the statutes of Aaron
opt3: Because Pharaoh demanded human sacrifices in exchange for military assistance
opt4: Because foreign chariots were unable to navigate the steep rocky terraces of Judea
correct: Because they stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD!
explanation: The core sin was displacement of faith: trusting quantitative military might (vast cavalry) while entirely ignoring the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah 31:1 (KJV) - "Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the LORD!"

question: What happens to both the pagan helper (Egypt) and the helped nation (Judah) if they persist in ungodly alliance in Isaiah 31:3?
opt1: The helper shall enslave the helped, and sell their children into foreign lands
opt2: Both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together
opt3: The helper shall be burned with fire, but the helped shall escape into the mountains
opt4: The helper shall flee across the sea, leaving the helped to be devoured by the sword
correct: Both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together
explanation: Human alliances cannot resist divine judgment: both the foreign protector and the protected nation collapse together in shared ruin. Isaiah 31:3 (KJV) - "When the LORD shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together."

question: What psychological panic seizes the Assyrian officers before the divine standard in Isaiah 31:9?
opt1: His captains shall cast away their bronze helmets and flee into the desert
opt2: His horsemen shall turn their swords against their own generals in darkness
opt3: His princes shall be afraid of the ensign
opt4: His archers shall break their bows upon the rocks and beg for bread
correct: His princes shall be afraid of the ensign
explanation: Assyria's elite commanders are paralyzed with dread at the sight of Yahweh's raised battle standard (the ensign). Isaiah 31:9 (KJV) - "And he shall pass over to his strong hold for fear, and his princes shall be afraid of the ensign, saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem."

question: How does Isaiah affirm that God's wisdom surpasses all secular diplomatic intelligence in Isaiah 31:2?
opt1: For he understandeth the secrets of the stars and knoweth the thoughts of kings
opt2: For his counsel is deeper than the ocean and his decrees cannot be shaken
opt3: For he confoundeth the astrologers of the east and maketh diviners mad
opt4: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers
correct: Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers
explanation: Isaiah uses irony: Judah's politicians thought themselves shrewd in negotiating treaties, but Yahweh 'also is wise' and His declared judgments are irreversible. Isaiah 31:2 (KJV) - "Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words: but will arise against the house of the evildoers, and against the help of them that work iniquity."

question: What righteous administration opens the Messianic kingdom vision in Isaiah 32:1?
opt1: Behold, a priest shall minister in holiness, and the sons of Aaron shall offer pure incense
opt2: Behold, a conqueror shall tread down the heathen, and his armies shall divide the spoil
opt3: Behold, a prophet shall arise like unto Moses, and all nations shall keep the sabbath
opt4: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment
correct: Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment
explanation: The Messianic era features a King reigning in absolute moral righteousness alongside princes governing with equitable justice. Isaiah 32:1 (KJV) - "Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment."

question: What four sheltering and refreshing metaphors describe the Messianic King (or righteous ruler) in Isaiah 32:2?
opt1: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land
opt2: A shield against the arrow, a fortress on the hill, an horn of salvation, and a crown of beauty
opt3: A fruitful vine on the terrace, a well of living water, an olive tree of peace, and an holy sanctuary
opt4: A tower of granite, a golden scepter, a fountain of wisdom, and a pavilion of fine linen
correct: And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land
explanation: Christ the righteous Man provides total protection (wind-shelter, tempest-covert) and life-giving revitalization (oasis rivers, massive rock shadow). Isaiah 32:2 (KJV) - "And a man shall be as an hiding place from the wind, and a covert from the tempest; as rivers of water in a dry place, as the shadow of a great rock in a weary land."

question: What moral clarity and linguistic integrity will abolish political correctness and ethical whitewashing in Isaiah 32:5?
opt1: The false prophet shall no more wear a rough garment to deceive, nor the hypocrite boast of fasting
opt2: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful
opt3: The oppressor shall no more be honored in the gate, nor the usurer welcomed in the courts
opt4: The wicked shall no more justify themselves by treaties, nor the thief boast of royal favor
correct: The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful
explanation: Society's moral vocabulary will be purified: scoundrels will no longer be praised as noble/generous ('liberal'), nor will greedy misers ('churls') be lauded as benefactors. Isaiah 32:5 (KJV) - "The vile person shall be no more called liberal, nor the churl said to be bountiful."

question: What noble character and enduring legacy distinguishes the truly generous person in Isaiah 32:8?
opt1: The righteous man giveth his bread to the hungry, and his name shall be remembered forever
opt2: The merciful man showeth mercy unto the poor, and his inheritance shall never fade
opt3: The liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand
opt4: The wise man storeth up understanding, and his children shall be honored in the gate
correct: The liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand
explanation: True nobility plans noble, generous deeds ('deviseth liberal things') and is permanently established by practicing that generous righteousness. Isaiah 32:8 (KJV) - "But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand."

question: What complacency of aristocratic women is condemned, warning of agricultural failure within a year in Isaiah 32:9-10?
opt1: Weep, ye daughters of Jerusalem, who recline upon ivory couches; for the bread of the palace is consumed
opt2: Gird yourselves with sackcloth, ye maidens of Zion; for your golden ornaments shall be taken away
opt3: Howl, ye women that drink sweet wine; for the vineyards of En-gedi are trodden down by the host
opt4: Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech. Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come
correct: Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech. Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come
explanation: Self-satisfied, indolent aristocratic women who live in careless luxury are jolted with the warning that the grape harvest and fruit gathering will totally fail. Isaiah 32:9-10 (KJV) - "Rise up, ye women that are at ease; hear my voice, ye careless daughters; give ear unto my speech. Many days and years shall ye be troubled, ye careless women: for the vintage shall fail, the gathering shall not come."

question: What catastrophic urban desertion transforms luxury palaces into animal dens in Isaiah 32:14?
opt1: The palaces shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; the forts and towers shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks
opt2: The royal chambers shall be filled with owls, and jackals shall howl upon the threshold of David
opt3: The mansions of the princes shall become heaps of chalk, and vipers shall nest in the royal baths
opt4: The citadel shall be plowed like a field of barley, and foxes shall run across the altar of burnt offerings
correct: The palaces shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; the forts and towers shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks
explanation: Urban desolation leaves luxury palaces and fortified watchtowers abandoned forever, becoming playground dens for wild donkeys and pastures for sheep. Isaiah 32:14 (KJV) - "Because the palaces shall be forsaken; the multitude of the city shall be left; the forts and towers shall be for dens for ever, a joy of wild asses, a pasture of flocks;"

question: Until what supernatural divine event will this desolation persist before the wilderness becomes a fertile orchard in Isaiah 32:15?
opt1: Until the seventy years of captivity in Babylon be accomplished by the decree of Cyrus
opt2: Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest
opt3: Until the high priest shall offer the red heifer and sprinkle the ashes upon the sanctuary
opt4: Until the sun shall return ten degrees upon the dial and King Hezekiah recover his strength
correct: Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest
explanation: Spiritual and environmental restoration occurs only when the Holy Spirit is sovereignly poured out from heaven, transforming deserts into lush orchards. Isaiah 32:15 (KJV) - "Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be counted for a forest."

question: What famous formula describes the twin eternal fruits produced by genuine righteousness in Isaiah 32:17?
opt1: And the fruit of righteousness shall be joy; and the harvest of truth abundance and glory
opt2: And the path of righteousness shall be light; and the crown of holiness honor and victory
opt3: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever
opt4: And the reward of righteousness shall be life; and the inheritance of faith salvation forever
correct: And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever
explanation: True righteousness produces authentic shalom (peace), yielding perpetual inner tranquility ('quietness') and unshakable confidence ('assurance forever'). Isaiah 32:17 (KJV) - "And the work of righteousness shall be peace; and the effect of righteousness quietness and assurance for ever."

question: What three peaceful dwelling descriptions portray the secure lifestyle of God's redeemed people in Isaiah 32:18?
opt1: In high fortresses of granite, in walled cities of safety, and in guarded palaces of gold
opt2: In fertile valleys of wine, in green pastures of plenty, and beside still waters of comfort
opt3: In pavilions of royal cedar, in tents of holiness, and beneath the shadow of the temple
opt4: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places
correct: And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places
explanation: Reversing wartime anxiety, God settles His people in peaceable homes, secure dwellings, and undisturbed resting places. Isaiah 32:18 (KJV) - "And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places;"

question: What blessed agrarian practice describes the generous, unhindered sowing of seed beside all waters in Isaiah 32:20?
opt1: Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feet of the ox and the ass
opt2: Blessed are ye that gather the harvest in joy, that tread the grapes in overflowing vats
opt3: Blessed are ye that build terraces upon the hills, that plant choice vines along the brooks
opt4: Blessed are ye that plow the fallow ground, that cast in principal wheat in the appointed place
correct: Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feet of the ox and the ass
explanation: Believers are commended for diligent, generous sowing across every well-watered soil, letting cattle and donkeys graze freely in peace. Isaiah 32:20 (KJV) - "Blessed are ye that sow beside all waters, that send forth thither the feet of the ox and the ass."

question: What law of divine retribution and boomerang judgment is pronounced against the ruthless imperial plunderer in Isaiah 33:1?
opt1: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee
opt2: Woe to the hammer of the earth, for thou shalt be broken in pieces; and woe to the golden city, for thou shalt be plundered!
opt3: Woe to the lion of the north that teareth the sheep; for the hunters shall surround thy den and cast thee into the pit!
opt4: Woe to them that build their fortresses with blood; for the stone shall cry out of the wall and the beam shall answer it!
correct: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee
explanation: The unprovoked predator (Assyria under Sennacherib) will experience strict lex talionis: once he finishes plundering, he will be plundered by others. Isaiah 33:1 (KJV) - "Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled; and dealest treacherously, and they dealt not treacherously with thee! when thou shalt cease to spoil, thou shalt be spoiled; and when thou shalt make an end to deal treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee."

question: What morning prayer of urgent dependence upon God is uttered by the besieged faithful in Isaiah 33:2?
opt1: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old
opt2: O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble
opt3: Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of thy name: and deliver us, and purge away our sins
opt4: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; shine forth before Ephraim and Manasseh
correct: O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble
explanation: The remnant pleads for daily morning strength and comprehensive deliverance in the hour of desperate crisis. Isaiah 33:2 (KJV) - "O LORD, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee: be thou their arm every morning, our salvation also in the time of trouble."

question: What three divine virtues provide the true anchor, stability, and treasure of God's people in Isaiah 33:6?
opt1: Gold, silver, and precious stones shall be the wealth of thy kings, and the strength of the sanctuary
opt2: Swords, shields, and iron chariots shall be the defense of thy borders, and the glory of the host
opt3: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure
opt4: Alliances with Egypt, treaties with Tyre, and walls of stone shall be the peace of Jerusalem
correct: And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure
explanation: National security is not rooted in material wealth or armaments, but in spiritual capital: divine wisdom, experiential knowledge, and the reverent fear of the LORD as its supreme treasure. Isaiah 33:6 (KJV) - "And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation: the fear of the LORD is his treasure."

question: What desperate diplomatic failure and treaty violation leaves Jerusalem's ambassadors weeping in the streets in Isaiah 33:7-8?
opt1: The envoys of Egypt were slain at the border, and their horses plundered by the Philistines
opt2: The tribute of thirty talents of gold was rejected by the emperor, and the royal messengers cast into prison
opt3: The scribes could not read the foreign script of the king of Assyria, and the heralds fled in panic
opt4: The ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man
correct: The ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man
explanation: Hezekiah's peace ambassadors weep bitterly because Sennacherib pocketed the massive silver/gold tribute yet treacherously broke the peace treaty and resumed his march on Jerusalem. Isaiah 33:7-8 (KJV) - "Behold, their valiant ones shall cry without: the ambassadors of peace shall weep bitterly. The highways lie waste, the wayfaring man ceaseth: he hath broken the covenant, he hath despised the cities, he regardeth no man."

question: What terrifying twin questions do hypocrites and sinners in Zion cry out before God's holy presence in Isaiah 33:14?
opt1: Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
opt2: Who can stand before the sword of the Assyrian? and who shall deliver us from his mighty host?
opt3: Where shall we hide from the fury of the storm? and who shall cover us in the day of wrath?
opt4: Can a man escape the plague of midnight? or shall any survive the famine of the siege?
correct: Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?
explanation: Terrified hypocrites realize that Yahweh's unapproachable, holy majesty is like a consuming fire that destroys all unrighteousness. Isaiah 33:14 (KJV) - "The sinners in Zion are afraid; fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites. Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire? who among us shall dwell with everlasting burnings?"

question: What sixfold moral integrity characterizes the righteous person qualified to dwell safely with God in Isaiah 33:15?
opt1: He that fasteth twice in the week, that payeth tithes of all he possesseth, that weareth broad phylacteries, that prayeth in the gates, that sacrificeth bulls, and that keepeth the sabbaths
opt2: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil
opt3: He that memorizeth the statutes of Moses, that defendeth the borders of Judah, that honoreth the high priest, that built the city wall, that giveth alms, and that cleanseth his hands with water
opt4: He that circumciseth his household, that eateth only clean meats, that offereth morning incense, that reciteth the psalms of David, that loveth his brethren, and that hateth the heathen
correct: He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil
explanation: Paralleling Psalm 15 and 24, the righteous life is defined by ethical conduct: upright walking, truthful speech, rejection of extortion, shaking hands clean of bribes, and shutting ears/eyes to violence and wickedness. Isaiah 33:15 (KJV) - "He that walketh righteously, and speaketh uprightly; he that despiseth the gain of oppressions, that shaketh his hands from holding of bribes, that stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood, and shutteth his eyes from seeing evil;"

question: What high fortress security and guaranteed physical sustenance are promised to the righteous in Isaiah 33:16?
opt1: He shall sit upon a throne of gold: his palace shall be fortified with bronze: wine shall be his drink, and meat his portion
opt2: He shall dwell in the temple courts: his shield shall be the angel of the covenant: manna shall fall for his house, and oil overflow
opt3: He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure
opt4: He shall inherit the holy mountain: his walls shall reach unto heaven: the rain of heaven shall water his crops, and cattle multiply
correct: He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure
explanation: The righteous enjoy impregnable rock fortress security where divine providence guarantees unceasing food and unfailing fresh water. Isaiah 33:16 (KJV) - "He shall dwell on high: his place of defence shall be the munitions of rocks: bread shall be given him; his waters shall be sure."

question: What glorious royal vision and expansive horizon are promised to the faithful in Isaiah 33:17?
opt1: Thine eyes shall behold the ark in its glory: they shall see the twelve tribes gathered in peace
opt2: Thine eyes shall see the temple rebuilt with cedar: they shall behold the riches of the Gentiles brought unto Zion
opt3: Thine eyes shall see the downfall of Assyria: they shall behold the armies of the heathen fleeing into the night
opt4: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off
correct: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off
explanation: Instead of terrified glimpses of foreign invaders, the redeemed will gaze upon the Messianic King in His radiant splendor and behold an unhindered, boundless kingdom. Isaiah 33:17 (KJV) - "Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off."

question: What threefold divine office reveals Yahweh as the supreme governmental authority and Saviour of His people in Isaiah 33:22?
opt1: For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us
opt2: For the LORD is our shepherd, the LORD is our rock, the LORD is our shield; he will defend us
opt3: For the LORD is our creator, the LORD is our redeemer, the LORD is our sanctifier; he will bless us
opt4: For the LORD is our light, the LORD is our fortress, the LORD is our strength; he will deliver us
correct: For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us
explanation: The three branches of government - judicial (Judge), legislative (Lawgiver), and executive (King) - are united in Yahweh, who brings total salvation. Isaiah 33:22 (KJV) - "For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us."

question: What miraculous physical healing and spiritual forgiveness crown the citizens of redeemed Zion in Isaiah 33:24?
opt1: And the mourner shall weep no more: the captives that return shall receive double portion of land
opt2: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity
opt3: And the lame shall leap like an hart: the blind shall see the glory of the temple
opt4: And death shall be swallowed up: the righteous shall shine as the stars of heaven
correct: And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity
explanation: Zion's inhabitants experience the complete integration of physical wholeness (no more sickness) and spiritual restoration (total expiation of sin). Isaiah 33:24 (KJV) - "And the inhabitant shall not say, I am sick: the people that dwell therein shall be forgiven their iniquity."

question: What cosmic de-creation of the heavenly bodies precedes the day of the LORD's vengeance in Isaiah 34:4?
opt1: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and notable day of the Lord come
opt2: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree
opt3: The stars shall fall from their orbits into the sea, and seven thunders shall utter their voices across the deep
opt4: The sky shall be covered with thick sackcloth of hair, and the pillars of heaven shall tremble with earthquake
correct: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree
explanation: The entire celestial host dissolves like withered grape leaves or overripe figs, and the skies roll shut like a scroll under cosmic judgment (Revelation 6:13-14). Isaiah 34:4 (KJV) - "And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree."

question: Upon what representative antagonistic nation does the sword of the LORD descend, bathed in heaven, in Isaiah 34:5-6?
opt1: Upon the princes of Philistia, and upon the inhabitants of the five royal cities of the coast
opt2: Upon the palaces of Damascus, and upon the high ramparts of the kings of Syria
opt3: For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment ... for the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea
opt4: Upon the towers of Babylon, and upon the astrologers that dwell by the river Euphrates
correct: For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment ... for the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea
explanation: God's sword falls upon Idumea (Edom), the ancestral enemy of Jacob, executing a sacrificial slaughter in its chief city Bozrah. Isaiah 34:5-6 (KJV) - "For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment. The sword of the LORD is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness ... for the LORD hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea."

question: What theological purpose justifies this day of international judgment in Isaiah 34:8?
opt1: For the iniquity of the Amorites is now full, and the land must be cleansed with fire
opt2: To avenge the seventy years of desolation, and rebuild the fallen tabernacle of David
opt3: That all the kingdoms of the earth may know that Yahweh alone is God over all flesh
opt4: For it is the day of the LORD's vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion
correct: For it is the day of the LORD's vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion
explanation: Divine judgment is legal vindication: the day of Yahweh's retribution to settle the legal dispute ('controversy of Zion') against those who oppressed His people. Isaiah 34:8 (KJV) - "For it is the day of the LORD's vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion."

question: Into what combustible volcanic substances will Edom's streams and dust be transformed in Isaiah 34:9-10?
opt1: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever
opt2: Her springs shall become bitter wormwood, and her rocks shall melt into rivers of molten bronze
opt3: Her soil shall be turned into salt, and her brooks shall dry up under the scorching east wind
opt4: Her valleys shall be filled with sulfur, and her mountains shall be consumed like thorns in a furnace
correct: And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever
explanation: Edom's ecology suffers Sodom-like perpetual incineration: waterways become boiling bitumen (pitch) and topsoil becomes sulfur (brimstone), smoking endlessly. Isaiah 34:9-10 (KJV) - "And the streams thereof shall be turned into pitch, and the dust thereof into brimstone, and the land thereof shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night nor day; the smoke thereof shall go up for ever: from generation to generation it shall lie waste; none shall pass through it for ever and ever."

question: What survey tools of de-creation and architectural emptiness does God stretch out over ruined Edom in Isaiah 34:11?
opt1: The measuring rod of wrath, and the plumbline of total destruction
opt2: He shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness
opt3: The iron chain of desolation, and the balance of divine fury
opt4: The reed of judgment, and the weights of perpetual silence
correct: He shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness
explanation: God reverses creation: stretching out a measuring line of tohu (confusion) and plumb-stones of bohu (emptiness), reducing society to primordial chaos. Isaiah 34:11 (KJV) - "But the cormorant and the bittern shall possess it; the owl also and the raven shall dwell in it: and he shall stretch out upon it the line of confusion, and the stones of emptiness."

question: What wilderness scavengers and eerie nocturnal creatures inherit Edom's ruined palaces in Isaiah 34:13-15?
opt1: Wolves shall lair in the royal bedchambers, and scorpions shall multiply upon the golden throne
opt2: Wild boars shall root up the gardens of the king, and ravens shall perch upon the broken battlements
opt3: Thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, and a court for owls. The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there ... there shall the great owl make her nest ... there shall the vultures also be gathered, every one with her mate
opt4: Desert jackals shall hunt in the courts, and vipers shall nest beneath the thresholds of the elders
correct: Thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, and a court for owls. The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there ... there shall the great owl make her nest ... there shall the vultures also be gathered, every one with her mate
explanation: Human civilization is replaced by wild animals, nocturnal birds, ostriches ('owls'), jackals ('dragons'), and desert satyrs nesting in thorn-choked palaces. Isaiah 34:13-15 (KJV) - "And thorns shall come up in her palaces, nettles and brambles in the fortresses thereof: and it shall be an habitation of dragons, and a court for owls. The wild beasts of the desert shall also meet with the wild beasts of the island, and the satyr shall cry to his fellow; the screech owl also shall rest there, and find for herself a place of rest. There shall the great owl make her nest, and lay, and hatch, and gather under her shadow: there shall the vultures also be gathered, every one with her mate."

question: What solemn scriptural verification command challenges future generations to confirm the literal accuracy of this prophecy in Isaiah 34:16?
opt1: Search the chronicles of the kings of Judah, and behold how every word hath been accomplished
opt2: Inquire of the elders of the gate, and verify that the sanctuary of Chemosh hath been cast down
opt3: Examine the monuments of the rocks of Sela, and see that no man inhabiteth the valley
opt4: Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them
correct: Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them
explanation: Readers are urged to cross-examine the written 'book of the LORD': every single creature listed will be found paired with its mate, exactly as God's mouth commanded. Isaiah 34:16 (KJV) - "Seek ye out of the book of the LORD, and read: no one of these shall fail, none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded, and his spirit it hath gathered them."

question: How does God legally apportion and deed Edom's ruined land to these wild creatures in Isaiah 34:17?
opt1: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein
opt2: He hath signed an eternal decree with his own finger, and sealed it with the royal signet of heaven
opt3: He hath driven out the seed of Esau, and given their inheritance unto the wild beasts of the south
opt4: He hath blotted out their boundaries from the map of the nations, and made it an eternal wilderness
correct: And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein
explanation: Just as Joshua cast lots and divided the Promised Land to the tribes of Israel, God sovereignly surveys and deeds Edom's ruins to wild beasts forever. Isaiah 34:17 (KJV) - "And he hath cast the lot for them, and his hand hath divided it unto them by line: they shall possess it for ever, from generation to generation shall they dwell therein."

question: What powerful wild beasts are poetically associated with Edom's aristocratic leaders in the sacrificial slaughter in Isaiah 34:7?
opt1: The mighty lions of the desert, and the leopards of the mountains of Seir
opt2: And the unicorns shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness
opt3: The fierce rams of Bashan, and the wild he-goats of the cliffs of En-gedi
opt4: The great eagles of the wilderness, and the stallions of the chariots of Bozrah
correct: And the unicorns shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness
explanation: Edom's haughty rulers are likened to wild oxen ('unicorns'), prime bullocks, and fierce bulls slaughtered in a massive divine sacrificial judgment. Isaiah 34:7 (KJV) - "And the unicorns shall come down with them, and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood, and their dust made fat with fatness."

question: What complete political extinction overtakes Edom's nobility and royal governance in Isaiah 34:12?
opt1: Her king shall be executed before the gate of Bozrah, and his crown melted in the fire
opt2: Her elders shall beg for bread among the nomads, and her counsellors shall be led away in chains
opt3: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there, and all her princes shall be nothing
opt4: Her governors shall be replaced by the captains of the host of Judah for seventy years
correct: They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there, and all her princes shall be nothing
explanation: Edom's aristocratic government vanishes completely; when citizens attempt to assemble nobles to proclaim a king, not a single leader exists. Isaiah 34:12 (KJV) - "They shall call the nobles thereof to the kingdom, but none shall be there, and all her princes shall be nothing."

question: What glorious botanical transformation rejoices and blossoms in the arid wilderness in Isaiah 35:1-2?
opt1: The barren rocks shall pour out streams of sweet wine, and the sands shall grow choice wheat
opt2: The terraces of the south shall yield pomegranates, and the fig trees shall blossom in winter
opt3: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose. It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon
opt4: The salt valleys of the Dead Sea shall flourish with olive groves, and cedars shall shade the hills
correct: The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose. It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon
explanation: Arid wastelands burst into exuberant floral bloom like a crocus/rose, endowed with the majestic forest splendor of Lebanon and the lush fertility of Carmel and Sharon. Isaiah 35:1-2 (KJV) - "The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose. It shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the excellency of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the LORD, and the excellency of our God."

question: What pastoral encouragement is given to strengthen the paralyzed and reassure fearful hearts in Isaiah 35:3-4?
opt1: Gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you
opt2: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father's good pleasure to give you the kingdom of peace
opt3: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God: speak ye comfortably to the heart of Jerusalem
opt4: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you
correct: Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you
explanation: Quoted in Hebrews 12:12, believers are exhorted to revive fainting hands and trembling knees with the certainty that God is coming in vindicating power to save them. Isaiah 35:3-4 (KJV) - "Strengthen ye the weak hands, and confirm the feeble knees. Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you."

question: What four miraculous physical healings herald the arrival of the Messianic age in Isaiah 35:5-6?
opt1: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing
opt2: The lepers shall be cleansed, the dead shall be raised to life, the sick shall be healed, and the sorrowful shall rejoice
opt3: The paralyzed shall walk, the withered hand shall be restored, the blind shall behold the light, and the deaf shall shout
opt4: The infirm shall receive new strength, the brokenhearted shall be comforted, the captive shall be loosed, and the mute shall speak
correct: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing
explanation: Jesus cited this exact passage to John the Baptist's disciples in Matthew 11:4-5 as absolute proof of His Messianic identity: blind see, deaf hear, lame leap, and mute sing. Isaiah 35:5-6 (KJV) - "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped. Then shall the lame man leap as an hart, and the tongue of the dumb sing: for in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert."

question: What hydrological transformation replaces the mirage and turns dragon dens into lush wetlands in Isaiah 35:7?
opt1: The scorching sands shall turn into rivers of milk, and the rocky caves into gardens of sweet balsam
opt2: And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of dragons, where each lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes
opt3: The dry cisterns shall overflow with rain, and the wild torrent beds shall run with fresh oil
opt4: The salt pits shall become sweet lakes, and the desert scrub shall be replaced by tall date palms
correct: And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of dragons, where each lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes
explanation: Deceptive desert mirages ('parched ground' / sharav) become authentic freshwater pools, and desolate jackal lairs are carpeted with aquatic reeds and papyrus. Isaiah 35:7 (KJV) - "And the parched ground shall become a pool, and the thirsty land springs of water: in the habitation of dragons, where each lay, shall be grass with reeds and rushes."

question: What holy arterial highway is constructed through the wilderness for the exclusive travel of the redeemed in Isaiah 35:8?
opt1: The royal road of the king; paved with polished stones; guarded by the captains of the temple
opt2: The path of the patriarchs; marked by twelve pillars of granite; reserved for the sons of Jacob
opt3: And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein
opt4: The avenue of triumph; illuminated by golden lamps; where no foreign captive may enter
correct: And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein
explanation: A divine, elevated causeway named 'The Way of Holiness' provides so plain and safe a route that even simple-minded pilgrims will never lose their way. Isaiah 35:8 (KJV) - "And an highway shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called The way of holiness; the unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those: the wayfaring men, though fools, shall not err therein."

question: What absolute immunity from predatory beasts is guaranteed along this holy highway in Isaiah 35:9?
opt1: The wild boars shall flee into the Jordan thickets, and the desert vipers shall lose their venom
opt2: The wolves shall be chained beside the way, and the leopards shall sleep upon the rocks
opt3: An angel with a flaming sword shall drive away every serpent and scorpion from the border
opt4: No lion shall be there, nor any ravenous beast shall go up thereon, it shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there
correct: No lion shall be there, nor any ravenous beast shall go up thereon, it shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there
explanation: Pilgrims enjoy total safety: no literal or spiritual predators (neither lion nor ravenous beast) can ever access the Way of Holiness. Isaiah 35:9 (KJV) - "No lion shall be there, nor any ravenous beast shall go up thereon, it shall not be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there:"

question: What exuberant celebration crowns the returning ransomed of the LORD as they arrive in Zion in Isaiah 35:10?
opt1: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away
opt2: They shall enter into the holy temple with shouts of triumph, and cast their crowns before the altar
opt3: They shall be clothed in robes of fine linen, and the tears of their exile shall be wiped away with gold
opt4: They shall sing the song of Moses and the Lamb, and their mourning shall be turned into an eternal dance
correct: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away
explanation: The ransomed pilgrims arrive on Mount Zion crowned with perpetual joy; sadness and groaning vanish forever into the past. Isaiah 35:10 (KJV) - "And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away."

question: In the structural symmetry of the Book of Isaiah, how does Chapter 35 function in relationship to Chapter 34?
opt1: Chapter 35 records the historical invasion of Sennacherib that fulfilled Chapter 34's prophecy
opt2: Chapter 35 provides the glorious, life-affirming contrast of redemption and Edenic renewal to Chapter 34's desolation and destruction of Edom
opt3: Chapter 35 lists the names of the exiles who returned from the captivity foretold in Chapter 34
opt4: Chapter 35 outlines the temple architectural blueprints required after the burning of Edom
correct: Chapter 35 provides the glorious, life-affirming contrast of redemption and Edenic renewal to Chapter 34's desolation and destruction of Edom
explanation: Isaiah 34 and 35 form a deliberate diptych: Chapter 34 depicts total de-creation and fiery ruin for God's enemies, while Chapter 35 reveals glorious re-creation, healing, and joy for God's people. Isaiah 35:1 (KJV) - "The wilderness and the solitary place shall be glad for them; and the desert shall rejoice, and blossom as the rose."

question: What spiritual reality is reflected in the phrase 'waters shall break out, and streams in the desert' in Isaiah 35:6?
opt1: The engineering of new aqueducts by King Hezekiah from the springs of Gihon
opt2: The melting of the glaciers of Mount Hermon replenishing the Jordan valley
opt3: The abundant, miraculous outpouring of the Holy Spirit and supernatural divine grace refreshing spiritually parched humanity
opt4: The discovery of subterranean wells by the nomadic herdsmen of the wilderness
correct: The abundant, miraculous outpouring of the Holy Spirit and supernatural divine grace refreshing spiritually parched humanity
explanation: Eschatological waters gushing in the desert symbolize the miraculous outpouring of divine life, the Spirit, and saving grace into arid human hearts. Isaiah 35:6 (KJV) - "For in the wilderness shall waters break out, and streams in the desert."

question: Who alone are permitted to travel upon the 'Way of Holiness' according to Isaiah 35:8-9?
opt1: The priests and Levites of the lineage of Zadok
opt2: The royal princes of the house of David
opt3: The merchants and diplomats of foreign nations
opt4: The redeemed and ransomed of the LORD
correct: The redeemed and ransomed of the LORD
explanation: The sacred highway is barred to moral uncleanness; it is exclusively reserved for the redeemed and ransomed people of God. Isaiah 35:8-9 (KJV) - "The unclean shall not pass over it; but it shall be for those ... but the redeemed shall walk there:"

question: In what pivotal fourteenth year of King Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria invade Judah in Isaiah 36:1?
opt1: In the tenth year of king Hezekiah, when Shalmaneser besieged the northern cities of Israel
opt2: In the twentieth year of king Hezekiah, when Sargon invaded the land of the Philistines
opt3: In the sixth year of king Hezekiah, when Samaria was captured and carried into exile
opt4: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them
correct: Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them
explanation: In 701 BC (Hezekiah's 14th year), Sennacherib swept through Judah, capturing 46 fortified cities before laying siege to Jerusalem. Isaiah 36:1 (KJV) - "Now it came to pass in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, that Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the defenced cities of Judah, and took them."

question: From what besieged Judahite fortress did Sennacherib dispatch the Rabshakeh with a great army to Jerusalem in Isaiah 36:2?
opt1: From Lachish
opt2: From Libnah
opt3: From Azekah
opt4: From Gath
correct: From Lachish
explanation: Sennacherib sent his chief royal spokesman (the Rabshakeh) from his siege headquarters at Lachish in the Shephelah to intimidate Jerusalem. Isaiah 36:2 (KJV) - "And the king of Assyria sent Rabshakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army. And he stood by the conduit of the upper pool in the highway of the fuller's field."

question: What three royal Judahite officials came out to negotiate with the Rabshakeh outside the walls in Isaiah 36:3?
opt1: Hilkiah the high priest, Shaphan the scribe, and Maaseiah the governor of the city
opt2: Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph's son, the recorder
opt3: Uriah the priest, Zechariah the son of Jeberechiah, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur
opt4: Seraiah the chief scribe, Baruch the son of Neriah, and Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
correct: Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph's son, the recorder
explanation: The diplomatic delegation comprised Eliakim (palace administrator), Shebna (now demoted to secretary/scribe), and Joah (court chronicler). Isaiah 36:3 (KJV) - "Then came forth unto him Eliakim, Hilkiah's son, which was over the house, and Shebna the scribe, and Joah, Asaph's son, the recorder."

question: To what treacherous, fragile plant does the Rabshakeh compare Egypt when warning Hezekiah against trusting her aid in Isaiah 36:6?
opt1: A dry thorn branch that snappeth in the storm and teareth the flesh of the traveler
opt2: A withered vine that cannot bear the weight of the cluster and roteth in the vineyard
opt3: Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him
opt4: A hollow cedar bough that breaketh under the foot of the climber upon the mountain
correct: Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him
explanation: The Rabshakeh astutely captures Egypt's unreliability: leaning on Pharaoh is like leaning on a cracked river reed that splinters and pierces the hand. Isaiah 36:6 (KJV) - "Lo, thou trustest in the staff of this broken reed, on Egypt; whereon if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all that trust in him."

question: How did the Rabshakeh cynically twist Hezekiah's religious centralization and removal of high places in Isaiah 36:7?
opt1: Did not Hezekiah melt the bronze serpent of Moses and desecrate the holy vessels of Solomon?
opt2: Hath not Hezekiah refused the daily morning sacrifices and closed the gates of the sanctuary?
opt3: Did not your king break down the pillars of Bethel and provoke the God of Jacob to anger?
opt4: Is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?
correct: Is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?
explanation: Misinterpreting Hezekiah's pious destruction of idolatrous high places, the Rabshakeh claimed Hezekiah had offended Yahweh by stripping away His rural altars. Isaiah 36:7 (KJV) - "But if thou say to me, We trust in the LORD our God: is it not he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and said to Judah and to Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar?"

question: What mocking military wager did the Rabshakeh propose to expose Judah's acute cavalry shortage in Isaiah 36:8?
opt1: I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them
opt2: I will give thee five hundred iron chariots, if thou canst find captains to drive them into battle
opt3: I will withdraw ten legions of footmen, if thou canst muster a single company of archers to face them
opt4: I will give thee ten thousand bronze shields, if thy warriors have the strength to lift them
correct: I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them
explanation: The Assyrian commander taunted Judah's military helplessness: Assyria would gift Hezekiah 2,000 horses if Judah could even find 2,000 trained riders to mount them. Isaiah 36:8 (KJV) - "Now therefore give pledges, I pray thee, to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give thee two thousand horses, if thou be able on thy part to set riders upon them."

question: What language did Hezekiah's officials plead with the Rabshakeh to speak to avoid demoralizing the citizens on the wall in Isaiah 36:11?
opt1: Speak in the tongue of the Chaldeans, which the scribes know, and not in the Hebrew speech of the people
opt2: Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews' language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall
opt3: Speak in the language of Egypt, for we are learned in it, and let not the common soldiers hear thy words
opt4: Speak in the Akkadian tongue of Nineveh, and send thy ambassadors into the palace to confer in secret
correct: Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews' language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall
explanation: Eliakim and Shebna requested Aramaic ('the Syrian language,' the international diplomatic lingua franca) rather than Judahite Hebrew ('the Jews' language') to prevent panic among the wall guards. Isaiah 36:11 (KJV) - "Then said Eliakim and Shebna and Joah unto Rabshakeh, Speak, I pray thee, unto thy servants in the Syrian language; for we understand it: and speak not to us in the Jews' language, in the ears of the people that are on the wall."

question: What crude, psychological warfare did the Rabshakeh shout to terrorize the soldiers garrisoned on Jerusalem's wall in Isaiah 36:12?
opt1: Hath not the king of Assyria commanded me to burn your houses with fire and sell your children for a pair of shoes?
opt2: Hear, ye starving watchmen on the ramparts: the siege shall not be lifted until your bones whiten the valleys!
opt3: Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?
opt4: Why will ye die by famine and thirst, while your king drinketh sweet wine in the inner chambers of the palace?
correct: Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?
explanation: The Rabshakeh deliberately aimed psychological terror at the common soldiers, warning that protracted siege would reduce them to consuming their own bodily excrement. Isaiah 36:12 (KJV) - "But Rabshakeh said, Hath my master sent me to thy master and to thee to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men that sit upon the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?"

question: What deceptive propaganda promise of agricultural paradise and deportation did the Rabshakeh offer to entice surrender in Isaiah 36:16-17?
opt1: Surrender your weapons and open the gates: and every man shall receive five talents of silver from the emperor's treasury
opt2: Pay homage to the great king: and ye shall dwell in your houses without tribute, and worship your God in peace
opt3: Deliver up King Hezekiah: and the king of Assyria will crown Eliakim, and make Judah a favored province of the empire
opt4: Make an agreement with me by a present, and come out to me: and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern; until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards
correct: Make an agreement with me by a present, and come out to me: and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern; until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards
explanation: The Rabshakeh painted a seductive, idealized picture of peaceful surrender and exile: immediate enjoyment of vines and cisterns, followed by deportation to an equally fertile land of corn and wine. Isaiah 36:16-17 (KJV) - "Hearken not to Hezekiah: for thus saith the king of Assyria, Make an agreement with me by a present, and come out to me: and eat ye every one of his vine, and every one of his fig tree, and drink ye every one the waters of his own cistern; Until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of corn and wine, a land of bread and vineyards."

question: What blasphemous theological challenge did the Rabshakeh issue against Yahweh, equating Him with the defeated local gods of foreign nations in Isaiah 36:18-20?
opt1: Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? Where are the gods of Hamath and Arphad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
opt2: Your God is powerless before the great gods Ashur and Ishtar who have given all kingdoms into the hand of Sennacherib!
opt3: Can the God of a single mountain withstand the emperor who hath conquered sixty nations and dried up the rivers of Egypt?
opt4: Behold the altars of Damascus and the ruins of Calno: did their sacrifices save them from the fury of our archers?
correct: Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? Where are the gods of Hamath and Arphad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?
explanation: The Rabshakeh overstepped into fatal blasphemy, demoting the Creator Yahweh to the level of defeated pagan idols (Hamath, Arphad, Sepharvaim, Samaria) and daring Him to intervene. Isaiah 36:18-20 (KJV) - "Beware lest Hezekiah persuade you, saying, The LORD will deliver us. Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? Where are the gods of Hamath and Arphad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim? and have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? Who are they among all the gods of these lands, that have delivered their land out of my hand, that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?"

question: What desperate obstetric proverb did King Hezekiah send through his sackcloth-clad delegation to Isaiah in Isaiah 37:3?
opt1: This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of blasphemy: for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth
opt2: We have labored in the night and brought forth only wind, and our strength is clean spent
opt3: The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved from the hand of the enemy
opt4: A woman in travail crieth out in her pain, but her child dieth before the rising of the sun
correct: This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of blasphemy: for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth
explanation: Hezekiah candidly confesses Judah's total human helplessness: the nation is like a mother in labor whose energy is exhausted at the moment of birth. Isaiah 37:3 (KJV) - "And they said unto him, Thus saith Hezekiah, This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of blasphemy: for the children are come to the birth, and there is not strength to bring forth."

question: What reassuring prophecy did Isaiah give Hezekiah concerning the fate of the blasphemous king of Assyria in Isaiah 37:6-7?
opt1: Gird on thy sword, for the host of Assyria shall be consumed by fire on the mount of Olives
opt2: Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard ... behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumour, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land
opt3: The armies of Egypt shall meet him at Libnah, and Sennacherib shall be bound in bronze chains
opt4: An earthquake shall swallow his siege engines, and the princes of Nineveh shall perish in the pit
correct: Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard ... behold, I will send a blast upon him, and he shall hear a rumour, and return to his own land; and I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land
explanation: God promises that Sennacherib will hear an unsettling rumor (Tirhakah's advance), withdraw to Nineveh, and ultimately be assassinated by the sword in his homeland. Isaiah 37:6-7 (KJV) - "Be not afraid of the words that thou hast heard, wherewith the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me.
