opt1: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: and they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses
opt2: I will send the early and the latter rain upon your terraces, and your sons shall grow like the cedars of Lebanon
opt3: I will open the windows of heaven with blessing, and your daughters shall be as the polished corners of the temple
opt4: I will refresh your vineyards with the dew of Mount Hermon, and your children shall multiply as the sand of the sea
correct: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: and they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses
explanation: Watering parched ground is equated with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, causing the rising generation to thrive luxuriantly like fast-growing willows on irrigation canals. Isaiah 44:3-4 (KJV) - "For I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground: I will pour my spirit upon thy seed, and my blessing upon thine offspring: And they shall spring up as among the grass, as willows by the water courses."

question: What voluntary inscriptions and personal identification demonstrate the joyful covenant dedication of the youth in Isaiah 44:5?
opt1: They shall wear golden phylacteries upon their foreheads and write the Ten Commandments on their doorposts
opt2: One shall say, I am the LORD's; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel
opt3: They shall take vows of the Nazarite and dedicate their firstborn sons to minister before the ark
opt4: They shall bring silver offerings to the temple and engrave their tribal genealogies upon bronze tablets
correct: One shall say, I am the LORD's; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel
explanation: Revitalized youth enthusiastically identify with Yahweh and His covenant people: verbally confessing, writing 'Belonging to Yahweh' on their hands, and proudly adopting the name Israel. Isaiah 44:5 (KJV) - "One shall say, I am the LORD's; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD, and surname himself by the name of Israel."

question: What supreme royal and redeemer titles are declared by the first and the last in Isaiah 44:6?
opt1: The Creator of heaven and earth, the Holy One of Jacob; I am the beginning and the end
opt2: The Shepherd of Israel, the Shield of Abraham; I am the Alpha and the Omega
opt3: The King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God
opt4: The Lord of all flesh, the Judge of nations; I am the everlasting Father
correct: The King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God
explanation: Yahweh Sabaoth unites sovereign kingship and personal redemption, asserting His eternal preeminence: 'I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.' Isaiah 44:6 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God."

question: What devastating satire exposes the absurdity of idol-making from a single tree trunk in Isaiah 44:14-17?
opt1: He buys costly cedar from Lebanon, carves an image, plates it with gold, and places it upon a throne of ivory
opt2: He consults astrologers to find an auspicious tree, cuts it under the full moon, and pours libations before it
opt3: He hires foreign artisans to shape an image with bronze tools, and sets up guards to prevent thieves from stealing it
opt4: With part of the wood he warms himself and bakes bread; with part he roasts meat and is satisfied; and with the residue thereof he maketh a god, falleth down unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god!
correct: With part of the wood he warms himself and bakes bread; with part he roasts meat and is satisfied; and with the residue thereof he maketh a god, falleth down unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god!
explanation: Isaiah brilliantly mocks pagan idiocy: a man cuts a tree, uses half of it as firewood for cooking and baking bread, and carves the leftover scrap into an 'almighty god,' bowing down and begging it to save him! Isaiah 44:16-17 (KJV) - "He burneth part thereof in fire; with part thereof he eateth flesh; he roasteth roast, and is satisfied: yea, he warmeth himself, and saith, Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire: And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god."

question: What psychological blindness and self-delusion traps the idolater so that he cannot rescue his own soul in Isaiah 44:20?
opt1: He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?
opt2: He drinketh the cup of poison: his eyes are blinded by the god of this world, that he cannot discern the light
opt3: He sleepeth in darkness: a spirit of slumber hath overtaken him, that he cannot hear the voice of the prophet
opt4: He pursueth after vanity: the riches of Egypt have ensnared him, that he cannot confess his folly
correct: He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?
explanation: The idolater feeds on worthless ashes; a self-deluded heart blinds him from recognizing the obvious fraud: 'Is there not a lie in my right hand?' Isaiah 44:20 (KJV) - "He feedeth on ashes: a deceived heart hath turned him aside, that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, Is there not a lie in my right hand?"

question: What atmospheric metaphor portrays the total dispersion and dissolution of Israel's sins in Isaiah 44:22?
opt1: Thy sins are washed away like the morning dew beneath the rising sun
opt2: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee
opt3: Thy transgressions are dissolved like smoke scattered by the south wind
opt4: Thy guilt is buried in the depths of the sea, and shall never rise again
correct: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee
explanation: Just as blazing sunlight and dry winds completely vaporize dark, threatening storm clouds into clear blue skies, God completely obliterates Israel's sins. Isaiah 44:22 (KJV) - "I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee."

question: What cosmic hymn summons all creation to burst into song over Israel's redemption in Isaiah 44:23?
opt1: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein: let the floods clap their hands
opt2: Praise ye the LORD from the heavens: praise him in the heights; praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, sun and moon
opt3: Sing, O ye heavens; for the LORD hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for the LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel
opt4: O clap your hands, all ye people; shout unto God with the voice of triumph: for the LORD most high is terrible
correct: Sing, O ye heavens; for the LORD hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for the LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel
explanation: The entire cosmos - heavens, earth's subterranean depths, towering mountains, and forests - is called to erupt in celebration over God redeeming Jacob and manifesting His glory. Isaiah 44:23 (KJV) - "Sing, O ye heavens; for the LORD hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for the LORD hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Israel."

question: What historical Persian emperor is explicitly prophesied by name a century and a half in advance as God's shepherd in Isaiah 44:28?
opt1: That saith of Darius the Mede, He is my servant, and shall open the gates of Babylon to my exiles
opt2: That saith of Artaxerxes the Persian, He is my friend, and shall decree the restoration of the walls of Zion
opt3: That saith of Alexander the Great, He is my battle-axe, and shall tread down the idols of the Chaldeans
opt4: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid
correct: That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid
explanation: In one of the most astonishing predictive prophecies in all literature, God names Cyrus 150 years before his birth, commissioning him as His shepherd to order the rebuilding of Jerusalem and the temple. Isaiah 44:28 (KJV) - "That saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure: even saying to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be built; and to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid."

question: What divine action confounds pagan astrologers and prognosticators while fulfilling the prophetic word of His servants in Isaiah 44:25-26?
opt1: That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish; that confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers
opt2: That striketh the magicians of Babylon blind, and burneth their astrological charts with unquenchable fire
opt3: That scattereth the false prophets like chaff, and drowneth the soothsayers in the river Euphrates
opt4: That closeth the mouths of the Chaldean enchanters, and overthroweth their temples in a single night
correct: That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish; that confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers
explanation: Yahweh drives pagan soothsayers and court diviners mad by falsifying their omens, while faithfully executing every single prediction uttered by His true prophetic messengers. Isaiah 44:25-26 (KJV) - "That frustrateth the tokens of the liars, and maketh diviners mad; that turneth wise men backward, and maketh their knowledge foolish; That confirmeth the word of his servant, and performeth the counsel of his messengers; that saith to Jerusalem, Thou shalt be inhabited; and to the cities of Judah, Ye shall be built, and I will raise up the decayed places thereof:"

question: What startling title does God bestow upon the pagan Persian monarch Cyrus in Isaiah 45:1?
opt1: Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut
opt2: Thus saith the Lord to my chosen servant Cyrus, whom I have raised up from the east to break the scepter of Babylon
opt3: Thus saith the Lord to my friend Cyrus, whom I have crowned with gold to execute my vengeance upon the heathen
opt4: Thus saith the Lord to my righteous captain Cyrus, whose sword shall shatter the bronze ramparts of the Chaldeans
correct: Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut
explanation: Astonishingly, God calls the Gentile ruler Cyrus His 'anointed' (Mashiach / Messiah), designating him as a divinely commissioned agent to conquer nations and liberate His people. Isaiah 45:1 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him; and I will loose the loins of kings, to open before him the two leaved gates; and the gates shall not be shut;"

question: Why did God supernaturally guide, empower, and name Cyrus decades before he was born according to Isaiah 45:4?
opt1: Because of the righteousness of Cyrus and his faithful observance of the laws of heaven
opt2: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me
opt3: To prove that the Persian empire was superior in wisdom to all the kingdoms of the Chaldeans
opt4: Because Cyrus offered sacrifices of bullocks and rams unto the God of Abraham in the wilderness
correct: For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me
explanation: Cyrus was chosen and named in advance strictly for the sake of covenant Israel ('for Jacob my servant's sake'), even though Cyrus did not personally know Yahweh. Isaiah 45:4 (KJV) - "For Jacob my servant's sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me."

question: What absolute, uncompromising statement of cosmic sovereignty refutes Persian dualism (light vs. darkness) in Isaiah 45:7?
opt1: I have set the sun to rule by day, and the moon by night, and no foreign god hath power over my works
opt2: I am the Lord of light, and my holy angels have triumphed over the dragon of darkness and confusion
opt3: I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things
opt4: I divide the light from the darkness, and the day of peace from the night of sorrow and judgment
correct: I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things
explanation: Directly countering Persian Zoroastrian dualism (which posited rival gods of light and darkness), Yahweh asserts total monotheistic sovereignty over all light, darkness, shalom (well-being), and calamity ('evil' / calamity). Isaiah 45:7 (KJV) - "I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the LORD do all these things."

question: What ceramic rebuke denounces human creatures who dare challenge their Creator's sovereign purposes in Isaiah 45:9?
opt1: Woe unto the vessel that questioneth the potter, for it shall be broken into pieces upon the floor!
opt2: Can the earthen pot boast against the wheel? or the clay refuse the design of the artisan?
opt3: Who art thou, O man, that repliest against God? shall the thing formed say, Why hast thou made me thus?
opt4: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?
correct: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?
explanation: It is absurd for a frail clay potsherd to contend with its sovereign Creator, insolently questioning His craftsmanship or competence (Romans 9:20-21). Isaiah 45:9 (KJV) - "Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker! Let the potsherd strive with the potsherds of the earth. Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? or thy work, He hath no hands?"

question: What unselfish, non-mercenary liberation will Cyrus grant to the exiled captives in Isaiah 45:13?
opt1: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts
opt2: He shall demand an hundred talents of silver for each tribe, but the treasury of the Lord shall provide it
opt3: He shall exchange the exiles of Judah for the captives of Babylon whom his captains took in battle
opt4: He shall release only the priests and the Levites, while the craftsmen remain in the service of Persia
correct: I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts
explanation: Cyrus released the Jewish exiles and commanded the rebuilding of Jerusalem entirely without demanding ransom, bribe, or financial reward ('not for price nor reward'). Isaiah 45:13 (KJV) - "I have raised him up in righteousness, and I will direct all his ways: he shall build my city, and he shall let go my captives, not for price nor reward, saith the LORD of hosts."

question: What confession of humble awe acknowledges God's mysterious, transcendent ways in Isaiah 45:15?
opt1: Truly thy ways are higher than our ways, and thy thoughts than our thoughts, O Lord
opt2: Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour
opt3: Behold, no man hath seen God at any time; he dwelleth in unapproachable light
opt4: O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments
correct: Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour
explanation: The prophet marvels that God often operates through hidden, surprising historical providences (such as using a pagan Persian king): 'Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.' Isaiah 45:15 (KJV) - "Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour."

question: What teleological purpose guided God's creation of the planet Earth in Isaiah 45:18?
opt1: He formed it to be a footstool for his throne, and a sanctuary where his holy angels may minister
opt2: He created it to display his power unto all generations, and to be an eternal habitation for the righteous
opt3: God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else
opt4: He made it as a proving ground for the sons of Adam, that they may choose between life and death
correct: God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else
explanation: God did not create the earth to be a chaotic void (tohu), but purposefully engineered and established it to be teeming with human life ('formed it to be inhabited'). Isaiah 45:18 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD that created the heavens; God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else."

question: What universal, global gospel invitation offers salvation to every human being on earth in Isaiah 45:22?
opt1: Turn ye unto me with all your heart, all ye nations, and ye shall inherit eternal life
opt2: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest
opt3: Hear the word of the Lord, ye Gentiles of the sea, and wash your hands in innocency
opt4: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else
correct: Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else
explanation: A monumental universal invitation: simply looking in faith to Yahweh brings instantaneous salvation to every soul across the globe, for He alone is God (the verse that converted C.H. Spurgeon). Isaiah 45:22 (KJV) - "Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else."

question: What solemn divine oath guarantees that every knee will bow and every tongue confess before God in Isaiah 45:23?
opt1: I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear
opt2: As I live, saith the Lord, all flesh shall bow before my throne, and every nation shall worship in my holy mountain
opt3: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but this decree shall stand: that all kings shall kiss the Son and submit to his law
opt4: By my great name have I sworn, that all idols shall perish, and every mouth shall confess that the Lord reigneth
correct: I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear
explanation: Quoted in Romans 14:11 and Philippians 2:10-11 concerning Christ, God swears by Himself that every knee in the universe will ultimately bend and every tongue confess His absolute supremacy. Isaiah 45:23 (KJV) - "I have sworn by myself, the word is gone out of my mouth in righteousness, and shall not return, That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear."

question: In whom alone do believers find genuine justification and spiritual strength in Isaiah 45:24-25?
opt1: In the keeping of the commandments of Moses and the offering of holy sacrifices
opt2: Surely, shall one say, in the LORD have I righteousness and strength ... In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory
opt3: In the ancestral covenant of Abraham and the bloodline of the house of David
opt4: In the repentance of our souls and the rebuilding of the temple of Jerusalem
correct: Surely, shall one say, in the LORD have I righteousness and strength ... In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory
explanation: Salvation is purely forensic and relational: true righteousness, spiritual power, and justification are found exclusively 'in the LORD' (foreshadowing Pauline 'in Christ'). Isaiah 45:24-25 (KJV) - "Surely, shall one say, in the LORD have I righteousness and strength: even to him shall men come; and all that are incensed against him shall be ashamed. In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory."

question: What two premier patron deities of Babylon collapse, strapped as heavy burdens onto exhausted pack animals, in Isaiah 46:1-2?
opt1: Marduk is fallen, Ishtar is broken, their golden statues are plundered by the Medes
opt2: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: your carriages were heavy loaden; they are a burden to the weary beast
opt3: Dagon is shattered, Chemosh is captive, their images are cast into the river Euphrates
opt4: Baal is confounded, Molech is destroyed, their priests are put to the sword before the altar
correct: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: your carriages were heavy loaden; they are a burden to the weary beast
explanation: Babylon's chief gods Bel (Marduk) and Nebo (god of wisdom/writing) are utterly helpless; their heavy statues must be hauled away as deadweight on exhausted donkeys and cattle. Isaiah 46:1-2 (KJV) - "Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle: your carriages were heavy loaden; they are a burden to the weary beast. They stoop, they bow down together; they could not deliver the burden, but themselves are gone into captivity."

question: What profound contrast exists between manufactured idols that must be carried and the true God who carries His people in Isaiah 46:3-4?
opt1: The gods of the heathen are carried upon the shoulders of men, but the angels of heaven bear up the children of Zion
opt2: The idols of silver stumble in the dust, but the Lord of hosts rideth upon the wings of the wind to defend Jacob
opt3: Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob ... which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you
opt4: Men must protect their manufactured images with locks and bars, but the Holy One of Israel is a wall of fire
correct: Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob ... which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you
explanation: Pagan worshippers must physically haul their inert idols; in breathtaking contrast, Yahweh created His people and carries them from birth, through life, and all the way to old age ('hoar hairs')! Isaiah 46:3-4 (KJV) - "Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb: And even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you."

question: What complete immobility and helplessness characterizes the manufactured golden idol in Isaiah 46:7?
opt1: He cannot open his eyes to see the distress of his worshippers, nor move his lips to pronounce a blessing
opt2: He hath hands, but he handleth not; feet hath he, but he walketh not: neither speaketh he through his throat
opt3: His priests must carry him from temple to temple, and his diviners must invent dreams to deceive the people
opt4: They bear him upon the shoulder, they carry him, and set him in his place, and he standeth; from his place shall he not remove: yea, one shall cry unto him, yet can he not answer, nor save him out of his trouble
correct: They bear him upon the shoulder, they carry him, and set him in his place, and he standeth; from his place shall he not remove: yea, one shall cry unto him, yet can he not answer, nor save him out of his trouble
explanation: A manufactured idol is totally paralyzed: once placed in a corner, it cannot take a single step; when cried unto, it is utterly incapable of answering or delivering. Isaiah 46:7 (KJV) - "They bear him upon the shoulder, they carry him, and set him in his place, and he standeth; from his place shall he not remove: yea, one shall cry unto him, yet can he not answer, nor save him out of his trouble."

question: What absolute proof of deity does God declare in Isaiah 46:9-10, demonstrating His sovereign control over history?
opt1: I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure
opt2: I am the Lord, and my wonders are known among all generations: I divide the seas and level the mountains
opt3: I am the Holy One, who brought forth light out of darkness, and whose throne is established upon righteousness
opt4: I am the Almighty, who weigheth the mountains in scales, and before whom the nations are as a drop of a bucket
correct: I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure
explanation: God's unmatched deity is proven by His ability to declare future history from the very beginning ('declaring the end from the beginning') and sovereignly fulfill His eternal counsel. Isaiah 46:9-10 (KJV) - "Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:"

question: What raptor metaphor describes the swift conqueror (Cyrus) summoned from the east to execute God's counsel in Isaiah 46:11?
opt1: Calling a roaring lion from the wilderness, the champion that breaketh the scepter of Babylon
opt2: Calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man that executeth my counsel from a far country: yea, I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it
opt3: Calling a mighty eagle from the mountain peaks, the prince that crusheth the gates of brass
opt4: Calling a swift leopard from the north, the king that devoureth the palaces of the Chaldeans
correct: Calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man that executeth my counsel from a far country: yea, I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it
explanation: Cyrus is pictured as a swift, predatory bird of prey ('ravenous bird' / ayit, eagle/falcon) swooping down rapidly from Persia to accomplish God's sovereign purpose. Isaiah 46:11 (KJV) - "Calling a ravenous bird from the east, the man that executeth my counsel from a far country: yea, I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it."

question: To whom is God's near salvation addressed, promising it will not tarry, in Isaiah 46:12-13?
opt1: Hearken unto me, ye faithful priests, who minister at the altar: I will restore your sacrifices in peace
opt2: Hearken unto me, ye princes of Judah, who weep by the rivers of Babylon: your captivity is ended
opt3: Hearken unto me, ye stouthearted, that are far from righteousness: I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry: and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory
opt4: Hearken unto me, ye humble and meek, who tremble at my word: I will give you crowns of righteousness
correct: Hearken unto me, ye stouthearted, that are far from righteousness: I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry: and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory
explanation: God addresses stubborn, rebellious exiles ('stouthearted, that are far from righteousness'), graciously offering imminent righteousness and salvation in Zion. Isaiah 46:12-13 (KJV) - "Hearken unto me, ye stouthearted, that are far from righteousness: I bring near my righteousness; it shall not be far off, and my salvation shall not tarry: and I will place salvation in Zion for Israel my glory."

question: What historical event fulfilled the humbling of Bel and Nebo described in Isaiah 46:1?
opt1: The plundering of the temple of Marduk by Sennacherib king of Assyria
opt2: The burning of the city of Nineveh by the allied armies of the Medes and Scythians
opt3: The destruction of the walls of Babylon by the Roman general Pompey
opt4: The peaceful capture of Babylon by Cyrus the Great in 539 BC, exposing the complete failure of the Babylonian pantheon
correct: The peaceful capture of Babylon by Cyrus the Great in 539 BC, exposing the complete failure of the Babylonian pantheon
explanation: When Cyrus captured Babylon in 539 BC, the imperial idols that supposedly protected the empire were demonstrated to be useless deadweight. Isaiah 46:1-2 (KJV) - "Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth, their idols were upon the beasts, and upon the cattle ... they could not deliver the burden, but themselves are gone into captivity."

question: What contrast is highlighted between the lavish gold spent on idols and their actual delivering power in Isaiah 46:6-7?
opt1: Men lavish gold out of the bag and hire a goldsmith to make a god, yet the costly manufactured object cannot answer prayer or save from trouble
opt2: The gold of the idols is purer than the vessels of Solomon, yet the high priest rejected it
opt3: The kings of the Chaldeans covered their gods with onyx, yet the fire melted them into slag
opt4: A man pays an hundred talents of silver for an image, yet a thief can steal it in the night
correct: Men lavish gold out of the bag and hire a goldsmith to make a god, yet the costly manufactured object cannot answer prayer or save from trouble
explanation: Huge financial expense (lavishing gold and hiring goldsmiths) cannot impart life: a million-dollar idol remains an impotent, deaf, mute statue. Isaiah 46:6-7 (KJV) - "They lavish gold out of the bag, and weigh silver in the balance, and hire a goldsmith; and he maketh it a god: they fall down, yea, they worship. They bear him upon the shoulder ... yet can he not answer, nor save him out of his trouble."

question: What mental command urges apostates to regain their rationality and recall God's historic wonders in Isaiah 46:8?
opt1: Awake, awake, and put on your strength, O ye foolish generation
opt2: Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors
opt3: Consider your ways, and ponder the path of your feet, ye backsliders
opt4: Stand in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way
correct: Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors
explanation: God urges idolaters to stop acting like irrational children and exercise mature masculine discernment ('shew yourselves men'): bring truth back to mind! Isaiah 46:8 (KJV) - "Remember this, and shew yourselves men: bring it again to mind, O ye transgressors."

question: What is the ultimate divine guarantee that God's plans will succeed according to Isaiah 46:11?
opt1: For my covenant with David cannot be broken, neither can the sun fail to shine
opt2: Because the angels of heaven stand ready to execute my decrees upon the earth
opt3: I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it
opt4: For I have sworn by the blood of the covenant that Israel shall possess the gate of her enemies
correct: I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it
explanation: Divine execution is absolute: whatever God speaks He brings to pass; whatever He sovereignly purposes He inevitably performs. Isaiah 46:11 (KJV) - "Yea, I have spoken it, I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed it, I will also do it."

question: What humiliating demotion from royal luxury to menial slave labor is ordered for the virgin daughter of Babylon in Isaiah 47:1-2?
opt1: Put off thy purple mantle, O queen of the Euphrates, and wear rags of mourning: wander barefoot in the desert
opt2: Cast away thy golden crown, O mistress of kingdoms, and dig the clay of the brick kilns like a bondmaid
opt3: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate. Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers
opt4: Strip off thy jewels, O city of astrologers, and carry water from the canals for the horses of the Medes
correct: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate. Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers
explanation: Babylon personified is dethroned from opulent delicacy and forced into the grueling, degrading labor of a female captive slave: sitting in dirt, grinding grain at millstones, and wading bare-legged through rivers into exile. Isaiah 47:1-2 (KJV) - "Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate. Take the millstones, and grind meal: uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh, pass over the rivers."

question: What pitiless cruelty did Babylon inflict upon aged Judahite exiles, exceeding God's disciplinary mandate, in Isaiah 47:6?
opt1: Thou didst slaughter the sucklings in the streets and cast the bodies of the prophets into the river
opt2: Thou didst burn the ancient manuscripts of the law and desecrate the holy vessels of Solomon
opt3: Thou didst force the priests of Levi to bow before the golden image in the plain of Dura
opt4: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke
correct: I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke
explanation: Although God used Babylon to discipline Judah, Babylon acted with ruthless sadism, showing zero mercy and imposing crushing forced-labor yokes even upon frail, elderly captives. Isaiah 47:6 (KJV) - "I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy; upon the ancient hast thou very heavily laid thy yoke."

question: What arrogant blasphemy of divine self-sufficiency did Babylon utter in her heart in Isaiah 47:8?
opt1: I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children
opt2: My high walls reach unto heaven, and my empire shall endure throughout all generations
opt3: The gods of the Chaldeans have given all nations into my hand, and none can deliver from my power
opt4: I have built the greatest city on the earth, and all kings shall bring their wealth unto my gates
correct: I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children
explanation: Babylon usurped God's exclusive self-declaration ('I am, and none else beside me'), boasting of invulnerability against national bereavement ('widowhood' / loss of citizens). Isaiah 47:8 (KJV) - "Therefore hear now this, thou that art given to pleasures, that dwellest carelessly, that sayest in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me; I shall not sit as a widow, neither shall I know the loss of children:"

question: What twin catastrophic tragedies strike Babylon simultaneously in a single day in Isaiah 47:9?
opt1: The sword and the famine; they shall devour thy young men and leave thy granaries desolate
opt2: These two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments
opt3: The fire and the earthquake; they shall level thy high towers and burn thy palaces with brimstone
opt4: The pestilence and the flood; they shall sweep away thy armies and drown thy merchant galleys
correct: These two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments
explanation: In a single night (539 BC), Babylon suffered total bereavement: losing her sovereign king/empire ('widowhood') and her citizens/nobles ('loss of children') despite all occult protections. Isaiah 47:9 (KJV) - "But these two things shall come to thee in a moment in one day, the loss of children, and widowhood: they shall come upon thee in their perfection for the multitude of thy sorceries, and for the great abundance of thine enchantments."

question: What fatal intellectual and occult pride perverted Babylon into self-deception in Isaiah 47:10?
opt1: Thy wealth of silver and gold hath blinded thee, and thou hast trusted in the horses of the desert
opt2: Thy military captains have deceived thee, and thou hast believed that thy ramparts were impenetrable
opt3: Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me
opt4: Thy foreign alliances have betrayed thee, and thou hast made a covenant with the princes of the sea
correct: Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me
explanation: Babylon's renowned astronomical and magical sciences perverted her moral judgment, convincing her that she was sovereign, unseen ('none seeth me'), and absolute. Isaiah 47:10 (KJV) - "For thou hast trusted in thy wickedness: thou hast said, None seeth me. Thy wisdom and thy knowledge, it hath perverted thee; and thou hast said in thine heart, I am, and none else beside me."

question: What occult practitioners and monthly prognosticators are challenged to stand up and rescue Babylon from divine ruin in Isaiah 47:13?
opt1: Let the priests of Bel, the readers of liver omens, and the casters of holy lots deliver thy city
opt2: Let the enchanters of Egypt, the sorcerers of Syria, and the diviners of the Philistines arise
opt3: Let the necromancers that peep and mutter, and the interpreters of midnight dreams plead for thee
opt4: Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee
correct: Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee
explanation: God mocks Babylon's elite occult establishment: astrologers, zodiac stargazers, and horoscope prognosticators are powerless to avert the catastrophe. Isaiah 47:13 (KJV) - "Thou art wearied in the multitude of thy counsels. Let now the astrologers, the stargazers, the monthly prognosticators, stand up, and save thee from these things that shall come upon thee."

question: To what flammable agricultural refuse are Babylon's astrologers and sorcerers compared as they burn up in Isaiah 47:14?
opt1: Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it
opt2: As dry chaff swept into the furnace of the potter, leaving only ashes behind
opt3: As withered thorns consumed in the forest, vanishing in a great cloud of smoke
opt4: As broken reeds cast into the kiln of the brickmaker, quenched without water
correct: Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it
explanation: The famed astrologers are mere dry stubble, instantly incinerated by divine judgment, unable even to save their own lives; the blaze is not a cozy hearth coal, but total destruction. Isaiah 47:14 (KJV) - "Behold, they shall be as stubble; the fire shall burn them; they shall not deliver themselves from the power of the flame: there shall not be a coal to warm at, nor fire to sit before it."

question: What complete abandonment by foreign commercial trading partners leaves Babylon utterly alone in Isaiah 47:15?
opt1: They shall sail their ships back to Tarshish and refuse to buy the merchandise of Chaldea
opt2: They shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee
opt3: They shall plunder the royal storehouses and divide the golden vessels among themselves
opt4: They shall join the armies of the Medes and rejoice over the ruins of the palace
correct: They shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee
explanation: Her lifelong commercial associates and mercenary merchants flee in self-preservation, scattering to their homelands and leaving Babylon to perish alone. Isaiah 47:15 (KJV) - "Thus shall they be unto thee with whom thou hast laboured, even thy merchants, from thy youth: they shall wander every one to his quarter; none shall save thee."

question: What title of imperial supremacy is permanently stripped away from Babylon in Isaiah 47:5?
opt1: The golden city of the east
opt2: The queen of the great waters
opt3: The lady of kingdoms
opt4: The hammer of the whole earth
correct: The lady of kingdoms
explanation: Babylon is told to sit silent in darkness, forever losing her proud imperial title: 'the lady of kingdoms' (Gevereth Mamlachoth). Isaiah 47:5 (KJV) - "Sit thou silent, and get thee into darkness, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called, The lady of kingdoms."

question: How unsparing is God's judicial retribution against Babylon according to Isaiah 47:3?
opt1: I will execute wrath with ten thousand angels, and none shall escape
opt2: I will smite thy princes with an iron scepter, and spare neither old nor young
opt3: I will remember the burning of Jerusalem, and reward thee double for thy cruelty
opt4: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man
correct: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man
explanation: God will execute vengeance with supernatural, unyielding omnipotence, refusing to be swayed or negotiated with like a human warrior: 'I will not meet thee as a man.' Isaiah 47:3 (KJV) - "Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man."

question: What hypocritical religious pretense characterizes the house of Jacob in the opening indictment of Isaiah 48:1-2?
opt1: Which offer unblemished sacrifices in the morning, but worship the host of heaven upon their housetops in the night
opt2: Which wear broad phylacteries in the streets, but rob the fatherless and take usury from the poor of the land
opt3: Which fast twice in the week, but pervert justice in the gate and reject the words of the seers
opt4: Which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness. For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; The LORD of hosts is his name
correct: Which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness. For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; The LORD of hosts is his name
explanation: Judah boasts of her orthodox theology and Jerusalem citizenship ('the holy city'), invoking Yahweh's name verbally while living in complete practical falsehood and unrighteousness. Isaiah 48:1-2 (KJV) - "Hear ye this, O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah, which swear by the name of the LORD, and make mention of the God of Israel, but not in truth, nor in righteousness. For they call themselves of the holy city, and stay themselves upon the God of Israel; The LORD of hosts is his name."

question: What metallurgical metaphors depict Israel's stubborn, unyielding obstinacy and insolence in Isaiah 48:4?
opt1: Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass
opt2: Thy heart is as hard as the nether millstone, and thy ears are stopped with lead
opt3: Thy skull is as cut granite, and thy tongue like a sharp two-edged sword of bronze
opt4: Thy conscience is seared with a hot iron, and thy knees refuse to bow before the altar
correct: Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass
explanation: God diagnosed Israel's chronic rebellion: a stiff neck like an unbreakable iron tendon and a brazen forehead incapable of blushing in shame. Isaiah 48:4 (KJV) - "Because I knew that thou art obstinate, and thy neck is an iron sinew, and thy brow brass;"

question: Why did God announce prophecies centuries before they occurred, preventing Israel from crediting her idols in Isaiah 48:5?
opt1: That the kings of the Gentiles might tremble before the wisdom of the house of David
opt2: I have even from the beginning declared it to thee; before it came to pass I shewed it thee: lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them
opt3: That the scribes might record the decrees in the royal archives of the temple of Solomon
opt4: That the false prophets of Baal might be put to death according to the statutes of Moses
correct: I have even from the beginning declared it to thee; before it came to pass I shewed it thee: lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them
explanation: God preempted idolaters: by predicting history long beforehand, He made it impossible for apostate Israelites to claim their wooden and metal statues engineered the events. Isaiah 48:5 (KJV) - "I have even from the beginning declared it to thee; before it came to pass I shewed it thee: lest thou shouldest say, Mine idol hath done them, and my graven image, and my molten image, hath commanded them."

question: In what refining crucible did God purify Israel, restraining His wrath to prevent total annihilation in Isaiah 48:9-10?
opt1: In the desert of Sinai for forty years of wandering, until the rebellious generation was consumed
opt2: In the waters of the Jordan, until the uncircumcised hearts of the people were circumcised
opt3: For my name's sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off. Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction
opt4: In the temple of Jerusalem with holy fire, until all the dross of their idolatry was purged
correct: For my name's sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off. Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction
explanation: God refined Israel not with the intense, destructive heat required for silver (which would have incinerated her completely), but tempered His discipline in 'the furnace of affliction' (Babylonian exile) for His name's sake. Isaiah 48:9-10 (KJV) - "For my name's sake will I defer mine anger, and for my praise will I refrain for thee, that I cut thee not off. Behold, I have refined thee, but not with silver; I have chosen thee in the furnace of affliction."

question: What supreme motive drives God's salvation and prevents His glory from being shared in Isaiah 48:11?
opt1: Because of the righteousness of Abraham and the faithful prayers of King David
opt2: Lest the heathen boast that their gods have triumphed over the ark of the covenant
opt3: To fulfill the oaths sworn unto the patriarchs before the foundation of the world
opt4: For mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will I do it: for how should my name be polluted? and I will not give my glory unto another
correct: For mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will I do it: for how should my name be polluted? and I will not give my glory unto another
explanation: God's ultimate passion is the defense of His own glory: twice repeating 'for mine own sake,' He refuses to let His holy name be defamed among pagan nations. Isaiah 48:11 (KJV) - "For mine own sake, even for mine own sake, will I do it: for how should my name be polluted? and I will not give my glory unto another."

question: What profound Trinitarian commissioning is spoken by the mysterious Divine Speaker in Isaiah 48:16?
opt1: Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me
opt2: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings
opt3: Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him
opt4: Thus saith the Lord unto his anointed, whose right hand I have holden, to subdue nations before him
correct: Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me
explanation: In an extraordinary Old Testament revelation of the Trinity, the pre-incarnate Messiah declares His eternal preexistence ('there am I') and His sending by the sovereign Father ('the Lord GOD') and the Holy Spirit ('his Spirit'). Isaiah 48:16 (KJV) - "Come ye near unto me, hear ye this; I have not spoken in secret from the beginning; from the time that it was, there am I: and now the Lord GOD, and his Spirit, hath sent me."

question: What pastoral divine self-description portrays God as the supreme Guide and Teacher of profitable living in Isaiah 48:17?
opt1: I am the Holy One of Israel which commandeth thy footsteps, and correcteth thee with the rod of truth
opt2: I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go
opt3: I am the Lord of hosts which fighteth thy battles, and delivereth thy soul from the hand of the enemy
opt4: I am the Shepherd of Jacob which feedeth thy flock, and leadeth thee beside the still waters of comfort
correct: I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go
explanation: Yahweh acts as the loving Mentor and Guide, instructing His people in truly profitable living and directing their steps in the optimal moral path. Isaiah 48:17 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the LORD thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go."

question: What tragic lamentation expresses what Israel would have experienced had she obeyed God's commandments in Isaiah 48:18-19?
opt1: If thou hadst kept my statutes, thou wouldest have reigned over all the kingdoms of the Gentiles
opt2: Hadst thou walked in my ways, the king of Babylon would never have burned the holy temple with fire
opt3: O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea: thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me
opt4: If ye had hearkened unto the voice of the prophets, the glory of Lebanon would have covered your hills
correct: O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea: thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me
explanation: God weeps over lost potential: obedience would have produced unbroken, flowing peace like a majestic river and boundless righteousness rolling like ocean waves. Isaiah 48:18-19 (KJV) - "O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea: Thy seed also had been as the sand, and the offspring of thy bowels like the gravel thereof; his name should not have been cut off nor destroyed from before me."

question: What joyful exodus command summons the redeemed exiles to flee Babylon and proclaim their salvation globally in Isaiah 48:20?
opt1: Arise and depart, for this is not your rest: return unto Mount Zion with songs of everlasting joy
opt2: Gather your silver and gold, ye captives of Judah, and march through the wilderness with the ark of the covenant
opt3: Blow the trumpet in the streets of the golden city, and shout aloud that the scepter of the oppressor is broken
opt4: Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth; say ye, The LORD hath redeemed his servant Jacob
correct: Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth; say ye, The LORD hath redeemed his servant Jacob
explanation: The exiles are commanded to make a swift, singing departure from Babylon, broadcasting the news of Yahweh's redemption of Jacob to the ends of the earth. Isaiah 48:20 (KJV) - "Go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans, with a voice of singing declare ye, tell this, utter it even to the end of the earth; say ye, The LORD hath redeemed his servant Jacob."

question: What famous somber recurring refrain concludes the first major division of the Book of Comfort (Chapters 40-48) in Isaiah 48:22?
opt1: There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked
opt2: For the soul that sinneth, it shall die, saith the Lord GOD
opt3: The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God
opt4: Behold, the triumphing of the wicked is short, and the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment
correct: There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked
explanation: Marking the end of the first of three 9-chapter cycles in Isaiah 40-66, God issues the solemn, immutable verdict: 'There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked.' Isaiah 48:22 (KJV) - "There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked."

question: What military weapon metaphors describe the Servant's speech and hidden preparation in God's hand in Isaiah 49:2?
opt1: He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me
opt2: He hath made my tongue like a bronze bow, and my lips like arrows of fire dipped in venom
opt3: He hath made my voice like a battering ram, and my words like a heavy iron hammer
opt4: He hath made my speech like a two-edged spear, and concealed my soul in the secret place of the tabernacle
correct: He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me
explanation: The Messiah's word is an incisive, penetrating weapon ('sharp sword') and an expertly honed, lethal arrow ('polished shaft') kept concealed in God's sovereign quiver until the appointed time. Isaiah 49:2 (KJV) - "And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me;"

question: What expansive global mission transcends the restoration of Israel, commissioning the Servant as a light to all Gentile nations in Isaiah 49:6?
opt1: Thou shalt conquer the kingdoms of the west, and enforce the law of Moses upon the islands of the sea
opt2: It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth
opt3: Thou shalt restore the twelve thrones of David in Jerusalem, and all heathen kings shall bring silver tribute
opt4: Thou shalt gather the lost sheep of Ephraim, and make an eternal covenant with the princes of the south
correct: It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth
explanation: Quoted by Paul in Acts 13:47, God declares that merely recovering ethnic Israel is too small a task for His Servant: He is appointed as the cosmic Light of the Gentiles, bringing salvation to the ends of the earth. Isaiah 49:6 (KJV) - "And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth."

question: What radical geopolitical reversal occurs when once-despising foreign monarchs behold the Servant in Isaiah 49:7?
opt1: Kings shall surrender their swords of iron, and princes shall flee into the mountain caves
opt2: Monarchs shall send fifty talents of gold, and governors shall offer burnt sacrifices at the altar
opt3: Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the LORD that is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, and he shall choose thee
opt4: Emperors shall plead for mercy before his feet, and their captains shall be bound in chains
correct: Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the LORD that is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, and he shall choose thee
explanation: Though initially abhorred and despised by men, the Servant will be recognized by sovereign kings who stand in reverence and prostrate themselves in worship. Isaiah 49:7 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, the Redeemer of Israel, and his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of the LORD that is faithful, and the Holy One of Israel, and he shall choose thee."

question: From what distant, mysterious land does a company of redeemed exiles gather in Isaiah 49:12?
opt1: The land of Tarshish
opt2: The land of Sheba
opt3: The land of Ophir
opt4: The land of Sinim
correct: The land of Sinim
explanation: Alongside north and west, pilgrims arrive from 'the land of Sinim' (traditionally identified with southern Egypt/Aswan / Syene, or the far eastern realms of China). Isaiah 49:12 (KJV) - "Behold, these shall come from far: and, lo, these from the north and from the west; and these from the land of Sinim."

question: What maternal love comparison proves God's impossible-to-forget devotion to Zion in Isaiah 49:15?
opt1: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee
opt2: Can a father disown his firstborn son, that he should cast him out into the wilderness?
opt3: Can a shepherd abandon his wounded lamb, that he should leave it to be devoured by wolves?
opt4: Can a mother forsake her nursing daughter, and refuse to give her milk in the day of sorrow?
correct: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee
explanation: Human maternal instinct is fierce, yet even if an earthly mother could abandon her nursing infant, Yahweh's compassionate memory of Zion is utterly indelible. Isaiah 49:15 (KJV) - "Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee."

question: What permanent inscription guarantees that Zion is constantly before God's eyes in Isaiah 49:16?
opt1: I have written thy name upon the golden breastplate of the high priest forever
opt2: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me
opt3: I have engraved thy memory upon the tablets of the covenant within the holy of holies
opt4: I have set thee as a signet ring upon my right hand, and sealed thee with my holy Spirit
correct: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me
explanation: God has indelibly tattooed or engraved Zion's name onto the palms of His hands, keeping her ruined walls continually before His attentive gaze. Isaiah 49:16 (KJV) - "Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me."

question: What sudden demographic explosion astounds previously childless, bereaved Zion in Isaiah 49:19-21?
opt1: Thy daughters shall outnumber the sand of the sea, and thy sons shall build twelve cities in the desert
opt2: The exiles shall return in ten thousand chariots of gold, and Jerusalem shall have no room for their flocks
opt3: The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell. Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro?
opt4: The Gentiles shall bring their sons to be circumcised, and Zion shall wonder at the riches of the heathen
correct: The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell. Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro?
explanation: Zion is astonished by an immense influx of spiritual children born during her bereavement, crowding the land so densely that they plead for room to expand. Isaiah 49:20-21 (KJV) - "The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other, shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me: give place to me that I may dwell. Then shalt thou say in thine heart, Who hath begotten me these, seeing I have lost my children, and am desolate, a captive, and removing to and fro? and who hath brought up these? Behold, I was left alone; these, where had they been?"

question: How will Gentile kings and queens minister to the returning children of Zion in Isaiah 49:22-23?
opt1: They shall pave the highway to Jerusalem with silver, and build royal palaces for the princes of Judah
opt2: They shall offer their crowns upon the altar of the temple, and serve as porters in the gates of the sanctuary
opt3: They shall provide five thousand chariots of cedar, and bring fine linen from the markets of Alexandria
opt4: They shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet
correct: They shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet
explanation: Gentile emperors and queens become foster parents and nursing attendants, tenderly carrying Israel's children and prostrating in humble homage at Zion's feet. Isaiah 49:22-23 (KJV) - "They shall bring thy sons in their arms, and thy daughters shall be carried upon their shoulders. And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me."

question: What divine intervention liberates captives from the seemingly invincible clutches of a tyrant in Isaiah 49:24-25?
opt1: Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children
opt2: The armies of the Medes shall break the gates of brass and loose the chains of the prisoners with the sword
opt3: An earthquake shall shatter the foundations of the prison house, and the captives shall walk forth in peace
opt4: The king of Babylon shall surrender his captives for forty talents of silver, and weep before the elders
correct: Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children
explanation: God directly battles the imperial oppressor: answering the skeptical question with sovereign authority, He wrests the prey from the tyrant and saves Zion's children. Isaiah 49:24-25 (KJV) - "Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? But thus saith the LORD, Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away, and the prey of the terrible shall be delivered: for I will contend with him that contendeth with thee, and I will save thy children."

question: What self-destructive cannibalistic judgment destroys Zion's oppressors, demonstrating God's Saviourhood to all flesh in Isaiah 49:26?
opt1: I will cast them into the burning lake of brimstone, and their memorial shall be blotted out under heaven
opt2: I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob
opt3: I will send a plague of biting serpents among their encampments, and their bones shall whiten the desert
opt4: I will cause their captains to fall upon their own swords in the night, and their horses shall drown in the sea
correct: I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob
explanation: Oppressive regimes collapse into fratricidal, cannibalistic civil warfare, proving globally that Yahweh is Israel's Saviour and the Mighty One of Jacob. Isaiah 49:26 (KJV) - "And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I the LORD am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob."

question: What legal metaphors of divorce and debt slavery refute the notion that God arbitrarily abandoned Israel in Isaiah 50:1?
opt1: Have I broken my holy covenant with Abraham? or have I forgotten the oath which I sware unto Isaac?
opt2: Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away
opt3: Did not your fathers choose the gods of Egypt, and sell their inheritance for a pair of bronze sandals?
opt4: Is the Lord bankrupt that he must borrow silver from the heathen, and surrender his children to strangers?
correct: Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away
explanation: God never issued a legal certificate of divorce terminating His marriage to Israel, nor was He forced by debt to pawn His children; Israel's own iniquities caused her exile. Isaiah 50:1 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement, whom I have put away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iniquities have ye sold yourselves, and for your transgressions is your mother put away."

question: What daily morning discipleship endowed the Servant with the ability to speak words of comfort to the weary in Isaiah 50:4?
opt1: He hath studied the scrolls of Moses from his youth, and memorized the wisdom of the ancient fathers
opt2: The Spirit of the Lord rested upon him in the wilderness, and taught him the secrets of the sanctuary
opt3: The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned
opt4: He consulted the seventy elders of the gate at dawn, and received understanding from the high priest
correct: The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned
explanation: The Third Servant Song reveals the Messiah's daily morning communion with the Father: an awakened, attentive ear receiving seasoned words of life for exhausted souls. Isaiah 50:4 (KJV) - "The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned, that I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary: he wakeneth morning by morning, he wakeneth mine ear to hear as the learned."

question: What bodily suffering, physical brutality, and public humiliation did the Servant willingly endure without resistance in Isaiah 50:5-6?
opt1: I surrendered my hands to the iron fetters, and my feet to the stocks of the prison house
opt2: I offered my neck to the bronze sword of the executioner, and my garments to the plunderers
opt3: I walked barefoot through the streets of Jerusalem, and drank the bitter gall of affliction
opt4: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting
correct: I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting
explanation: Prefiguring Christ's trial and scourging, the Servant submits voluntarily: back to scourging whips, cheeks to beard-plucking, and face to humiliating spit. Isaiah 50:5-6 (KJV) - "The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back. I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting."

question: What geological metaphor expresses the Servant's unshakeable, resolute determination in the face of suffering in Isaiah 50:7?
opt1: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed
opt2: I have made my brow like bronze, and my chest like a wall of cut granite
opt3: I have anchored my soul upon the rock of ages, and my heart shall never tremble
opt4: I have strengthened my knees like iron, and my spirit like the cedar of Lebanon
correct: For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed
explanation: Quoted in Luke 9:51 as Jesus set His face to go to Jerusalem, setting His face 'like a flint' depicts unbending resolve grounded in the Father's vindication. Isaiah 50:7 (KJV) - "For the Lord GOD will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed."

question: What courtroom confidence allows the Servant to boldly challenge any prosecutor or adversary to condemn Him in Isaiah 50:8-9?
opt1: My righteousness is recorded in the books of heaven; who can bring an accusation against the anointed of God?
opt2: He is near that justifieth me; who will contend with me? let us stand together: who is mine adversary? let him come near to me. Behold, the Lord GOD will help me; who is he that shall condemn me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up
opt3: The angels of the host defend my cause; let the kings of the earth bring forth their legal witnesses
opt4: The law of the Lord is my shield; who shall lay anything to the charge of God's elect before the altar?
correct: He is near that justifieth me; who will contend with me? let us stand together: who is mine adversary? let him come near to me. Behold, the Lord GOD will help me; who is he that shall condemn me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up
explanation: Quoted by Paul in Romans 8:33-34, the Servant stands with absolute judicial confidence because God Himself justifies Him; all human accusers will rot like moth-eaten garments. Isaiah 50:8-9 (KJV) - "He is near that justifieth me; who will contend with me? let us stand together: who is mine adversary? let him come near to me. Behold, the Lord GOD will help me; who is he that shall condemn me? lo, they all shall wax old as a garment; the moth shall eat them up."

question: What pastoral direction is given to the faithful believer who walks in circumstantial darkness without seeing light in Isaiah 50:10?
opt1: Let him light a torch of resin and run swiftly through the valley of the shadow of death
opt2: Let him fast forty days in sackcloth and plead for the appearance of the morning star
opt3: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God
opt4: Let him consult the Urim and Thummim before the high priest in the sanctuary
correct: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God
explanation: When faithful obedience leads through perplexing darkness devoid of light, the believer must not manufacture artificial light, but simply trust Yahweh's name and lean ('stay upon') his God. Isaiah 50:10 (KJV) - "Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God."

question: What tragic fate awaits self-reliant rebels who attempt to illuminate their own way by kindling artificial sparks in Isaiah 50:11?
opt1: Your fire shall be quenched in a moment, and ye shall wander into outer darkness forever
opt2: The sparks of your pride shall burn your garments, and your flesh shall be consumed with brimstone
opt3: A sudden tempest from heaven shall scatter your coals, and the cold of the night shall slay you
opt4: Walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparks that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow
correct: Walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparks that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow
explanation: Those who reject God's guidance to walk in the deceptive glow of their own human-engineered fires and sparks will suffer divine judgment: lying down in perpetual sorrow. Isaiah 50:11 (KJV) - "Behold, all ye that kindle a fire, that compass yourselves about with sparks: walk in the light of your fire, and in the sparks that ye have kindled. This shall ye have of mine hand; ye shall lie down in sorrow."

question: What cosmic power over seas and celestial bodies does God cite to prove His hand is not shortened in Isaiah 50:2-3?
opt1: Behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering
opt2: I cause the mountains to melt like wax, and the foundations of the earth to shake with earthquake
opt3: I summon the lightning to strike the towers of the kings, and withhold the rain from the fields
opt4: I command the sun to stand still in the sky, and lead the stars by their appointed numbers
correct: Behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering
explanation: God proves His absolute ability to save: His rebuke dried the Red Sea, desiccated rivers, and cloaked the cosmic heavens in mourning sackcloth. Isaiah 50:2-3 (KJV) - "Is my hand shortened at all, that it cannot redeem? or have I no power to deliver? behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea, I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stinketh, because there is no water, and dieth for thirst. I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering."

question: What is the structural significance of the Third Servant Song in Isaiah 50:4-9?
opt1: It outlines the architectural blueprints for rebuilding the temple walls destroyed by Babylon
opt2: It reveals the Servant's intimate personal obedience and voluntary submission to suffering, bridging the Servant's commissioning in Chapter 49 to His vicarious atoning death in Chapter 53
opt3: It records the historical accession of King Cyrus and his conquest of the Persian empire
opt4: It pronounces the final judgment against the seven pagan nations of the Mediterranean coast
correct: It reveals the Servant's intimate personal obedience and voluntary submission to suffering, bridging the Servant's commissioning in Chapter 49 to His vicarious atoning death in Chapter 53
explanation: The Third Servant Song moves deeper into the psychology of Messiah: showing His spotless obedience, His daily communion, and His steadfast endurance of physical brutality for our redemption.
