Isaiah 50:4-9 (KJV) - "The Lord GOD hath given me the tongue of the learned ... I gave my back to the smiters ... therefore have I set my face like a flint:"

question: What does the phrase 'the Lord GOD hath opened mine ear' signify in Isaiah 50:5?
opt1: The physical healing of natural deafness by a miraculous touch from heaven
opt2: The ability to hear the secret songs of the seraphim around the throne of glory
opt3: A willing, submissive posture of total obedience to divine revelation, echoing the pierced ear of the devoted bondservant in Exodus 21:6
opt4: The legal right of the firstborn to inherit the prophetic mantle of Elijah
correct: A willing, submissive posture of total obedience to divine revelation, echoing the pierced ear of the devoted bondservant in Exodus 21:6
explanation: An 'opened ear' denotes receptive, unreserved willingness to obey God's will whatever the cost, refusing to shrink back from suffering. Isaiah 50:5 (KJV) - "The Lord GOD hath opened mine ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned away back."

question: To what ancestral quarry and solitary patriarch are believers directed to look for encouragement in Isaiah 51:1-2?
opt1: Look unto the mountain of Moriah where the ram was caught in the thicket by its horns
opt2: Look unto King David who was taken from the sheepfolds to reign over all Israel
opt3: Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him
opt4: Look unto Moses who was drawn from the waters of the Nile to deliver the people
correct: Look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him
explanation: Discouraged exiles are told to remember their historical roots: God took a single, childless elderly man (Abraham) and his barren wife (Sarah) and multiplied them into a vast nation. Isaiah 51:1-2 (KJV) - "Hearken to me, ye that follow after righteousness, ye that seek the LORD: look unto the rock whence ye are hewn, and to the hole of the pit whence ye are digged. Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him."

question: What Edenic transformation will God perform upon Zion's ruined waste places in Isaiah 51:3?
opt1: He will rebuild her broken walls with cut cedar, and pave her courtyards with the gold of Ophir
opt2: He will plant choice vines of Sibmah upon her hills, and cause sweet wine to flow in her streets
opt3: He will open twelve freshwater springs from the threshold of the temple, and heal the salt sea
opt4: He will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody
correct: He will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody
explanation: God will restore Zion's scorched ruins into a lush paradise like the Garden of Eden, filled with overflowing joy, thanksgiving, and exuberant music. Isaiah 51:3 (KJV) - "For the LORD shall comfort Zion: he will comfort all her waste places; and he will make her wilderness like Eden, and her desert like the garden of the LORD; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the voice of melody."

question: What cosmic transience contrasts with the eternal permanence of God's salvation and righteousness in Isaiah 51:6?
opt1: The heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished
opt2: The stars shall fall like unripe figs, and the sea shall be turned into dry sand: but my mercy endureth
opt3: The mountains shall melt like wax, and the clouds shall roll together as a scroll: but my word abideth
opt4: The empires of the earth shall crumble into dust, and all crowns shall perish: but Zion shall stand
correct: The heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished
explanation: Though the physical universe dissolves like dissipating smoke and the earth rots like an old moth-eaten coat, God's salvation and righteousness remain forever indestructible. Isaiah 51:6 (KJV) - "Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath: for the heavens shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment, and they that dwell therein shall die in like manner: but my salvation shall be for ever, and my righteousness shall not be abolished."

question: What mythic and historical monsters did the arm of the LORD slay in ancient days at the Red Sea in Isaiah 51:9-10?
opt1: Art thou not it that shattered Leviathan in the wilderness, and broke the head of the serpent in the deep?
opt2: Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?
opt3: Art thou not it that drowned the chariots of Pharaoh, and slew the behemoth of the reed marshes?
opt4: Art thou not it that cleft the rock in Horeb, and cast down the winged lion of the Euphrates?
correct: Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?
explanation: Zion appeals to God's ancient Exodus power: smiting Rahab (poetic title for Egypt as a sea monster / dragon) and carving a dry highway through the depths for the ransomed. Isaiah 51:9-10 (KJV) - "Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD; awake, as in the ancient days, in the generations of old. Art thou not it that hath cut Rahab, and wounded the dragon? Art thou not it which hath dried the sea, the waters of the great deep; that hath made the depths of the sea a way for the ransomed to pass over?"

question: What joyous arrival song of the ransomed is repeated verbatim from Chapter 35 in Isaiah 51:11?
opt1: They shall enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him
opt2: Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God: we have waited for his salvation
opt3: Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away
opt4: The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord: let the earth rejoice and shout
correct: Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away
explanation: Reiterating Isaiah 35:10 verbatim, God promises that the ransomed will re-enter Zion with triumphant songs, crowned with everlasting joy, while grief vanishes. Isaiah 51:11 (KJV) - "Therefore the redeemed of the LORD shall return, and come with singing unto Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their head: they shall obtain gladness and joy; and sorrow and mourning shall flee away."

question: Why is trembling fear of mortal oppressors rebuked as foolish in Isaiah 51:12-13?
opt1: For the oppressor hath no power against the angels of God, and his bronze swords shall be broken
opt2: Because the king of Babylon shall perish in seventy years, and his empire shall be given to the Medes
opt3: Why tremblest thou at shadows, when the Holy One of Israel is a wall of fire around thy dwellings?
opt4: Who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass; and forgettest the LORD thy maker, that hath stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and hast feared continually every day because of the fury of the oppressor?
correct: Who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass; and forgettest the LORD thy maker, that hath stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and hast feared continually every day because of the fury of the oppressor?
explanation: Fearing mortal human tyrants who wither like grass is irrational when it causes one to forget the almighty Creator who stretched out the cosmos. Isaiah 51:12-13 (KJV) - "I, even I, am he that comforteth you: who art thou, that thou shouldest be afraid of a man that shall die, and of the son of man which shall be made as grass; And forgettest the LORD thy maker, that hath stretched forth the heavens, and laid the foundations of the earth; and hast feared continually every day because of the fury of the oppressor, as if he were ready to destroy? and where is the fury of the oppressor?"

question: What terrifying intoxicating goblet had Jerusalem drained to the bitter dregs in Isaiah 51:17?
opt1: The cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out
opt2: The vial of unquenchable wrath; thou hast swallowed the wine of astonishment
opt3: The bowl of ancient indignation; thou hast tasted the bitter gall of judgment
opt4: The golden flagon of idolatry; thou hast poured out libations unto foreign gods
correct: The cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out
explanation: Jerusalem had experienced full divine discipline: draining the goblet of God's wrath, drinking down the bitter sediment ('dregs') of staggering terror. Isaiah 51:17 (KJV) - "Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury; thou hast drunken the dregs of the cup of trembling, and wrung them out."

question: To what exhausted, captured animals are Jerusalem's fainting sons compared at the street corners in Isaiah 51:20?
opt1: As wounded sheep bleeding in the thicket of the mountain
opt2: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of thy God
opt3: As young lions trapped in the pit of the hunters
opt4: As fledglings cast out of the nest upon the rocky terraces
correct: Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of thy God
explanation: Jerusalem's starving young men lie helpless at every street intersection, exhausted and struggling like trapped antelopes ('wild bull' / te'o) ensnared in a hunter's net. Isaiah 51:20 (KJV) - "Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net: they are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of thy God."

question: Into whose hands does God transfer the terrifying cup of trembling in Isaiah 51:22-23?
opt1: Into the hands of the false prophets and priests who deceived my people with lies
opt2: Into the depths of the sea, where it shall be swallowed up forever
opt3: Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: but I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee
opt4: Unto the four winds of heaven, that it may consume all the kingdoms of the earth
correct: Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: but I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee
explanation: In an absolute reversal, God removes the cup of trembling from Jerusalem forever and forces her brutal oppressors (the Babylonians) to drink it to the dregs. Isaiah 51:22-23 (KJV) - "Thus saith thy Lord the LORD, and thy God that pleadeth the cause of his people, Behold, I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling, even the dregs of the cup of my fury; thou shalt no more drink it again: But I will put it into the hand of them that afflict thee;"

question: What degrading physical atrocity did foreign conquerors force conquered Jerusalem to endure in Isaiah 51:23?
opt1: They bound thy princes to the wheels of their chariots and dragged them through the dust
opt2: They forced thy daughters to dance before their idols and stripped them of their linen mantles
opt3: They branded thy elders with hot irons and sold thy youth for five pieces of silver
opt4: Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over
correct: Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over
explanation: Brutal imperial conquerors literally treated Jewish captives like pavement, ordering them to prostrate so soldiers could trample over their backs like street dust. Isaiah 51:23 (KJV) - "Which have said to thy soul, Bow down, that we may go over: and thou hast laid thy body as the ground, and as the street, to them that went over."

question: What royal garments and purified status is captive Zion commanded to put on in Isaiah 52:1?
opt1: Put on the armor of light, O daughter of David; gird on the sword of victory: for the oppressor is fallen
opt2: Put on thy linen robes, O sanctuary of peace; anoint thy head with sweet oil: for the exiles return
opt3: Clothe thyself with purple, O queen of the mountains; take up thy golden scepter: for the king reigneth
opt4: Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean
correct: Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean
explanation: Zion is summoned to awaken from depression, don her festive bridal/royal robes, and celebrate that foreign pagan invaders ('the uncircumcised and unclean') will never profane her again. Isaiah 52:1 (KJV) - "Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, the holy city: for henceforth there shall no more come into thee the uncircumcised and the unclean."

question: What paradoxical commercial transaction defines Israel's exile and divine redemption in Isaiah 52:3?
opt1: Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money
opt2: Ye were bought with thirty pieces of silver; and ye shall be redeemed with the gold of Ophir
opt3: Ye were traded for horses of Egypt; and ye shall be ransomed with the treasures of Tyre
opt4: Ye were mortgaged for your debts; and your redemption is paid by the blood of bulls
correct: Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money
explanation: Israel received no profit when her sins caused her exile ('sold for nought'), and God pays Babylon zero ransom money to liberate her - redemption is accomplished purely by sovereign power and grace. Isaiah 52:3 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD, Ye have sold yourselves for nought; and ye shall be redeemed without money."

question: What famous proclamation of gospel peace and divine reign celebrates the arrival of the herald upon the mountains in Isaiah 52:7?
opt1: How glorious upon the hills is the voice of the watchman, that bloweth the trumpet of freedom
opt2: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
opt3: Behold upon the mountains the standard of the King, that proclaimeth liberty throughout all the land
opt4: How lovely in the gates are the messengers of triumph, that shout aloud, The oppressor is broken!
correct: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!
explanation: Quoted in Romans 10:15, this classic gospel text celebrates the herald bounding over the mountains with the ultimate message of peace, good news, salvation, and the royal proclamation: 'Thy God reigneth!' Isaiah 52:7 (KJV) - "How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace; that bringeth good tidings of good, that publisheth salvation; that saith unto Zion, Thy God reigneth!"

question: What joyful harmony do Jerusalem's watchmen share when they see the LORD return to Zion in Isaiah 52:8?
opt1: They shall blow the silver trumpets from the pinnacle of the temple with shouting
opt2: They shall cast away their spears and embrace the messengers in the gates
opt3: Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion
opt4: They shall bow down in tears of thanksgiving and anoint their heads with oil
correct: Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion
explanation: The city sentinels sing together in unified harmony because they witness Yahweh's personal return to Zion clearly, intimately, and face to face ('see eye to eye'). Isaiah 52:8 (KJV) - "Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing: for they shall see eye to eye, when the LORD shall bring again Zion."

question: What warrior action reveals God's salvation to all the ends of the earth in Isaiah 52:10?
opt1: The Lord hath drawn his glittering sword before the princes of the earth
opt2: The Almighty hath sounded his thunder from the highest heaven
opt3: The King of kings hath ridden upon his chariot of fire through the sea
opt4: The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God
correct: The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God
explanation: Like an ancient warrior rolling back his sleeve for unhindered combat, Yahweh 'makes bare His holy arm' to execute visible, global salvation before all Gentile nations. Isaiah 52:10 (KJV) - "The LORD hath made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God."

question: What ceremonial purity and holy decorum must characterize the priests and exiles carrying temple vessels out of Babylon in Isaiah 52:11?
opt1: Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD
opt2: Wash your garments with water, sprinkle the blood of the covenant, and wear white linen
opt3: Flee in the night watches, hide the sacred vessels in sacks of haircloth, and avoid the caravan routes
opt4: Fast seven days before the departure, and carry the ark upon the shoulders of the Levites
correct: Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD
explanation: Quoted in 2 Corinthians 6:17, those carrying the sacred temple vessels out of idolatrous Babylon are commanded to maintain strict moral and ritual purity, touching no unclean thing. Isaiah 52:11 (KJV) - "Depart ye, depart ye, go ye out from thence, touch no unclean thing; go ye out of the midst of her; be ye clean, that bear the vessels of the LORD."

question: What divine vanguard and rear-guard escort guarantees that the return from Babylon will not be a panicked flight in Isaiah 52:12?
opt1: Twelve legions of angels shall surround the host, and a pillar of cloud shall cover the caravans
opt2: For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward
opt3: The cavalry of Cyrus shall guard your flanks, and the princes of the Medes shall provide wheat
opt4: You shall march with banners of triumph, and no enemy shall dare approach within forty furlongs
correct: For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward
explanation: Unlike the hurried midnight escape from Egypt, this exodus is orderly and peaceful because Yahweh leads the front (vanguard) and guards the back ('rereward' / rear-guard). Isaiah 52:12 (KJV) - "For ye shall not go out with haste, nor go by flight: for the LORD will go before you; and the God of Israel will be your rereward."

question: What supreme threefold exaltation opens the climactic Fourth Servant Song in Isaiah 52:13?
opt1: Behold, my chosen one shall conquer, he shall reign in righteousness, and possess the nations
opt2: Behold, the Branch of David shall arise, he shall build the temple, and bear the glory
opt3: Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high
opt4: Behold, my holy king shall triumph, he shall judge the earth, and sit on David's throne
correct: Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high
explanation: The Fourth Servant Song (Isaiah 52:13-53:12) opens with the Servant's wise success and ultimate cosmic elevation: 'exalted, extolled, and very high' (Philippians 2:9). Isaiah 52:13 (KJV) - "Behold, my servant shall deal prudently, he shall be exalted and extolled, and be very high."

question: What shocking physical disfigurement stunned observers beholding the Servant in Isaiah 52:14?
opt1: His body was covered with wounds of iron, and his brow pierced with sharp thorns
opt2: His eyes were dimmed with bitter tears, and his cheeks withered with fasting
opt3: His garments were stained with blood, and his hands bound with chains of bronze
opt4: As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men
correct: As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men
explanation: The Servant's brutalized appearance was so horrifically disfigured by torture and scourging that He barely resembled a human being, leaving onlookers paralyzed in shock. Isaiah 52:14 (KJV) - "As many were astonied at thee; his visage was so marred more than any man, and his form more than the sons of men:"

question: What priestly cleansing of Gentile nations and speechless awe of kings concludes Isaiah 52:15?
opt1: So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider
opt2: So shall he judge the heathen; the princes shall fall before him: for his scepter is righteous
opt3: So shall he conquer the kings; their crowns shall be cast into the dust: for the Lord hath spoken
opt4: So shall he gather the outcasts; the Gentiles shall bring silver: for Zion is redeemed
correct: So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider
explanation: Acting as the supreme High Priest, the suffering Servant 'sprinkles' (ceremonially purifies with atoning blood) multi-ethnic Gentile nations, reducing world emperors to stunned, reverent silence. Isaiah 52:15 (KJV) - "So shall he sprinkle many nations; the kings shall shut their mouths at him: for that which had not been told them shall they see; and that which they had not heard shall they consider."

question: What agricultural metaphors depict the obscure, fragile origins of the Servant in Isaiah 53:2?
opt1: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him
opt2: He shall arise like a cedar of Lebanon, and as a fruitful vine on the hills of Carmel
opt3: He shall bud like an olive tree by running streams, and blossom as a rose in Sharon
opt4: He shall spring up like an oak of Bashan, and as a willow by the water courses
correct: For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him
explanation: Messiah arises from humble, unpromising surroundings: like a vulnerable sapling ('tender plant') or a root struggling in arid soil, devoid of superficial royal glamour or physical ostentation. Isaiah 53:2 (KJV) - "For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him."

question: What sorrowful title and universal human rejection characterize the Servant in Isaiah 53:3?
opt1: He was mocked by the rulers and condemned by the elders; an outcast of his brethren
opt2: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not
opt3: He was betrayed by his friends and forsaken by his disciples; a stranger in his own house
opt4: He was accused by false witnesses and scourged before the heathen; a victim of violence
correct: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not
explanation: Christ is the prototypical 'Man of Sorrows,' intimately familiar with human heartbreak, universally ostracized, avoided as if repulsive, and written off as worthless by humanity. Isaiah 53:3 (KJV) - "He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not."

question: What tragic human misinterpretation viewed the suffering Servant as cursed by God rather than suffering vicariously in Isaiah 53:4?
opt1: We believed he suffered for his own blasphemy, and was condemned by the law of Moses
opt2: We thought he was punished for the sins of his fathers, and cast out from the holy sanctuary
opt3: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted
opt4: We judged him as a deceiver of the people, and worthy of the curse of the tree
correct: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted
explanation: Onlookers falsely assumed that God was justly punishing Him for His own crimes (like Job's friends), blind to the reality that He was bearing our sicknesses and carrying our griefs. Isaiah 53:4 (KJV) - "Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted."

question: What central, definitive declaration of penal substitutionary atonement establishes our healing in Isaiah 53:5?
opt1: He laid down his life as an example of love, that we might follow his footsteps in righteousness
opt2: He died as a martyr for the truth, that the covenant of Abraham might be confirmed unto the Gentiles
opt3: He bore the reproach of the heathen, that the glory of the temple might be restored forever
opt4: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed
correct: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed
explanation: The heart of the gospel: Christ was pierced for our rebellions and crushed for our moral iniquities; His judicial punishment purchased our shalom (peace), and His scourging wounds heal our souls (1 Peter 2:24). Isaiah 53:5 (KJV) - "But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed."

question: What pastoral confession of universal human depravity and divine imputation is articulated in Isaiah 53:6?
opt1: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all
opt2: We have all sinned and come short of the glory of God, and none doeth good, no, not one
opt3: We were born in iniquity and conceived in sin, but the blood of the Lamb hath cleansed our guilt
opt4: The whole head is sick and the whole heart faint, but the Lord hath redeemed his flock with his right hand
correct: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all
explanation: All humanity shares universal waywardness like scattered sheep, each pursuing selfish rebellion, yet Yahweh transferred and imputed ('laid on him') the collective guilt of us all onto Christ. Isaiah 53:6 (KJV) - "All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all."

question: To what sacrificial animals is the silent, uncomplaining submission of the Servant compared in Isaiah 53:7?
opt1: As an unblemished bullock led to the altar, so he yielded his life without crying
opt2: He is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth
opt3: As a turtledove offered for a sin offering, so his spirit departed in quiet peace
opt4: As an heifer bearing the yoke without turning, so he endured the cross with patience
correct: He is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth
explanation: Quoted by Philip to the Ethiopian eunuch in Acts 8:32-33, Jesus submitted to judicial murder with total silence and voluntary surrender, like a lamb led to slaughter or a sheep before shearers. Isaiah 53:7 (KJV) - "He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth."

question: What extraordinary burial paradox paired the innocent Servant with both criminals and the wealthy in Isaiah 53:9?
opt1: He was buried in the Potter's Field with strangers, though crowned with spices of the king
opt2: He was cast into the pit of the transgressors, but his body saw no corruption in the dust
opt3: And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth
opt4: He was laid in the royal sepulchre of David, though condemned as a malefactor by the council
correct: And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth
explanation: Foreshadowing Jesus crucified between two thieves ('with the wicked') yet buried in the private rock-tomb of wealthy Joseph of Arimathea ('with the rich in his death'), His absolute moral innocence is confirmed. Isaiah 53:9 (KJV) - "And he made his grave with the wicked, and with the rich in his death; because he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his mouth."

question: What sovereign divine pleasure ordained the Servant's death as a guilt offering (asham) in Isaiah 53:10?
opt1: It was the wrath of the Gentiles that slew him, but the Lord raised him up to reign forever
opt2: He surrendered himself to the hands of lawless men, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled
opt3: God permitted the dragon to bruise his heel, that the head of the serpent might be crushed
opt4: Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand
correct: Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand
explanation: Behind human executioners was Yahweh's sovereign redemptive pleasure: crushing Him as a substitutionary guilt offering ('asham'), followed by resurrection triumph ('prolong his days') and spiritual progeny ('see his seed'). Isaiah 53:10 (KJV) - "Yet it pleased the LORD to bruise him; he hath put him to grief: when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days, and the pleasure of the LORD shall prosper in his hand."

question: What divine satisfaction and forensic justification are achieved through the Servant's agonizing soul-travail in Isaiah 53:11?
opt1: He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities
opt2: He shall look upon the fruit of his labor with joy: by his blood shall he purchase an holy priesthood
opt3: He shall behold the redeemed of all nations: by his intercession shall he reconcile the world
opt4: He shall rejoice in the kingdom of peace: by his stripes shall he establish the covenant
correct: He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities
explanation: Looking beyond the agony of the cross, Christ is profoundly satisfied with the redemptive harvest: through experiential knowledge of Him, the Righteous Servant forensically justifies many by bearing their sins. Isaiah 53:11 (KJV) - "He shall see of the travail of his soul, and shall be satisfied: by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities."

question: What victorious royal reward and intercessory ministry crown the climax of the Fourth Servant Song in Isaiah 53:12?
opt1: He shall sit upon the throne of his father David, and reign over the house of Jacob forever
opt2: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors
opt3: All kings shall fall down before him, and all nations shall serve him in the holy mountain
opt4: He shall be crowned with glory and honor, and lead captivity captive into eternal light
correct: Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors
explanation: Because He poured out His soul unto death, was counted among outlaws (Luke 22:37), bore the sins of many, and interceded for His executioners (Luke 23:34), the Father crowns Him with cosmic victory and royal plunder. Isaiah 53:12 (KJV) - "Therefore will I divide him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he hath poured out his soul unto death: and he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors."

question: What triumphant celebration is commanded of formerly barren Zion following the Servant's sacrifice in Isaiah 54:1?
opt1: Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion; shout, O daughter of Jerusalem: behold, thy King cometh unto thee
opt2: Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD
opt3: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee in the wilderness
opt4: Put on thy beautiful garments, O Jerusalem, and celebrate with timbrel and harp before the altar
correct: Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD
explanation: Quoted in Galatians 4:27, barren Zion is commanded to sing exuberantly because through the Servant's atonement, her spiritual children far outnumber those of her former married state. Isaiah 54:1 (KJV) - "Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear; break forth into singing, and cry aloud, thou that didst not travail with child: for more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife, saith the LORD."

question: What nomadic architectural expansion is required to accommodate the vast influx of new spiritual children in Isaiah 54:2?
opt1: Build higher the stone walls of Jerusalem, and widen the iron gates of the citadel
opt2: Plant new terraces along the valleys, and dig cisterns for the returning multitude
opt3: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes
opt4: Pitch twelve royal pavilions on Mount Zion, and prepare tables of cedar for the feast
correct: Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes
explanation: Zion must radically expand her living quarters: widening tent curtains, lengthening guy-ropes, and driving heavier tent pegs to accommodate the massive international family. Isaiah 54:2 (KJV) - "Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes;"

question: What intimate conjugal and cosmic titles belong to Israel's divine Redeemer in Isaiah 54:5?
opt1: For thy King is thy shield; the Lord of glory is his name; and thy Shepherd the Rock of Ages
opt2: For thy Creator is thy father; the Almighty is his name; and thy Saviour the King of saints
opt3: For the Lord is thy fortress; Yahweh Sabaoth is his name; and the Holy One thy eternal portion
opt4: For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called
correct: For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called
explanation: God presents Himself as Zion's loving Husband (Ba'al): Yahweh Sabaoth, the Holy One of Israel, and sovereign God of the entire earth. Isaiah 54:5 (KJV) - "For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel; The God of the whole earth shall he be called."

question: What temporal contrast exists between God's momentary disciplinary anger and His permanent redemptive gathering in Isaiah 54:7-8?
opt1: For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer
opt2: For seventy years did I chasten thee in Babylon, but for a thousand generations shall my peace abide
opt3: In fierce judgment did I scatter thy children, but with songs of joy shall they enter into the promised land
opt4: For three days was the light of my countenance withdrawn, but an eternal sun of righteousness hath arisen
correct: For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer
explanation: Divine wrath during the exile is viewed as merely a fleeting moment ('small moment'), whereas His gathering compassion is characterized by boundless 'everlasting kindness' (chesed olam). Isaiah 54:7-8 (KJV) - "For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee. In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer."

question: To what historic covenant oath does God compare His unbreakable pledge never to pour out wrath upon redeemed Zion again in Isaiah 54:9?
opt1: As the covenant of circumcision with Abraham which cannot be disannulled forever
opt2: For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee
opt3: As the pillar of cloud and fire that guided the children of Israel through the wilderness
opt4: As the sure mercies of David sworn unto the son of Jesse before the ark of the covenant
correct: For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee
explanation: Just as God swore after the Flood that global waters would never again destroy the earth (Genesis 9:11), He swears an inviolable oath of perpetual peace with His redeemed people. Isaiah 54:9 (KJV) - "For this is as the waters of Noah unto me: for as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over the earth; so have I sworn that I would not be wroth with thee, nor rebuke thee."

question: What geological collapse could sooner occur than the removal of God's covenant of peace in Isaiah 54:10?
opt1: The stars shall fall from heaven, and the sun be turned into darkness, before my love shall fail
opt2: The ocean shall dry up, and the rivers cease to flow, before my promise shall be broken
opt3: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee
opt4: The earth shall reel like a drunkard, and the foundations of the world melt, before my truth changeth
correct: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee
explanation: Even if the most permanent earthly landmarks - towering mountains and ancient hills - were pulverized and removed, God's steadfast kindness and covenant of shalom (peace) remain eternally unshakeable. Isaiah 54:10 (KJV) - "For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee."

question: What precious gems and dazzling lapidary architecture will adorn reconstructed Zion in Isaiah 54:11-12?
opt1: Thy walls shall be built of cut onyx, thy courtyards paved with pure gold, and thy battlements of beryl
opt2: Thy towers shall be of polished jasper, thy gates of single pearls, and thy foundations of emerald
opt3: Thy threshold shall be carved of chrysolite, thy pillars of amethyst, and thy roofs of silver
opt4: Behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones
correct: Behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones
explanation: Storm-tossed Zion is transformed into a jewel-box city: sapphire foundations, antimony mortar ('fair colours'), agate windows/battlements, carbuncle/ruby gates, and precious gem perimeter walls (Revelation 21:18-21). Isaiah 54:11-12 (KJV) - "O thou afflicted, tossed with tempest, and not comforted, behold, I will lay thy stones with fair colours, and lay thy foundations with sapphires. And I will make thy windows of agates, and thy gates of carbuncles, and all thy borders of pleasant stones."

question: What divine pedagogy and psychological peace are promised to all the children of Zion in Isaiah 54:13?
opt1: And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children
opt2: They shall be instructed by the prophets, and no sickness shall touch their households
opt3: They shall memorize the law of Moses, and their righteousness shall shine like the sun
opt4: They shall be guided by the high priest, and possess the gates of their enemies forever
correct: And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children
explanation: Quoted by Jesus in John 6:45, all of Zion's children enjoy direct divine illumination ('taught of the LORD') resulting in deep, profound, comprehensive shalom. Isaiah 54:13 (KJV) - "And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children."

question: How does God's sovereign creation of the blacksmith and the destroyer guarantee Zion's absolute security in Isaiah 54:16-17?
opt1: The armor of the enemy shall melt in the fire, and their swords shall break upon the shields of Zion
opt2: Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn
opt3: An army of cherubim shall guard every gate, and the tongues of the false accusers shall be struck dumb
opt4: The arrows of the archers shall turn backward in the wind, and foreign kings shall flee before the Lord
correct: Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn
explanation: Because God created both the weaponsmith who forges swords and the military conqueror who wields them, He holds total control over both: no weapon forged can ever succeed against His people, and all judicial accusations are silenced. Isaiah 54:16-17 (KJV) - "Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy. No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper; and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn."

question: What is the permanent covenant heritage of the servants of the LORD concluding Isaiah 54:17?
opt1: An eternal kingdom on Mount Zion, and a crown of life that fadeth not away
opt2: The blessings of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and an inheritance among all the saints
opt3: This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD
opt4: Victory over all flesh, and an abundant entrance into the city of peace
correct: This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD
explanation: The ultimate legacy of God's servants is inviolable divine protection and God-given righteousness: 'their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD.' Isaiah 54:17 (KJV) - "This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their righteousness is of me, saith the LORD."

question: What gracious, universal market-cry offers spiritual nourishment entirely without financial cost in Isaiah 55:1?
opt1: Come unto me, all ye that labour, and bring your silver into the storehouse of the Lord
opt2: Whosoever will, let him take of the water of life freely, and offer two turtle doves at the altar
opt3: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price
opt4: Hear the word of the Lord, ye hungry of the earth; purchase grain from the granaries of Zion
correct: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price
explanation: God issues a magnificent gospel invitation to spiritually impoverished humanity: come and purchase life-giving water, wine, and milk completely free of charge ('without money and without price'). Isaiah 55:1 (KJV) - "Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price."

question: What piercing diagnostic question exposes the futility of seeking satisfaction in worldly pursuits in Isaiah 55:2?
opt1: Why do ye build palaces of cedar that must perish in the fire, and hoard silver that rusteth?
opt2: Can a man satisfy his hunger with the wind of the east, or quench his thirst in broken cisterns?
opt3: What shall it profit a man if he gain the treasures of Egypt and lose his inheritance in Jacob?
opt4: Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness
correct: Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness
explanation: God challenges the absurdity of exhausting financial resources and life energy on worldly substitutes that fail to satisfy, urging souls to feast on divine truth. Isaiah 55:2 (KJV) - "Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me, and eat ye that which is good, and let your soul delight itself in fatness."

question: What eternal covenant guarantee does God pledge to all who hear and come to Him in Isaiah 55:3?
opt1: Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David
opt2: The covenant of circumcision sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob throughout their generations
opt3: The perpetual priesthood of Phinehas and the blessings of Mount Gerizim forever
opt4: The inheritance of the twelve tribes in the promised land, confirmed with an holy oath
correct: Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David
explanation: Quoted in Acts 13:34, God promises to bestow upon believers the resurrected Messianic blessings known as 'the sure mercies of David' (chesed David ha-ne'emanim). Isaiah 55:3 (KJV) - "Incline your ear, and come unto me: hear, and your soul shall live; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David."

question: What twin conditions of genuine repentance and promise of pardon are commanded in Isaiah 55:6-7?
opt1: Turn ye unto the temple with fasting and tears: offer unblemished rams for your sin offering: and God will heal your land
opt2: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon
opt3: Rend your hearts and not your garments: keep the sabbaths of the Lord without polluting them: and your peace shall be as a river
opt4: Confess your transgressions before the elders of the gate: restore the stolen goods fourfold: and the Lord will remember your affliction
correct: Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon
explanation: True conversion requires abandoning both sinful actions ('his way') and unrighteous mindsets ('his thoughts'), met by God's lavish, overflowing forgiveness ('abundantly pardon'). Isaiah 55:6-7 (KJV) - "Seek ye the LORD while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon."

question: What cosmic distance illustrates the infinite transcendence of God's thoughts and ways above human comprehension in Isaiah 55:8-9?
opt1: As the east is far from the west, so hath he removed our iniquities, and his wisdom is deeper than the ocean
opt2: As the mountains are exalted above the valleys, so are the decrees of the Almighty above the counsels of princes
opt3: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts
opt4: As the light of the sun exceedeth the candle, so doth the knowledge of the Holy One surpass the scribes
correct: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts
explanation: God's redemptive mercy and sovereign purposes transcend finite human expectations as vastly as the infinite heavens tower above the earth. Isaiah 55:8-9 (KJV) - "For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts."

question: What meteorological cycle guarantees the infallible, fruitful efficacy of God's spoken word in Isaiah 55:10-11?
opt1: As the early and latter rain replenish the wells of the desert, so shall the law of the Lord revive the souls of the simple
opt2: As the dew of Mount Hermon falleth upon the mountains of Zion, so shall the promises of the covenant endure forever
opt3: As the south wind bloweth upon the garden to disperse its spices, so shall the gospel be proclaimed unto all nations
opt4: For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: so shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it
correct: For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: so shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it
explanation: Just as rain and snow inevitably saturate the soil to produce harvest without failing, God's decree never returns empty (void), but infallibly achieves His sovereign purpose. Isaiah 55:10-11 (KJV) - "For as the rain cometh down, and the snow from heaven, and returneth not thither, but watereth the earth, and maketh it bring forth and bud, that it may give seed to the sower, and bread to the eater: So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please, and it shall prosper in the thing whereto I sent it."

question: What joyful cosmic personification celebrates the return of the redeemed in Isaiah 55:12?
opt1: For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands
opt2: The stars of heaven shall shout for joy, and the rivers of the desert shall dance in their courses
opt3: The desert shall blossom like the lily, and the wild beasts of the forest shall bow before your path
opt4: The gates of Jerusalem shall open with shouting, and the stones of the sanctuary shall sing together
correct: For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands
explanation: Creation erupts in joyful celebration: mountains and hills sing antiphonally, and forest trees personified clap their branch-hands in rhythm as exiles return. Isaiah 55:12 (KJV) - "For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands."

question: What curse-reversing botanical transformation provides an everlasting sign to the LORD in Isaiah 55:13?
opt1: Instead of the thistle shall grow the olive, and instead of the wormwood shall flourish the sweet vine of Sibmah
opt2: Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off
opt3: Instead of the desert scrub shall rise the cedar of Lebanon, and the parched ground shall blossom as the rose
opt4: Instead of the nettle shall spring up the pomegranate, and the rocky terraces shall overflow with milk and honey
correct: Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off
explanation: The Genesis 3 curse of briers and thorns is reversed into noble cypress (fir) and fragrant myrtle trees, standing as an indestructible monument to God's name. Isaiah 55:13 (KJV) - "Instead of the thorn shall come up the fir tree, and instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to the LORD for a name, for an everlasting sign that shall not be cut off."

question: What three leadership offices does the Davidic Messiah fulfill for the nations according to Isaiah 55:4?
opt1: A priest to the sanctuary, a judge to the tribes, and a king to all flesh
opt2: A shepherd to the flock, an architect of the temple, and a conqueror of the heathen
opt3: A witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people
opt4: A prophet of the covenant, an horn of salvation, and a rock of defence
correct: A witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people
explanation: God appointed Messiah as the faithful Witness (proclaiming divine truth), the princely Leader (Nagid), and the authoritative Commander (Tzavveh) over global peoples. Isaiah 55:4 (KJV) - "Behold, I have given him for a witness to the people, a leader and commander to the people."

question: Why will unknown Gentile nations run eagerly unto Israel in Isaiah 55:5?
opt1: Because of the abundance of the gold and silver of Solomon restored unto Zion
opt2: Because of the mighty armies of Judah that conquer the coastlands of the sea
opt3: Because of the wisdom of the scribes who teach the statutes in the gate
opt4: Because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee
correct: Because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee
explanation: Foreign nations hasten to join God's people not attracted by human prowess, but drawn by the visible glory that Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed upon her. Isaiah 55:5 (KJV) - "Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not, and nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee because of the LORD thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for he hath glorified thee."

question: What inclusive covenant status is promised to castrated eunuchs who keep God's sabbaths and hold fast His covenant in Isaiah 56:4-5?
opt1: They shall be given an inheritance of silver among the priests, and their memorial shall endure for forty generations
opt2: They shall be anointed as royal scribes in the palace of David, and their names recorded in the book of the kings
opt3: They shall receive the portion of the firstborn in the land of Benjamin, and minister before the veil
opt4: Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off
correct: Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off
explanation: Overturning the old covenant exclusion of Deuteronomy 23:1, God promises obedient eunuchs an enduring memorial monument ('yad va-shem') and an eternal name superior to natural sons and daughters. Isaiah 56:4-5 (KJV) - "For thus saith the LORD unto the eunuchs that keep my sabbaths, and choose the things that please me, and take hold of my covenant; Even unto them will I give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name better than of sons and of daughters: I will give them an everlasting name, that shall not be cut off."

question: What universal designation for God's temple welcomes converted Gentiles ('sons of the stranger') in Isaiah 56:7?
opt1: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people
opt2: For my temple shall be called the sanctuary of the twelve tribes of Jacob
opt3: For Mount Zion shall be called the perfection of beauty and the throne of David forever
opt4: For my courts shall be called the dwelling place of righteousness and the joy of Israel
correct: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people
explanation: Quoted by Jesus when cleansing the temple in Matthew 21:13, God declares that His holy sanctuary is destined to be an international house of prayer welcoming all global peoples. Isaiah 56:7 (KJV) - "Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people."

question: What promise of ongoing Gentile ingathering beyond ethnic Israel is stated in Isaiah 56:8?
opt1: He shall assemble the lost sheep of the house of Joseph, and restore the ten tribes from Assyria
opt2: The Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him
opt3: He shall bring the seed of Abraham from the four corners of the earth, and none shall be left behind
opt4: He shall ransom the captives of Judah from the islands of the sea, and establish their borders in peace
correct: The Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him
explanation: Quoted in John 10:16 ('other sheep I have which are not of this fold'), Yahweh gathers non-Israelite Gentiles alongside the recovered outcasts of Israel. Isaiah 56:8 (KJV) - "The Lord GOD which gathereth the outcasts of Israel saith, Yet will I gather others to him, beside those that are gathered unto him."

question: To what useless, sleeping domestic animals are Judah's irresponsible, negligent watchmen compared in Isaiah 56:10?
opt1: They are deaf serpents that hear not the voice of the charmer, wandering in the rocks
opt2: They are blind moles burrowing in the dust, and bats nesting in the broken walls
opt3: His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber
opt4: They are wild asses braying in the wilderness, loving the solitary places of the desert
correct: His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber
explanation: The spiritual leaders are scathingly satirized as blind watchmen and mute guard-dogs ('dumb dogs') that fail to bark when predators attack, spending their days snoring in lazy slumber. Isaiah 56:10 (KJV) - "His watchmen are blind: they are all ignorant, they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark; sleeping, lying down, loving to slumber."

question: What insatiable greed and selfish exploitation characterizes these corrupt spiritual leaders in Isaiah 56:11?
opt1: They shear the sheep and consume the fatlings, leaving the flock to wander on the mountains
opt2: They demand heavy taxes of silver and take bribes against the innocent in the gates
opt3: They devour the houses of widows and for a pretense make long prayers in the streets
opt4: Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter
correct: Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter
explanation: These negligent leaders are ravenous dogs with insatiable appetites ('never have enough') and undiscerning shepherds who pursue only selfish personal enrichment. Isaiah 56:11 (KJV) - "Yea, they are greedy dogs which can never have enough, and they are shepherds that cannot understand: they all look to their own way, every one for his gain, from his quarter."

question: What drunken, reckless hedonism characterizes the corrupt leaders' daily routine in Isaiah 56:12?
opt1: Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant
opt2: Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die; and let no man consider the judgment of God
opt3: We will drink wine in golden bowls and anoint ourselves with chief ointments in the palace
opt4: The harvest of the vineyard is plentiful; let us celebrate forty days of feasting in the gates
correct: Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant
explanation: The leaders indulge in alcoholic binges, arrogantly assuming that tomorrow will bring even greater, unhindered self-indulgence. Isaiah 56:12 (KJV) - "Come ye, say they, I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink; and to morrow shall be as this day, and much more abundant."

question: What core covenant practice is repeatedly highlighted as a vital sign of covenant faithfulness for both native Israelites and foreigners in Isaiah 56:2, 4, 6?
opt1: Offering daily morning and evening burnt offerings of lambs without blemish
opt2: Keeping the sabbath from polluting it, and keeping his hand from doing any evil
opt3: Observing the three annual pilgrim feasts of Unleavened Bread, Weeks, and Tabernacles
opt4: Paying the annual half-shekel temple tax for the service of the sanctuary
correct: Keeping the sabbath from polluting it, and keeping his hand from doing any evil
explanation: Sabbath observance is elevated as the quintessential touchstone of covenant fidelity, accompanied by ethical abstinence from all evil conduct. Isaiah 56:2 (KJV) - "Blessed is the man that doeth this, and the son of man that layeth hold on it; that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and keepeth his hand from doing any evil."

question: What sorrowful self-assessment did the marginalized eunuch express before hearing God's gracious promise in Isaiah 56:3?
opt1: Behold, I am a broken cistern that can hold no water
opt2: Behold, I am a withered bough cut off from the house of Israel
opt3: Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree
opt4: Behold, I am an outcast without an inheritance in the promised land
correct: Neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree
explanation: Excluded from fathering children, the eunuch lamented being a sterile, dead sapling ('a dry tree'), but God promises him a legacy superior to biological descendants. Isaiah 56:3 (KJV) - "Neither let the son of the stranger, that hath joined himself to the LORD, speak, saying, The LORD hath utterly separated me from his people: neither let the eunuch say, Behold, I am a dry tree."

question: What ravenous predatory summons invites foreign invaders to devour unprotected Israel in Isaiah 56:9?
opt1: All ye lions of the desert, arise and scatter the sheep of Jacob
opt2: All ye vultures of heaven, gather together unto the great supper of God
opt3: All ye wolves of the evening, break into the fold and spare not the lambs
opt4: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest
correct: All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest
explanation: Because the nation's spiritual watchdogs are mute and asleep, wild predatory beasts (foreign imperial armies) are invited to devour the defenseless flock. Isaiah 56:9 (KJV) - "All ye beasts of the field, come to devour, yea, all ye beasts in the forest."

question: What divine moral imperative precedes the revelation of near salvation in Isaiah 56:1?
opt1: Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed
opt2: Sanctify yourselves, for tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you
opt3: Repent and be baptized every one of you for the remission of your sins
opt4: Wash your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded
correct: Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed
explanation: Eschatological salvation is not an excuse for ethical laxity: because God's deliverance is imminent, His people must maintain justice and practice righteousness. Isaiah 56:1 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, Keep ye judgment, and do justice: for my salvation is near to come, and my righteousness to be revealed."

question: What compassionate divine purpose explains why godly and righteous individuals often die prematurely in Isaiah 57:1?
opt1: The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come
opt2: Because their days of pilgrimage on earth are accomplished and their reward is prepared in heaven
opt3: Lest their hearts be corrupted by the idolatry of their neighbours and they lose their inheritance
opt4: That they may enter into the rest of the patriarchs and be spared the seventy years of exile
correct: The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come
explanation: Unnoticed by an indifferent society, the untimely death of the righteous is often an act of divine mercy, sparing them from impending historical calamities ('the evil to come'). Isaiah 57:1 (KJV) - "The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart: and merciful men are taken away, none considering that the righteous is taken away from the evil to come."

question: What peaceful rest and upright walk reward the deceased righteous in Isaiah 57:2?
opt1: He shall sit upon a throne of gold: they shall reign with the angels of light
opt2: He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness
opt3: He shall drink of the river of life: they shall be crowned with the stars of heaven
opt4: He shall dwell in the holy of holies: they shall feast at the table of the King
correct: He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness
explanation: Physical death for the believer is a peaceful sleep ('rest in their beds' / tombs) leading into eternal shalom for all who walked uprightly. Isaiah 57:2 (KJV) - "He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness."

question: What horrific pagan child sacrifices in rocky ravines are condemned in Isaiah 57:5?
opt1: Burning your sons and your daughters in the fire of Molech upon the high place of Tophet
opt2: Offering your firstborn upon altars of stone in the dark caves of Mount Hermon
opt3: Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks
opt4: Drowning your infants in the river Euphrates to appease the water gods of the Chaldeans
correct: Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks
explanation: Apostates indulged in Canaanite fertility orgies under sacred trees and slaughtered their own children in rocky wadis as human sacrifices. Isaiah 57:5 (KJV) - "Enflaming yourselves with idols under every green tree, slaying the children in the valleys under the clifts of the rocks?"

question: To what water-smoothed pagan objects did idolaters pour out libation drink offerings in Isaiah 57:6?
opt1: Unto the carved images of wood hidden in the secret chambers of the threshold
opt2: Unto the bronze pillars set up before the temples of Baal in the high places
opt3: Unto the golden calves worshipped at Dan and Bethel throughout their generations
opt4: Among the smooth stones of the stream is thy portion; they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou poured a drink offering, thou hast offered a meat offering
correct: Among the smooth stones of the stream is thy portion; they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou poured a drink offering, thou hast offered a meat offering
explanation: Idolaters deified river-worn stones (sacred boundary markers or cultic stones), pouring wine and grain offerings to inanimate rocks. Isaiah 57:6 (KJV) - "Among the smooth stones of the stream is thy portion; they, they are thy lot: even to them hast thou poured a drink offering, thou hast offered a meat offering. Should I receive comfort in these?"

question: What exhaustive diplomatic and religious debasement, stooping even unto Sheol, did Judah pursue in Isaiah 57:9?
opt1: And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst increase thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers far off, and didst debase thyself even unto hell
opt2: Thou didst hire the cavalry of Egypt with the gold of the sanctuary, and bowed before Pharaoh
opt3: Thou didst send fifty talents of silver to the king of Assyria, and worshipped his gods in Nineveh
opt4: Thou didst consult the necromancers of the desert, and offered sacrifices to the dead in the tombs
correct: And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst increase thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers far off, and didst debase thyself even unto hell
explanation: Like an adulterous woman perfuming herself for lovers, Judah debased herself to subterranean depths ('even unto hell' / Sheol) seeking foreign treaties and pagan patron deities. Isaiah 57:9 (KJV) - "And thou wentest to the king with ointment, and didst increase thy perfumes, and didst send thy messengers far off, and didst debase thyself even unto hell."

question: What dual dwelling place characterizes the High and Lofty One that inhabiteth eternity in Isaiah 57:15?
opt1: I dwell in the highest heavens, and in the temple of Jerusalem between the cherubim
opt2: I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones
opt3: I reign upon the throne of glory, and among the twelve tribes of Jacob in the wilderness
opt4: I abide in unapproachable light, and with the righteous kings who keep my commandments
correct: I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones
explanation: The transcendent God who inhabits eternity chooses a second, astonishing terrestrial home: within the broken, humble heart of the contrite person to revive and heal. Isaiah 57:15 (KJV) - "For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones."

question: Why does God refuse to remain perpetually angry or contend forever with humanity in Isaiah 57:16?
opt1: Because he remembereth his covenant with David and will not permit the scepter to depart
opt2: Lest the enemy boast that the heritage of Jacob hath been utterly destroyed from the earth
opt3: For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth: for the spirit should fail before me, and the souls which I have made
opt4: For he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, repenting him of the evil
correct: For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth: for the spirit should fail before me, and the souls which I have made
explanation: God restrains His infinite wrath because if He unleashed it without limit, human breath and mortal souls ('which I have made') would faint and be utterly extinguished. Isaiah 57:16 (KJV) - "For I will not contend for ever, neither will I be always wroth: for the spirit should fail before me, and the souls which I have made."

question: What vocal praise does God supernaturally create, offering comprehensive peace to both distant and near in Isaiah 57:19?
opt1: I create songs of thanksgiving; Salvation, salvation to the seed of Abraham and the outcasts of Israel
opt2: I put a new hymn in their mouth; Glory, glory to the King of Zion and the righteous of the earth
opt3: I inspire the prayers of the saints; Mercy, mercy to the brokenhearted and the captive in Babylon
opt4: I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him
correct: I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him
explanation: Quoted in Ephesians 2:17 regarding Christ reconciling Jews ('near') and Gentiles ('far off'), God creates the joyful fruit of lips proclaiming double shalom: 'Peace, peace!' Isaiah 57:19 (KJV) - "I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him."

question: To what restless, churning body of water are the wicked compared in Isaiah 57:20?
opt1: The wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt
opt2: Like a raging river overflowing its banks, sweeping away the bridges in the flood
opt3: Like a stagnant pool in the summer heat, filled with green scum and bitter gall
opt4: Like an angry whirlwind in the desert, casting sand into the eyes of the traveler
correct: The wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt
explanation: The ungodly live in perpetual psychological and spiritual turmoil, like an agitated, stormy ocean whose ceaseless churn dredges up filthy mud and refuse. Isaiah 57:20 (KJV) - "But the wicked are like the troubled sea, when it cannot rest, whose waters cast up mire and dirt."

question: What solemn divine verdict concludes the second major 9-chapter cycle of the Book of Comfort in Isaiah 57:21?
opt1: For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life
