opt2: There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked
opt3: The soul that sinneth shall surely die, saith the Lord of hosts
opt4: Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire prepared for the devil
correct: There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked
explanation: Concluding the second 9-chapter division (Chapters 49-57, matching 48:22), God reiterates the absolute spiritual law: 'There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked.' Isaiah 57:21 (KJV) - "There is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked."

question: What trumpet-like vocal proclamation is commanded to expose religious hypocrisy in Isaiah 58:1?
opt1: Blow the shofar in Zion, sound an alarm on the holy mountain, and call a solemn assembly
opt2: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins
opt3: Proclaim liberty throughout all the land, and declare the day of vengeance of our God
opt4: Speak comfortably to Jerusalem, and cry unto her that her warfare is accomplished
correct: Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins
explanation: The prophet must shout at maximum volume without holding back, like a piercing ram's horn (shofar), confronting superficial religion with its sins. Isaiah 58:1 (KJV) - "Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins."

question: Why did God reject the people's pious fasting and ascetic soul-affliction in Isaiah 58:3-4?
opt1: Because ye fast without sprinkling ashes upon your heads and refuse to wear coarse sackcloth
opt2: Because ye offer unblemished lambs while neglecting the morning incense of the sanctuary
opt3: Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high
opt4: Because ye fast only on the new moons while worshipping foreign idols upon the high places
correct: Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high
explanation: Their fasts were religious theater masking social exploitation: pursuing selfish business profits, mistreating day-laborers, and engaging in petty quarrels and violent fistfights. Isaiah 58:3-4 (KJV) - "Wherefore have we fasted, say they, and thou seest not? wherefore have we afflicted our soul, and thou takest no knowledge? Behold, in the day of your fast ye find pleasure, and exact all your labours. Behold, ye fast for strife and debate, and to smite with the fist of wickedness: ye shall not fast as ye do this day, to make your voice to be heard on high."

question: What six social justice actions define the true, God-chosen fast in Isaiah 58:6?
opt1: To build synagogues in every city, to recite the Torah at the gates, to offer double tithes, and to observe forty days of mourning
opt2: To abstain from meat and wine, to sleep on the ground, to walk barefoot, and to give alms to the priests
opt3: To circumcise foreign slaves, to cleanse the temple vessels, to repair the city walls, and to banish foreign merchants
opt4: To loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke
correct: To loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke
explanation: True fasting is ethical, liberating, and activist: dismantling unjust debt contracts, relieving crushing burdens, liberating the oppressed, and shattering every oppressive yoke. Isaiah 58:6 (KJV) - "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? to loose the bands of wickedness, to undo the heavy burdens, and to let the oppressed go free, and that ye break every yoke?"

question: What practical compassion toward the poor, homeless, and naked is commanded in Isaiah 58:7?
opt1: Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
opt2: To distribute copper coins to the beggars in the gate, and pour wine for the sick in the hospital
opt3: To build storehouses for the fatherless, and hire Egyptian physicians to heal the lepers
opt4: To send grain to the desert nomads, and sacrifice three bullocks for the redemption of the destitute
correct: Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?
explanation: Authentic worship shares food with the starving, opens homes to shelter the destitute, clothes the shivering, and refuses to turn a blind eye to suffering fellow human beings. Isaiah 58:6-7 (KJV) - "Is not this the fast that I have chosen? ... Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?"

question: What radiant dawn, rapid physical healing, and divine vanguard/rearguard accompany true compassion in Isaiah 58:8?
opt1: Then shall the sun stand still in the heavens, and the angels of God shall encamp around thy dwellings
opt2: Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward
opt3: Then shall thy riches increase tenfold, and the kings of the Gentiles shall bring tribute unto thy gates
opt4: Then shall all sickness be banished from thy borders, and thy days shall be multiplied as the sand of the sea
correct: Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward
explanation: Active social mercy unlocks explosive spiritual breakthrough: light dawning like the sun, rapid healing, personal righteousness leading the vanguard, and Yahweh's glory guarding the rear. Isaiah 58:8 (KJV) - "Then shall thy light break forth as the morning, and thine health shall spring forth speedily: and thy righteousness shall go before thee; the glory of the LORD shall be thy rereward."

question: What instantaneous divine response to prayer is promised when oppressive finger-pointing and malicious speech are eliminated in Isaiah 58:9?
opt1: Before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will send my angel with deliverance
opt2: The Lord shall hear from his holy heaven, and shall open the windows of blessing above your heads
opt3: Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity
opt4: Thy voice shall enter into the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth, and he shall execute judgment upon thine enemies
correct: Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity
explanation: When believers stop accusing others ('putting forth of the finger') and uttering malicious gossip, God answers prayer with immediate, loving intimacy: 'Here I am!' Isaiah 58:9 (KJV) - "Then shalt thou call, and the LORD shall answer; thou shalt cry, and he shall say, Here I am. If thou take away from the midst of thee the yoke, the putting forth of the finger, and speaking vanity;"

question: What horticultural and hydrological metaphors describe the nourished soul that ministers to the afflicted in Isaiah 58:11?
opt1: Thou shalt be like an olive tree planted by running waters, and like a vineyard that yieldeth choice wine
opt2: Thou shalt be like a cedar of Lebanon in the forest, and like a well of living water in the desert
opt3: Thou shalt be like a fruitful palm in the oasis of Jericho, and like a fountain sealed in the garden of the king
opt4: The LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not
correct: The LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not
explanation: The selfless soul is continually guided, energized ('fat bones'), and transformed into a lush irrigated garden fed by an unfailing, perennial freshwater spring. Isaiah 58:11 (KJV) - "And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not."

question: What noble architectural and civil reconstruction titles are bestowed upon the obedient community in Isaiah 58:12?
opt1: Thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in
opt2: The builder of the sanctuary, The keeper of the holy gates
opt3: The restorer of the throne of David, The defender of the city of peace
opt4: The rebuilder of the temple, The watchman of the walls of Zion
correct: Thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in
explanation: They rebuild ancient generational foundations and receive glorious titles: 'The repairer of the breach' and 'The restorer of paths to dwell in.' Isaiah 58:12 (KJV) - "And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places: thou shalt raise up the foundations of many generations; and thou shalt be called, The repairer of the breach, The restorer of paths to dwell in."

question: What joyful, honoring attitude toward the Sabbath is commanded, turning away from selfish pursuits in Isaiah 58:13?
opt1: If thou walk not more than a sabbath day's journey, and kindle no fire in any of your habitations
opt2: If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words
opt3: If thou offer two lambs of the first year without spot, and bake twelve loaves of shewbread before the altar
opt4: If thou close the city gates to foreign traders, and compel all bondmen to rest according to the law
correct: If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words
explanation: True Sabbath keeping is not grim legalism, but a joyful celebration ('a delight'): setting aside personal business, selfish pleasures, and idle talk to honor God wholeheartedly. Isaiah 58:13 (KJV) - "If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the LORD, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words:"

question: What triumphant spiritual elevation and patriarchal inheritance reward genuine Sabbath delight in Isaiah 58:14?
opt1: Then shalt thou inherit the kingdom of heaven, and sit upon twelve thrones judging the tribes of Israel
opt2: Then shall the wealth of the Gentiles be poured into thy storehouses, and all kings shall bow before thee
opt3: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it
opt4: Then shall thy days be prolonged in the land, and thy children shall be as the stars of the sky in multitude
correct: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it
explanation: Honoring God's holy day elevates the soul above earthly tribulations ('ride upon the high places of the earth') and guarantees full enjoyment of the covenant inheritance of Jacob. Isaiah 58:14 (KJV) - "Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it."

question: What profound theological truth explains why prayers seem unanswered and salvation delayed in Isaiah 59:1-2?
opt1: The Lord hath turned away his face because the temple altar was broken down by the Chaldeans
opt2: God is testing the patience of the house of Jacob, to see if they will remain faithful in the furnace of affliction
opt3: Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear
opt4: The decrees of heaven are sealed until the seventy years of captivity in Babylon be accomplished
correct: Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: but your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear
explanation: God's power is never diminished ('hand not shortened') nor His perception dulled ('ear not heavy'); human sin and unrepentant iniquity create the barrier separating mankind from God. Isaiah 59:1-2 (KJV) - "Behold, the LORD's hand is not shortened, that it cannot save; neither his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you, that he will not hear."

question: What venomous and fragile metaphors depict the lethal schemes and useless self-justifications of wicked conspirators in Isaiah 59:5-6?
opt1: They plant bitter wormwood in the valleys, and sow seeds of thistle in the vineyards of the king
opt2: They dig deep pits in the darkness, and weave heavy nets of iron to ensnare the innocent
opt3: They forge sharp swords of bronze, and drink the poison of asps from the golden vessels of the temple
opt4: They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper. Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works
correct: They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper. Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works
explanation: Evil plots produce deadly vipers ('cockatrice eggs') that poison anyone tasting them, while their fragile web-weaving can never serve as a genuine moral garment to cover their guilt. Isaiah 59:5-6 (KJV) - "They hatch cockatrice' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he that eateth of their eggs dieth, and that which is crushed breaketh out into a viper. Their webs shall not become garments, neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands."

question: How does Paul quote Isaiah 59:7-8 in Romans 3 to prove universal human depravity?
opt1: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood ... the way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings
opt2: There is none righteous, no, not one; they are all gone out of the way, they are together become unprofitable
opt3: Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; the poison of asps is under their lips
opt4: Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness; destruction and misery are in their paths
correct: Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood ... the way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings
explanation: Paul incorporates Isaiah 59:7-8 into Romans 3:15-17 to demonstrate total depravity: feet eager to shed blood, thoughts of destruction, and complete ignorance of the path of peace. Isaiah 59:7-8 (KJV) - "Their feet run to evil, and they make haste to shed innocent blood: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity; wasting and destruction are in their paths. The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths: whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace."

question: What sensory blindness and disorientation depict society's moral helplessness in Isaiah 59:9-10?
opt1: We wander in the desert without a guide, and drink salt water from the broken cisterns of the wilderness
opt2: We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men
opt3: We sleep in darkness like prisoners in the pit, and our knees tremble before the shadow of the oppressor
opt4: We flee before the sound of a shaken leaf, and our eyes fail with looking upward in vain
correct: We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men
explanation: Society stumbles blindly in broad daylight like blind men groping along walls, spiritually lifeless and directionless like corpses in a tomb. Isaiah 59:10 (KJV) - "We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men."

question: What animal sounds express the populace's frustrated groaning and persistent grief in Isaiah 59:11?
opt1: We howl like jackals in the desert, and cry like pelicans in the wilderness
opt2: We bray like wild asses upon the mountains, and chatter like cranes in the storm
opt3: We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us
opt4: We weep like calves trapped in the net, and scream like eagles wounded on the rocks
correct: We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us
explanation: The people alternate between angry animalistic bellowing ('roar like bears') and pitiful, mournful cooing ('mourn sore like doves') over the complete absence of justice. Isaiah 59:11 (KJV) - "We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far off from us."

question: What civic collapse is personified in the public square, showing truth fallen and equity barred from entering in Isaiah 59:14-15?
opt1: The elders have fled from the gate, and the judges take bribes of gold; the law of the Lord is trampled in the mud
opt2: The sanctuary is defiled with blood, and the witnesses lie in the darkness; the innocent are sold for silver
opt3: The city wall is broken down, and the council of the princes is divided; the righteous are banished from the assembly
opt4: Judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey
correct: Judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey
explanation: In personified judicial collapse, Truth collapses like an injured man in the public street, Justice stands exiled afar, Equity is locked outside, and anyone trying to live righteously becomes hunted prey. Isaiah 59:14-15 (KJV) - "And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: and the LORD saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment."

question: What divine wonder and solo warrior intervention occurs when God finds no human champion to execute justice in Isaiah 59:16?
opt1: And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him
opt2: He summoned the archangel Michael to lead the host of heaven, and cast down the dragon into the abyss
opt3: He commanded King Cyrus to march with two hundred thousand chariots, and deliver his people from Babylon
opt4: He caused an earthquake to shake the foundations of the earth, and executed vengeance upon all the heathen
correct: And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him
explanation: God is astonished at the total absence of human leadership or intercessors; therefore, He steps in personally, His own sovereign arm achieving redemption. Isaiah 59:16 (KJV) - "And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor: therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him."

question: What military panoply of divine armor does Yahweh put on to execute cosmic justice in Isaiah 59:17?
opt1: He girded on the sword of the covenant, took up the shield of faith, and put on the sandals of the gospel
opt2: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke
opt3: He wore the breastplate of Urim, the golden crown of David, and the royal mantle of fine linen
opt4: He put on the belt of truth, the armor of light, and the iron greaves of judgment
correct: He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke
explanation: The foundational source for Paul's armor of God in Ephesians 6:14-17: Yahweh equips Himself with the breastplate of righteousness, helmet of salvation, garments of vengeance, and cloak of holy zeal. Isaiah 59:17 (KJV) - "For he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and an helmet of salvation upon his head; and he put on the garments of vengeance for clothing, and was clad with zeal as a cloke."

question: What divine defense repels the adversary when he invades like an overwhelming river flood in Isaiah 59:19?
opt1: The angel of the Lord shall encamp round about them that fear him, and deliver them from the deep waters
opt2: A mighty wall of fire shall descend from heaven, and the chariots of the adversary shall be consumed
opt3: When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him
opt4: The trumpet of Zion shall sound from the mountain, and the host of the heathen shall flee in panic
correct: When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him
explanation: When demonic or imperial enemies advance like a swollen, destructive flash-flood, the Holy Spirit sovereignly hoists His unconquerable battle banner (standard) to rout the foe. Isaiah 59:19 (KJV) - "So shall they fear the name of the LORD from the west, and his glory from the rising of the sun. When the enemy shall come in like a flood, the Spirit of the LORD shall lift up a standard against him."

question: What eternal covenant promise guarantees the permanent presence of the Spirit and God's Word through all future generations in Isaiah 59:20-21?
opt1: And the Messiah shall reign in Jerusalem ... and the law of Moses shall be written upon tablets of bronze forever
opt2: And the High Priest shall make atonement ... and the holy fire upon the altar shall never be extinguished
opt3: And the twelve tribes shall inherit the land ... and their children shall possess the riches of the Gentiles world without end
opt4: And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob ... My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever
correct: And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob ... My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever
explanation: Quoted in Romans 11:26-27, the coming Redeemer guarantees an unbreakable generational covenant: the Holy Spirit and God's inspired words will never depart from the mouths of His redeemed line forever. Isaiah 59:20-21 (KJV) - "And the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob, saith the LORD. As for me, this is my covenant with them, saith the LORD; My spirit that is upon thee, and my words which I have put in thy mouth, shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed, saith the LORD, from henceforth and for ever."

question: What radiant sunrise command summons Zion to illuminate a world covered in spiritual gloom in Isaiah 60:1-2?
opt1: Awake, awake; put on thy strength, O Zion; for the morning star hath appeared in the east to guide the nations
opt2: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Jerusalem; for the sun of righteousness hath arisen with healing in his wings
opt3: Lift up thine eyes unto the mountains, O city of peace; for the clouds of mourning have rolled away forever
opt4: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee
correct: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee
explanation: While dense spiritual blindness ('gross darkness') blankets global humanity, Zion is commanded to blaze with reflected light because Yahweh's glorious presence dawns upon her like a sunrise. Isaiah 60:1-2 (KJV) - "Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the LORD shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee."

question: What international pilgrimage brings Gentile kings and wealth flocking to Zion's dawn in Isaiah 60:3-5?
opt1: And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising ... the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee
opt2: The princes of Egypt shall bring silver in five thousand galleys, and the governors of Babylon shall build thy walls
opt3: The monarchs of Tarshish shall fall down in the dust, and the islands shall send their sons to minister in the temple
opt4: All the kingdoms of the earth shall surrender their crowns, and the riches of the heathen shall pave the streets of Zion
correct: And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising ... the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee
explanation: Drawn by the supernatural illumination, Gentile rulers and multi-ethnic caravans converge on Zion, surrendering the wealth ('forces' / wealth) of maritime nations. Isaiah 60:3, 5 (KJV) - "And the Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising ... Then thou shalt see, and flow together, and thine heart shall fear, and be enlarged; because the abundance of the sea shall be converted unto thee, the forces of the Gentiles shall come unto thee."

question: What camel caravans from Midian, Ephah, and Sheba arrive bearing gifts, prefiguring the Magi, in Isaiah 60:6?
opt1: Caravans of white asses from Damascus, bearing myrrh and frankincense to anoint the altar of the sanctuary
opt2: The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the LORD
opt3: Merchant troops from Kedar and Dedan, bearing woven scarlet textiles and vessels of refined silver
opt4: Armies of riders from Arabia, presenting ten thousand talents of gold and spices from the mountains of the east
correct: The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the LORD
explanation: Echoed in Matthew 2:11 at the Epiphany, Arabian camel caravans from Midian, Ephah, and Sheba arrive laden with gold and frankincense to praise Yahweh. Isaiah 60:6 (KJV) - "The multitude of camels shall cover thee, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah; all they from Sheba shall come: they shall bring gold and incense; and they shall shew forth the praises of the LORD."

question: To what soaring clouds and homing birds are returning maritime fleets likened in Isaiah 60:8?
opt1: Who are these that march like locusts over the hills, and as eagles soaring to their aerie?
opt2: Who are these that sail like swans upon the great deep, and as swallows returning in the spring?
opt3: Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?
opt4: Who are these that advance like chariots of fire, and as falcons diving upon the prey?
correct: Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?
explanation: Looking toward the Mediterranean, Zion marvels at billowing white sails gliding swiftly across the horizon like clouds or flocks of homing doves flying toward their roosting dovecotes. Isaiah 60:8 (KJV) - "Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?"

question: Why are Zion's gates ordered to remain perpetually open day and night in Isaiah 60:11?
opt1: That the watchmen may see the sunrise upon Mount Olivet, and that no enemy may find a place to ambush the city
opt2: That the river of life may flow freely through the streets, and that the trees of the sanctuary may be watered
opt3: That the sacrifices of the twelve tribes may enter without delay, and the priests minister without ceasing
opt4: Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought
correct: Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought
explanation: Quoted in Revelation 21:25, Zion's gates never shut because absolute peace reigns and an unending stream of Gentile wealth and tributary kings flows into the city around the clock. Isaiah 60:11 (KJV) - "Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought."

question: What three noble Lebanese trees are imported to beautify the sanctuary and make God's footstool glorious in Isaiah 60:13?
opt1: The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious
opt2: The tall cedar, the fragrant myrtle, and the green olive tree together, to overlay the courtyards with wood
opt3: The ancient oak of Bashan, the sycamore of the plain, and the palm of Jericho, to build the outer gates
opt4: The cypress of Chittim, the almond of Bethel, and the acacia of the desert, to carve the golden doors
correct: The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious
explanation: Cypress (fir), pine, and boxwood/cedar are brought from Lebanon to construct and beautify the holy sanctuary - the earthly footstool of God's presence. Isaiah 60:13 (KJV) - "The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my feet glorious."

question: What ultimate architectural and civic upgrades replace inferior base metals with precious materials in Isaiah 60:17?
opt1: For stone I will bring cut granite, and for clay refined marble, and for lead pure tin from the islands
opt2: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness
opt3: For bronze shields I will forge golden bucklers, and for iron chariots royal pavilions of cedar
opt4: For common timber I will provide ivory from the south, and for gravel diamonds from the mountains
correct: For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness
explanation: Solomonic splendor is eclipsed: base metals are upgraded to precious metals (gold for bronze, silver for iron), and civil rulers are personified as Peace and Righteousness. Isaiah 60:17 (KJV) - "For brass I will bring gold, and for iron I will bring silver, and for wood brass, and for stones iron: I will also make thy officers peace, and thine exactors righteousness."

question: What glorious new names replace the conventional defensive walls and city gates of Zion in Isaiah 60:18?
opt1: Thou shalt call thy ramparts Holiness, and thy portals Peace
opt2: Thou shalt call thy towers Deliverance, and thy battlements Glory
opt3: Thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise
opt4: Thou shalt call thy foundations Truth, and thy thresholds Righteousness
correct: Thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise
explanation: Warfare and violence vanish; physical walls are named 'Salvation' (Yeshuah) and entry gates are named 'Praise' (Tehillah). Isaiah 60:18 (KJV) - "Violence shall no more be heard in thy land, wasting nor destruction within thy borders; but thou shalt call thy walls Salvation, and thy gates Praise."

question: What celestial illumination is permanently superseded by God's own uncreated, everlasting light in Isaiah 60:19-20?
opt1: The stars of heaven shall shine sevenfold brighter, and the morning star shall rule the day without ceasing
opt2: A pillar of fire shall illuminate the city by day, and twelve golden lamps shall burn throughout the night
opt3: The clouds of glory shall reflect the light of the sun, so that darkness shall never fall upon the holy mountain
opt4: The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself
correct: The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself
explanation: Quoted in Revelation 21:23 and 22:5, natural created luminaries (sun and moon) become obsolete because Yahweh Himself serves as the city's eternal, unsetting light. Isaiah 60:19-20 (KJV) - "The sun shall be no more thy light by day; neither for brightness shall the moon give light unto thee: but the LORD shall be unto thee an everlasting light, and thy God thy glory. Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended."

question: What supernatural demographic explosion will transform the smallest remnant into a powerful nation in Isaiah 60:22?
opt1: A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the LORD will hasten it in his time
opt2: A single family shall inherit twelve cities, and the least among them shall conquer a legion
opt3: The children of the desolate shall outnumber the stars of heaven, and their seed shall possess the gates of the earth
opt4: The remnant of Judah shall be multiplied as the sand of the sea, and their princes shall rule over kings
correct: A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the LORD will hasten it in his time
explanation: The tiniest, most insignificant clan multiplies miraculously into a thousand, and the smallest tribe becomes a mighty nation; Yahweh guarantees to accelerate it rapidly at the appointed hour. Isaiah 60:22 (KJV) - "A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the LORD will hasten it in his time."

question: What famous Messianic manifesto of the Spirit's anointing and liberation ministry did Jesus read in the Nazareth synagogue in Isaiah 61:1-2?
opt1: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; to proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God
opt2: The Spirit of wisdom hath rested upon me; because the Lord hath chosen me to teach the law of Moses in the gates and build the walls of Jerusalem
opt3: The glory of the Lord is risen upon me; because the Almighty hath crowned me with the scepter of David to conquer the armies of the heathen
opt4: The word of the Lord came unto me, saying, Arise and prophesy against the false shepherds who scatter the flock of Jacob in the wilderness
correct: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; to proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God
explanation: In Luke 4:18-21, Jesus inaugurated His public ministry by reading this exact text, declaring its fulfillment in Himself as the Spirit-anointed Herald of liberty, healing, and the acceptable year of the Lord (the Jubilee). Isaiah 61:1-2 (KJV) - "The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound; To proclaim the acceptable year of the LORD, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn;"

question: What three miraculous reversals of mourning and new botanical identity are bestowed upon grief-stricken Zion in Isaiah 61:3?
opt1: To give them gold for bronze, sweet wine for bitter water, and fine linen for haircloth; that they might be called the princes of the sanctuary
opt2: To give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified
opt3: To give them joy for sorrow, singing for lamentation, and light for darkness; that they might be called the pillars of truth on Mount Zion
opt4: To give them peace for war, health for sickness, and crowns for dust; that they might be called the children of the covenant forever
correct: To give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified
explanation: God replaces funeral ashes with a bridal crown ('beauty'), weeping with fragrant perfumed oil ('oil of joy'), and despair with a festive cloak ('garment of praise'), establishing believers as majestic 'trees of righteousness' (oaks of justice) for His glory. Isaiah 61:3 (KJV) - "To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified."

question: What priestly title and ministerial role will the nations ascribe to redeemed Israel in Isaiah 61:6?
opt1: Ye shall be named the Kings of the earth: men shall call you the Captains of the host of David
opt2: Ye shall be named the Judges of the nations: men shall call you the Scribes of the holy law
opt3: But ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves
opt4: Ye shall be named the Prophets of the Most High: men shall call you the Shepherds of the flocks of God
correct: But ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves
explanation: Fulfilling the Exodus 19:6 ideal, the entire redeemed community is consecrated as royal mediators: named 'the Priests of the LORD' and 'Ministers of our God' sustained by Gentile riches. Isaiah 61:6 (KJV) - "But ye shall be named the Priests of the LORD: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles, and in their glory shall ye boast yourselves."

question: What double portion and joyful compensation replaces Israel's past humiliation and reproach in Isaiah 61:7?
opt1: For your poverty ye shall receive ten thousand talents of gold, and for your exile an eternal inheritance in Zion
opt2: For your tears ye shall reap overflowing harvests of wheat, and for your wounds the health of the righteous
opt3: For your captivity ye shall rule over seven nations, and for your mourning a crown that fadeth not away
opt4: For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them
correct: For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them
explanation: In place of historic shame, God awards the firstborn's double portion of blessing and permanent rejoicing within their own land: 'everlasting joy shall be unto them.' Isaiah 61:7 (KJV) - "For your shame ye shall have double; and for confusion they shall rejoice in their portion: therefore in their land they shall possess the double: everlasting joy shall be unto them."

question: What bridal and priestly garments adorn the rejoicing soul clothed by God in Isaiah 61:10?
opt1: He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels
opt2: He hath crowned me with the diadem of David, and girded my loins with the belt of truth and gold
opt3: He hath anointed me with the oil of gladness, and clothed me in the purple mantle of the kings of Judah
opt4: He hath washed my soul in the river of life, and placed the signet ring of the covenant upon my hand
correct: He hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels
explanation: The redeemed soul celebrates divine salvation dressed in royal bridal regalia: clothed in the garments of salvation and wrapped in the immaculate robe of Christ's imputed righteousness. Isaiah 61:10 (KJV) - "I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decketh himself with ornaments, and as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels."

question: To what natural seed germination in a cultivated garden is the worldwide sprout of righteousness compared in Isaiah 61:11?
opt1: As the rain of heaven causeth the grass to grow upon the mountains, so shall the law of the Lord enlighten all flesh
opt2: For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations
opt3: As the river of Egypt watereth the delta in the harvest, so shall the knowledge of God overflow the earth
opt4: As the vine of Sibmah spreadeth its branches unto the sea, so shall the peace of Zion cover the kingdoms
correct: For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations
explanation: Just as fertile soil reliably germinates seeds sown within it, the Lord GOD will cause international righteousness and global praise to sprout visibly before all Gentile nations. Isaiah 61:11 (KJV) - "For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations."

question: What moral hatred of corrupt worship and social robbery is articulated by the LORD in Isaiah 61:8?
opt1: I hate sacrifices offered with unwashed hands, and abominate the new moons of the hypocrite
opt2: I despise the prayers of those that shed blood, and turn away mine eyes from the gifts of extortion
opt3: For I the LORD love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them
opt4: I will not accept the blood of bulls from the hands of the proud, neither will I smell your sweet incense
correct: For I the LORD love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them
explanation: God loves authentic justice and detests religious offerings financed through extortion or theft ('robbery for burnt offering'), establishing an everlasting covenant in truth. Isaiah 61:8 (KJV) - "For I the LORD love judgment, I hate robbery for burnt offering; and I will direct their work in truth, and I will make an everlasting covenant with them."

question: What universal recognition will Gentile nations accord to the physical and spiritual descendants of Israel in Isaiah 61:9?
opt1: All kings shall fall down before their gates, and confess that their God is the Lord of heaven
opt2: All peoples shall marvel at their wisdom, and seek instruction from the elders of the gate
opt3: All the families of the earth shall bring offerings, and praise the Holy One of Jacob in the temple
opt4: All that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed
correct: All that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed
explanation: Wherever Israel's offspring are encountered globally, onlookers will immediately recognize and acknowledge them as the uniquely blessed seed of Yahweh. Isaiah 61:9 (KJV) - "And their seed shall be known among the Gentiles, and their offspring among the people: all that see them shall acknowledge them, that they are the seed which the LORD hath blessed."

question: Who will perform the agrarian and pastoral labor for the redeemed priests of the LORD in Isaiah 61:5?
opt1: Strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers
opt2: The captive soldiers of Babylon shall till the soil, and the princes of Assyria shall prune the vineyards
opt3: The Levites of the rural towns shall pasture the cattle, and the outcasts of Ephraim shall reap the barley
opt4: Egyptian day-labourers shall dig the irrigation canals, and the merchants of Tyre shall manage the flocks
correct: Strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers
explanation: Foreigners and Gentiles ('strangers' and 'sons of the alien') willingly manage the physical farming, plowing, and flocks, freeing Israel for her sacred priestly calling. Isaiah 61:5 (KJV) - "And strangers shall stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers."

question: What architectural reconstruction of ancient ruins is accomplished by the empowered community in Isaiah 61:4?
opt1: They shall erect a second temple with cedar of Lebanon, and fortify the gates of Jerusalem with bronze
opt2: They shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations
opt3: They shall restore the twelve cities of refuge, and rebuild the palaces of Solomon on Mount Zion
opt4: They shall pave the highway to Babylon with stone, and raise up the fallen watchtowers of Judah
correct: They shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations
explanation: The redeemed community repairs ruins that had lain desolate for generations, rebuilding ancient waste cities and restoring generational desolations. Isaiah 61:4 (KJV) - "And they shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations, and they shall repair the waste cities, the desolations of many generations."

question: What relentless, unceasing intercessory commitment does the prophet (or Messiah) vow for Jerusalem's vindication in Isaiah 62:1?
opt1: For the temple's sake I will fast forty days, and for the altar's sake I will weep until the glory returneth
opt2: For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth
opt3: For David's sake will I pray day and night, and for Jacob's heritage will I lift up my voice without ceasing
opt4: For the covenant's sake will I stand upon the watchtower, and for the exiles' sake will I blow the silver trumpet
correct: For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth
explanation: The speaker vows unceasing intercession and action without rest until Zion's righteousness blazes like the dawn and her salvation shines like a torch. Isaiah 62:1 (KJV) - "For Zion's sake will I not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until the righteousness thereof go forth as brightness, and the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth."

question: What two transformative new covenant names replace Zion's tragic titles 'Forsaken' and 'Desolate' in Isaiah 62:4?
opt1: Thou shalt be called Jedidiah, and thy land Moriah: for the Lord loveth thee, and thy borders are holy
opt2: Thou shalt be called Hadassah, and thy land Sharon: for the Lord hath chosen thee, and thy valleys are fruitful
opt3: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married
opt4: Thou shalt be called Naomi, and thy land Carmel: for the Lord hath comforted thee, and thy vineyards rejoice
correct: Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married
explanation: Reversing abandonment, God names Zion Hephzi-bah ('My Delight is in Her') and her land Beulah ('Married'), celebrating intimate covenant delight and divine union. Isaiah 62:4 (KJV) - "Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married."

question: To what exuberant marital joy does the prophet compare God's delight over redeemed Jerusalem in Isaiah 62:5?
opt1: As a father rejoiceth over his firstborn son, so shall the Almighty take pleasure in Mount Zion
opt2: As a king boasteth of his royal crown of gold, so shall the Lord of hosts glory in his holy city
opt3: As a shepherd delighteth in his unblemished flock, so shall the Shepherd of Israel lead his people
opt4: As a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee
correct: As a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee
explanation: God's love for Zion is depicted with intense romantic and bridal passion: rejoicing over His people as an enraptured bridegroom rejoices over his bride. Isaiah 62:5 (KJV) - "For as a young man marrieth a virgin, so shall thy sons marry thee: and as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy God rejoice over thee."

question: What 24/7 vigil of persistent prayer is assigned to the watchmen stationed on Jerusalem's walls in Isaiah 62:6-7?
opt1: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, and give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth
opt2: Watchmen that blow the shofar at every new moon, and sound an alarm whenever foreign armies approach
opt3: Sentinels that guard the gates from the uncircumcised, and keep the holy vessels of the temple from pollution
opt4: Prophets that proclaim judgment against the heathen, and anoint the kings of Judah with holy oil
correct: I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, and give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth
explanation: Intercessors ('watchmen') are stationed around the clock, commanded never to keep silent and literally to give God 'no rest' until He establishes Jerusalem as a global praise. Isaiah 62:6-7 (KJV) - "I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence, And give him no rest, till he establish, and till he make Jerusalem a praise in the earth."

question: What divine oath sworn by God's right hand guarantees agricultural security against foreign pillage in Isaiah 62:8-9?
opt1: The Lord hath sworn that the locust shall never devour the barley of Rephaim, nor the mildew blight the vines of Sibmah
opt2: The LORD hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: but they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness
opt3: The Almighty hath pledged that five hundred chariots shall defend the granaries, and no tax of silver be demanded
opt4: The Holy One hath promised that the early and latter rain shall never fail, and the presses shall overflow with oil
correct: The LORD hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: but they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness
explanation: God swears by His own almighty arm that foreign marauders will never again confiscate Judah's grain and wine; those who harvest will peacefully enjoy it within the temple courts. Isaiah 62:8-9 (KJV) - "The LORD hath sworn by his right hand, and by the arm of his strength, Surely I will no more give thy corn to be meat for thine enemies; and the sons of the stranger shall not drink thy wine, for the which thou hast laboured: But they that have gathered it shall eat it, and praise the LORD; and they that have brought it together shall drink it in the courts of my holiness."

question: What highway engineering instructions prepare the royal road for the arrival of the redeemed in Isaiah 62:10?
opt1: Pave the road with cut granite from the quarry; build bridges across the rivers; post sentinels every mile
opt2: Level the mountains of the north; dig wells along the caravan trails; plant shade trees in the desert
opt3: Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people
opt4: Open the double-leaved iron doors; sweep the marketplace of Jerusalem; burn incense on the towers
correct: Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people
explanation: The community is commanded to prepare the return route: clearing obstacles, elevating the causeway ('cast up'), clearing away loose stones, and raising a visible rallying standard. Isaiah 62:10 (KJV) - "Go through, go through the gates; prepare ye the way of the people; cast up, cast up the highway; gather out the stones; lift up a standard for the people."

question: What royal arrival proclamation is broadcast to the ends of the earth concerning the coming Saviour in Isaiah 62:11?
opt1: Proclaim among all nations: Behold, the King of glory cometh, riding upon a white horse with ten thousand saints
opt2: Sound the trumpet in all islands: Behold, the Judge of all flesh appeareth with the golden scepter of David
opt3: Cry aloud unto the Gentiles: Behold, the Redeemer entereth his sanctuary, and his glory shall cover the earth
opt4: Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him
correct: Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him
explanation: Quoted in Matthew 21:5 and Revelation 22:12, the global proclamation announces to Zion the arrival of her personal Salvation (Messiah), bringing His reward and recompense with Him. Isaiah 62:11 (KJV) - "Behold, the LORD hath proclaimed unto the end of the world, Say ye to the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy salvation cometh; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him."

question: What four glorious honorific titles will be given to the redeemed community in Isaiah 62:12?
opt1: The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken
opt2: The royal priesthood, The chosen generation, The perfection of beauty, The fortress of peace
opt3: The sons of the kingdom, The heritage of David, The crown of glory, The joy of all the earth
opt4: The pillars of truth, The light of the Gentiles, The planting of the Lord, The temple of praise
correct: The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken
explanation: The restored city and its citizens receive four permanent covenant titles: 'The holy people,' 'The redeemed of the LORD,' 'Sought out' (Derushah), and 'A city not forsaken.' Isaiah 62:12 (KJV) - "And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken."

question: What royal jewelry metaphor portrays Zion held safely in God's hand in Isaiah 62:3?
opt1: A signet ring of beaten gold upon the right hand of the King of kings
opt2: Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God
opt3: A breastplate of twelve sparkling gems worn before the ark of the covenant
opt4: A necklace of fine pearls from the sea, adorned with sapphires from Ophir
correct: Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God
explanation: Zion is prized as a spectacular crown of glory and royal diadem, displayed proudly and safely held in the palms of Yahweh's hands. Isaiah 62:3 (KJV) - "Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God."

question: What is the identity of the 'remembrancers' of the LORD mentioned in Isaiah 62:6?
opt1: The official court chroniclers who recorded the royal chronicles of the kings of Judah
opt2: The Levitical priests who blew the silver trumpets over the morning burnt offerings
opt3: Dedicated, persistent intercessors whose sacred duty is to constantly remind God of His covenant promises until Jerusalem is fully restored
opt4: The angelic scribes who write the deeds of the righteous in the heavenly book of life
correct: Dedicated, persistent intercessors whose sacred duty is to constantly remind God of His covenant promises until Jerusalem is fully restored
explanation: The phrase 'ye that make mention of the LORD' (ha-mazkirim et-Yahweh / God's remembrancers) designates unflagging intercessors holding God to His written word. Isaiah 62:6 (KJV) - "I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, which shall never hold their peace day nor night: ye that make mention of the LORD, keep not silence,"

question: What solitary, majestic Warrior approaches from Edom with blood-stained crimson garments in Isaiah 63:1?
opt1: The archangel Michael returning from the overthrow of the dragon in the wilderness of Paran
opt2: King Cyrus the Persian marching in victory with the plundered robes of the princes of Babylon
opt3: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save
opt4: The high priest coming forth from the holy of holies with the blood of the sin offering
correct: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save
explanation: The divine Messiah approaches as an awe-inspiring Champion from Bozrah (Edom's capital), clad in crimson-dyed robes, identifying Himself: 'I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save.' Isaiah 63:1 (KJV) - "Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength? I that speak in righteousness, mighty to save."

question: Why are the Warrior's garments stained red like one who treads in an ancient winepress in Isaiah 63:2-3?
opt1: Because he was wounded on the cross for the transgressions of his people, and his own blood covered his vesture
opt2: Because he offered ten thousand rams upon the altar of Bozrah to cleanse the land from idolatry
opt3: Because the archers of the heathen shot at him, and pierced his armor with bronze arrows in battle
opt4: I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment
correct: I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment
explanation: Quoted in Revelation 19:13, 15, the red stains on His robes are not His own blood, but the lifeblood of crushed, rebellious nations trodden down in the winepress of divine wrath. Isaiah 63:2-3 (KJV) - "Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat? I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments, and I will stain all my raiment."

question: What dual eschatological calendar governs the Warrior's solo intervention in Isaiah 63:4-5?
opt1: For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come ... mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me
opt2: The seventy years of exile are completed, and the jubilee of liberty hath arrived
opt3: The hour of judgment is proclaimed, and the sabbatical year of rest hath dawned
opt4: The time of the Gentiles is fulfilled, and the reign of the house of David is established
correct: For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come ... mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me
explanation: The Warrior acts with solo omnipotence: combining the day of retributive vengeance upon oppressors with the arrival of the grand Jubilee year of redemption for His people. Isaiah 63:4-5 (KJV) - "For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come. And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me."

question: What profound empathy and divine presence delivered Israel in all her historical tribulations in Isaiah 63:9?
opt1: In all their distress he sent his prophets, and the priests of Aaron sprinkled the blood of the covenant
opt2: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old
opt3: He watched over their caravans with ten thousand angels, and parted the sea with an east wind
opt4: He remembered his holy oath unto Abraham, and defended their borders with chariots of fire
correct: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old
explanation: One of the most touching verses in the Old Testament: God personally shares the suffering of His people ('in all their affliction he was afflicted'), saving them through the Angel of His Presence. Isaiah 63:9 (KJV) - "In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old."

question: How did Israel's chronic rebellion grieve the Holy Spirit, turning God into their adversary in Isaiah 63:10?
opt1: They broke the tablets of stone, and worshipped the golden calf; therefore the plague consumed three thousand men
opt2: They despised the manna of the wilderness, and murmured against Moses; therefore fiery serpents bit the people
opt3: But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them
opt4: They served the baals of Canaan, and rejected the temple; therefore the sword of Babylon plundered Zion
correct: But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them
explanation: Quoted in Ephesians 4:30 ('grieve not the Holy Spirit'), Israel's persistent rebellion caused deep personal grief to the Holy Spirit, provoking God to fight against them as an enemy. Isaiah 63:10 (KJV) - "But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them."

question: What Exodus retrospection recalls God's Holy Spirit leading the flock through the Red Sea in Isaiah 63:11-14?
opt1: Where is the pillar of cloud that shielded our fathers from Pharaoh's host in the desert?
opt2: Where is the rock of Horeb that gushed with living waters when Moses smote it with his rod?
opt3: Where is the ark of the covenant that divided the Jordan before the priests of Joshua?
opt4: Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock? where is he that put his holy Spirit within him? that led them by the right hand of Moses with his glorious arm, dividing the water before them ... as a beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest
correct: Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock? where is he that put his holy Spirit within him? that led them by the right hand of Moses with his glorious arm, dividing the water before them ... as a beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest
explanation: The prophet recalls the golden age of Moses, where the Holy Spirit resided within the leadership and guided the nation as gently as cattle descending into a quiet pasture valley. Isaiah 63:11-12, 14 (KJV) - "Then he remembered the days of old, Moses, and his people, saying, Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock? where is he that put his holy Spirit within him? That led them by the right hand of Moses with his glorious arm, dividing the water before them, to make himself an everlasting name? ... As a beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest: so didst thou lead thy people, to make thyself a glorious name."

question: What bold confession of divine Paternity claims God as Father above Abraham or Jacob in Isaiah 63:16?
opt1: Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O LORD, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting
opt2: Thou art our Creator, and we are the sheep of thy hand: remember the covenant of our fathers
opt3: Thou art the King of Israel, and we are thy servants: do not forsake the work of thine own hands
opt4: Thou art the Rock of our salvation, and we are thy chosen seed: deliver us from the pit of corruption
correct: Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O LORD, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting
explanation: Even if the revered patriarchs Abraham and Jacob (Israel) were dead, unaware, or disowned them, Yahweh Himself remains their true, eternal Father and Redeemer. Isaiah 63:16 (KJV) - "Doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Israel acknowledge us not: thou, O LORD, art our father, our redeemer; thy name is from everlasting."

question: What mournful complaint laments that foreign adversaries desecrated the holy sanctuary in Isaiah 63:18?
opt1: The golden vessels of Solomon are carried away to Shinar, and the altar is burned with fire
opt2: The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary
opt3: The house of prayer is become a den of thieves, and the gates of Zion lie in ruins
opt4: The cherubim have departed from the mercy seat, and the songs of the Levites are silenced
correct: The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary
explanation: Compared to eternity, Israel possessed her holy land and temple only briefly before foreign adversaries ruthlessly trampled down the sanctuary. Isaiah 63:18 (KJV) - "The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary."

question: What sorrowful alienation concludes Chapter 63, contrasting Israel with pagan nations that never bore God's name in Isaiah 63:19?
opt1: We are like sheep without a shepherd, while the heathen dwell in fortified cities of peace
opt2: We have become as Sodom and Gomorrah, while the uncircumcised boast of their golden idols
opt3: We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name
opt4: We wander in darkness without a guide, while the kings of the east rejoice in their palaces
correct: We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name
explanation: Israel appeals to her unique covenant status: despite current misery, we belong to You, whereas pagan conquerors were never ruled by You or called by Your holy name. Isaiah 63:19 (KJV) - "We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name."

question: What is the theological significance of the Warrior treading the winepress 'alone' in Isaiah 63:3?
opt1: It signifies that King Hezekiah had no allies when Sennacherib besieged the walls of Jerusalem
opt2: It proves that the high priest alone could enter into the holy of holies on the Day of Atonement
opt3: It indicates that Cyrus conquered Babylon without the assistance of the Medes or Persians
opt4: It reveals that the ultimate cosmic defeat of evil and execution of divine justice cannot be accomplished by human armies, but solely by the solitary omnipotence of the Messiah
correct: It reveals that the ultimate cosmic defeat of evil and execution of divine justice cannot be accomplished by human armies, but solely by the solitary omnipotence of the Messiah
explanation: The imagery underscores the absolute solitariness and unique sufficiency of the Messiah: in both atoning sacrifice (cross) and final judgment (winepress), He stands alone without creaturely help. Isaiah 63:3 (KJV) - "I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me: for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury;"

question: What passionate prayer pleads for God to tear open the heavens and descend in mountain-melting power in Isaiah 64:1-2?
opt1: Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke; cast forth lightning, and scatter them
opt2: Awake, awake, put on thy strength, O arm of the Lord; descend upon the clouds of Mount Sinai with thunder and fire
opt3: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him; as smoke is driven away
opt4: Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might flow down at thy presence, as when the melting fire burneth, the fire causeth the waters to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence!
correct: Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might flow down at thy presence, as when the melting fire burneth, the fire causeth the waters to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence!
explanation: The prophet cries out for a visible, dramatic theophany: tearing apart the celestial skies so that mountains dissolve like boiling water before God's terrifying presence. Isaiah 64:1-2 (KJV) - "Oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might flow down at thy presence, As when the melting fire burneth, the fire causeth the waters to boil, to make thy name known to thine adversaries, that the nations may tremble at thy presence!"

question: What unmatched, unprecedented grace has God prepared for those who wait for Him in Isaiah 64:4?
opt1: For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him
opt2: The glory of the heavenly Jerusalem paved with gold, and the tree of life bearing twelve manner of fruits
opt3: An eternal kingdom where sorrow and sighing flee away, and the righteous shine as the brightness of the firmament
opt4: The secret mysteries of the covenant kept hidden from the foundation of the earth, revealed unto his holy apostles
correct: For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him
explanation: Quoted in 1 Corinthians 2:9, no human ear has heard and no eye has ever seen any god like Yahweh, who acts so magnificently on behalf of those who patiently wait for Him. Isaiah 64:4 (KJV) - "For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him."

question: What devastating confession exposes human self-righteousness as putrid defilement and withered leaves in Isaiah 64:6?
opt1: Our hearts are deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know them? we are all gone out of the way
opt2: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away
opt3: We were shapen in iniquity, and in sin did our mothers conceive us: there is none that doeth good, no, not one
opt4: Our lips are polluted with falsehood, and our hands stained with blood: we are as broken potsherds cast into the pit
correct: But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away
explanation: Even humanity's best moral deeds ('all our righteousnesses') are repulsive like ritual pollution rags ('filthy rags' / beged iddim, menstrual cloths), leaving us withered like dead leaves blown by the gale. Isaiah 64:6 (KJV) - "But we are all as an unclean thing, and all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags; and we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities, like the wind, have taken us away."

question: What tragic spiritual apathy and divine withdrawal is lamented in Isaiah 64:7?
opt1: The prophets have ceased from the land, and no man seeketh after the law of the Lord; the sanctuary is forgotten
opt2: The priests sleep in the gates, and the elders offer strange fire at the altar; all flesh hath corrupted its way
opt3: And there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee: for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us, because of our iniquities
opt4: Our prayers are returned empty, and our fasting is rejected; the heavens are as brass above our heads
correct: And there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee: for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us, because of our iniquities
explanation: Society is paralyzed by spiritual lethargy: not a single person exerts himself to take hold of God in passionate intercession, while God hides His face due to their sins. Isaiah 64:7 (KJV) - "And there is none that calleth upon thy name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of thee: for thou hast hid thy face from us, and hast consumed us, because of our iniquities."

question: What tender pottery prayer appeals to God's creative craftsmanship and fatherhood in Isaiah 64:8?
opt1: Remember, O Lord, that we are but dust, and our days are as a shadow that declineth on the wall
opt2: Thou hast formed our bones in secret, and fashioned our souls according to thy sovereign purpose
opt3: We are the sheep of thy pasture, and thou art our Shepherd; lead us not into temptation
