opt4: But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand
correct: But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand
explanation: The community casts itself entirely on sovereign mercy: acknowledging God as Father, submitting as pliable clay to the divine Potter, pleading that He will not destroy the work of His own hands. Isaiah 64:8 (KJV) - "But now, O LORD, thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand."

question: What tragic destruction of Solomon's magnificent temple is mourned in Isaiah 64:11?
opt1: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned up with fire: and all our pleasant things are laid waste
opt2: The ark of the covenant is taken by the heathen, and the golden cherubim are broken in pieces by the Chaldeans
opt3: The two bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz are melted down, and the altar of burnt offerings is cast into the dust
opt4: The holy of holies is defiled by foreign soldiers, and the cedar carvings of palm trees are hacked with axes
correct: Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned up with fire: and all our pleasant things are laid waste
explanation: Looking ahead to 586 BC, the prophet grieves the incineration of the first temple: 'our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned up with fire.' Isaiah 64:11 (KJV) - "Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised thee, is burned up with fire: and all our pleasant things are laid waste."

question: What agonizing closing question challenges God's apparent restraint and prolonged silence in Isaiah 64:12?
opt1: How long, LORD? wilt thou hide thyself for ever? shall thy wrath burn like fire upon the house of Jacob?
opt2: Wilt thou refrain thyself for these things, O LORD? wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?
opt3: Wilt thou be angry with us forever? wilt thou draw out thine anger to all generations?
opt4: Lord, where are thy former lovingkindnesses, which thou swarest unto David in thy truth?
correct: Wilt thou refrain thyself for these things, O LORD? wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?
explanation: The intercessory prayer closes on a suspenseful, raw note: can Yahweh remain silent and restrain His compassion while His sanctuary lies in ashes and His people are crushed? Isaiah 64:12 (KJV) - "Wilt thou refrain thyself for these things, O LORD? wilt thou hold thy peace, and afflict us very sore?"

question: What desolation overtook the urban landscape of Judah according to Isaiah 64:10?
opt1: The walls of Zion are plowed like a field, and foxes run across the heights of Mount Moriah
opt2: The gates of Judah are burned with brimstone, and wild asses graze in the palaces of the king
opt3: Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation
opt4: The vineyards of the hill country are choked with thorns, and no man passeth through the cities
correct: Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation
explanation: Judah's once-thriving cities, including sacred Zion and Jerusalem, were reduced to empty, barren wilderness wastelands. Isaiah 64:10 (KJV) - "Thy holy cities are a wilderness, Zion is a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation."

question: What does the phrase 'neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him' reveal about God's character in Isaiah 64:4?
opt1: That God reveals the blueprints of the heavenly city exclusively to the prophets of Israel
opt2: That no human being can look upon God's unveiled face without suffering instant physical death
opt3: That the mysteries of the end times are sealed within the golden ark of the sanctuary
opt4: Unlike manufactured pagan idols that demand exhausting labor from worshippers, Yahweh is the only God who graciously works and acts on behalf of those who wait for Him
correct: Unlike manufactured pagan idols that demand exhausting labor from worshippers, Yahweh is the only God who graciously works and acts on behalf of those who wait for Him
explanation: The verse highlights the radical uniqueness of Yahweh: pagan gods demand constant service, but Yahweh is the only God who actively works and intervenes for those who trust Him. Isaiah 64:4 (KJV) - "For since the beginning of the world men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither hath the eye seen, O God, beside thee, what he hath prepared for him that waiteth for him."

question: What posture towards God's judgment is confessed in Isaiah 64:5?
opt1: Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways: behold, thou art wroth; for we have sinned
opt2: The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works, though our houses be desolate
opt3: Thy judgments are true and righteous altogether, more to be desired than fine gold from Ophir
opt4: Righteous art thou, O LORD, when I plead with thee: yet let me talk with thee of thy judgments
correct: Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways: behold, thou art wroth; for we have sinned
explanation: The community confesses that God warmly welcomes those who practice joyful righteousness, but acknowledges that their present misery is the direct consequence of persistent sin. Isaiah 64:5 (KJV) - "Thou meetest him that rejoiceth and worketh righteousness, those that remember thee in thy ways: behold, thou art wroth; for we have sinned: in those is continuance, and we shall be saved."

question: How does Paul quote Isaiah 65:1-2 in Romans 10 to explain the inclusion of Gentiles and the rejection of Israel?
opt1: I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people
opt2: The Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising, but the children of the kingdom shall be cast out
opt3: I will provoke you to jealousy by them that are no people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you, saith the Lord
opt4: Out of Zion shall come the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob, but blind eyes cannot perceive it
correct: I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people
explanation: In Romans 10:20-21, Paul reveals that verse 1 prophesies Gentile conversion (found by those who never sought Him), while verse 2 depicts God standing with outstretched hands all day long toward obstinate, rebellious ethnic Israel. Isaiah 65:1-2 (KJV) - "I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts;"

question: What nauseating self-righteous hypocrisy is compared to continuous irritating smoke in God's nostrils in Isaiah 65:5?
opt1: Which offer sacrifices of swine upon the altar, and boast that their hands are clean before the law
opt2: Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day
opt3: Which wear broad phylacteries in the market, and say, We are the children of Abraham and need no repentance
opt4: Which fast twice in the week, and say, God, I thank thee that I am not as other men are, extortioners or unjust
correct: Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day
explanation: Pagan syncretists who practiced grave-necromancy and ate pork arrogantly claimed superior sanctity ('Stand by thyself; I am holier than thou'), producing an offensive stench like irritating smoke in God's nose. Isaiah 65:5 (KJV) - "Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou. These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day."

question: What agricultural proverb of the grape cluster spares the righteous remnant from total national destruction in Isaiah 65:8?
opt1: As an olive tree beaten with a rod, leaving two or three berries on the topmost bough, so shall the remnant survive
opt2: As a gleaner gathering ears of corn in the valley of Rephaim, so will the Lord rescue the seed of David
opt3: As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all
opt4: As a root sprouting from the stump of an oak, so shall the holy seed take root in the promised land
correct: As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all
explanation: Just as a vinedresser refuses to throw away an entire defective grape bunch because a few juicy grapes contain sweet wine ('a blessing is in it'), God spares the whole nation for the sake of the godly remnant. Isaiah 65:8 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, As the new wine is found in the cluster, and one saith, Destroy it not; for a blessing is in it: so will I do for my servants' sakes, that I may not destroy them all."

question: What pagan deities of Fortune and Destiny are denounced for tempting apostates to set tables of food and drink in Isaiah 65:11-12?
opt1: Ye that sacrifice unto Baal-peor on the mountains, and pour libations unto the queen of heaven in the streets
opt2: Ye that bow before Chemosh in the valleys, and offer your children to Molech in the fire of Tophet
opt3: Ye that worship the golden bull of Bethel, and consult the astrologers of Babylon under the green trees
opt4: But ye are they that forsake the LORD, that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for that troop, and that furnish the drink offering unto that number. Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter
correct: But ye are they that forsake the LORD, that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for that troop, and that furnish the drink offering unto that number. Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter
explanation: Apostates set cultic banquet tables for Gad (pagan god of Fortune/'that troop') and Meni (god of Fate/Destiny/'that number'); God plays on Meni: He will 'number' them to the slaughtering sword! Isaiah 65:11-12 (KJV) - "But ye are they that forsake the LORD, that forget my holy mountain, that prepare a table for that troop, and that furnish the drink offering unto that number. Therefore will I number you to the sword, and ye shall all bow down to the slaughter: because when I called, ye did not answer; when I spake, ye did not hear; but did evil before mine eyes, and did choose that wherein I delighted not."

question: What sharp fourfold contrast distinguishes the joyful destiny of God's true servants from the starvation of apostates in Isaiah 65:13-14?
opt1: Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit
opt2: My servants shall sit on thrones of gold, but ye shall wander in chains; my servants shall wear fine linen, but ye shall be clad in sackcloth
opt3: My servants shall inherit the holy mountain, but ye shall be cast into the pit; my servants shall drink of the river, but ye shall perish in drought
opt4: My servants shall shine as the sun, but ye shall sleep in darkness; my servants shall feast at the altar, but ye shall be devoured by the sword
correct: Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit
explanation: God draws a stark, absolute dichotomy: His faithful servants eat, drink, rejoice, and sing for joy of heart, while religious hypocrites starve, thirst, face public shame, and howl in agony. Isaiah 65:13-14 (KJV) - "Therefore thus saith the Lord GOD, Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit."

question: What monumental cosmic re-creation is announced, permanently obliterating the memory of past sorrow in Isaiah 65:17?
opt1: Behold, I rebuild Jerusalem with sapphires and carbuncles, and her walls shall reach unto the firmament
opt2: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind
opt3: Behold, I make all kingdoms subject unto the house of David, and the earth shall be filled with gold
opt4: Behold, I roll back the skies like a scroll, and the throne of glory shall descend upon Mount Zion
correct: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind
explanation: Quoted in 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1, God promises the ultimate cosmic regeneration: creating a brand-new heavens and earth where all former grief is so completely erased that it never comes to mind. Isaiah 65:17 (KJV) - "For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind."

question: What extraordinary longevity and reversal of infant mortality characterizes the restored Messianic community in Isaiah 65:20?
opt1: A man shall live a thousand years like the days of Adam, and sickness shall be utterly unknown in the gates
opt2: Death shall have no power over the righteous, and their children shall multiply as the stars of heaven
opt3: There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed
opt4: The aged shall renew their youth like the eagle, and infants shall possess the strength of mighty men
correct: There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed
explanation: In this millennial portrayal of longevity, premature infant death is abolished, living to age 100 is considered mere childhood, and only an unrepentant sinner dying at 100 is considered cursed. Isaiah 65:20 (KJV) - "There shall be no more thence an infant of days, nor an old man that hath not filled his days: for the child shall die an hundred years old; but the sinner being an hundred years old shall be accursed."

question: To what enduring natural monument is the lifespan of God's elect compared in Isaiah 65:22?
opt1: As the days of the sun upon the firmament, so shall their generations flourish in peace
opt2: As the ancient mountains of Judah, so shall their inheritance abide throughout all ages
opt3: As the stars of heaven, so shall the children of the covenant shine without fading
opt4: As the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands
correct: As the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands
explanation: Believers will live long, peaceful lives paralleling ancient, deep-rooted trees (like centuries-old oaks or olive trees), fully enjoying the houses they build and vineyards they plant. Isaiah 65:22 (KJV) - "They shall not build, and another inhabit; they shall not plant, and another eat: for as the days of a tree are the days of my people, and mine elect shall long enjoy the work of their hands."

question: What instantaneous divine communion anticipates the prayers of the redeemed in Isaiah 65:24?
opt1: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear
opt2: Their petitions shall ascend with the morning incense, and the angel of the covenant shall answer with peace
opt3: They shall knock, and the gates of heaven shall be opened; they shall seek, and immediately find
opt4: I will write their requests upon the palms of my hands, and fulfill all the desire of their hearts
correct: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear
explanation: Intimacy with God reaches absolute perfection: Yahweh answers before words are formed, granting requests while prayers are still on the lips. Isaiah 65:24 (KJV) - "And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear."

question: What peaceful reconciliation of wild beasts and humiliation of the serpent concludes Isaiah 65:25?
opt1: The leopard and the kid shall sleep in the olive grove, and the eagle shall nest beside the dove
opt2: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD
opt3: The dragon shall be cast out into the outer sea, and the leviathan shall praise God in the deep
opt4: The wild beasts shall be banished beyond the Euphrates, and only domestic flocks shall graze in Zion
correct: The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD
explanation: Reiterating the Edenic peace of Chapter 11, carnivores eat vegetation alongside prey, violence is permanently banished, and the serpent remains crawling in the dust under the Genesis 3:14 curse. Isaiah 65:25 (KJV) - "The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent's meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD."

question: What cosmic throne-room declaration exposes the impossibility of containing God in an earthly stone temple in Isaiah 66:1-2?
opt1: Behold, the heaven of heavens cannot contain thee; how much less this house that I have builded for thy name?
opt2: God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands
opt3: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? For all those things hath mine hand made ... but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word
opt4: The Lord is in his holy temple, the Lord's throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men
correct: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? For all those things hath mine hand made ... but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word
explanation: Quoted by Stephen in Acts 7:49-50, the Creator whose throne is heaven and footstool is earth needs no stone building; the true sanctuary He delights in is the humble, contrite heart that trembles reverently at His word. Isaiah 66:1-2 (KJV) - "Thus saith the LORD, The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest? For all those things hath mine hand made, and all those things have been, saith the LORD: but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembleth at my word."

question: What shocking abominations does God equate with hypocritical, unrepentant animal sacrifices in Isaiah 66:3?
opt1: He that offereth a ram is as if he shed innocent blood; and he that sprinkleth salt, as if he cursed the covenant
opt2: He that bringeth a heifer is as if he bowed before Baal; and he that titheth mint, as if he robbed the poor
opt3: He that slayeth a goat is as if he practiced witchcraft; and he that poureth wine, as if he drank with the heathen
opt4: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol
correct: He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol
explanation: Outward ritualism performed with an unrepentant heart is totally abhorrent to God: slaughtering an ox is equated with murder, a lamb offering with snapping a dog's neck, grain oblations with offering swine's blood, and incense with blessing an idol! Isaiah 66:3 (KJV) - "He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man; he that sacrificeth a lamb, as if he cut off a dog's neck; he that offereth an oblation, as if he offered swine's blood; he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol. Yea, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delighteth in their abominations."

question: How did self-righteous religious brethren mock the faithful remnant who trembled at God's word in Isaiah 66:5?
opt1: Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed
opt2: They said, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were
opt3: They mocked them in the gate, saying, Behold the mourners of Zion who refuse to drink wine with the princes
opt4: They cast them into prison, saying, Let your God deliver you if he delighteth in your prayers
correct: Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed
explanation: Religious formalists excommunicated and cast out humble believers with sanctimonious sneers ('Let the LORD be glorified!'), but God promises that Messiah will appear to vindicate the faithful while shaming the persecutors. Isaiah 66:5 (KJV) - "Hear the word of the LORD, ye that tremble at his word; Your brethren that hated you, that cast you out for my name's sake, said, Let the LORD be glorified: but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed."

question: What miraculous instantaneous delivery of a male child and national birth occurs without labor pains in Isaiah 66:7-8?
opt1: In forty days of mourning, the twelve tribes were restored; in a single night of victory, the exiles returned
opt2: Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children
opt3: As the sun ariseth in the east, so did the kingdom of David appear without the sword or bow of iron
opt4: Like an olive tree springing from the rock, so was the remnant gathered from the four winds in an hour
correct: Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children
explanation: In an unprecedented miracle violating natural biology, Zion gives birth to a male child (Messiah) before experiencing labor pains, and a whole redeemed nation is born in a single day! Isaiah 66:7-8 (KJV) - "Before she travailed, she brought forth; before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child. Who hath heard such a thing? who hath seen such things? Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day? or shall a nation be born at once? for as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children."

question: What maternal nursing metaphor portrays God's tender comfort of His people in Jerusalem in Isaiah 66:12-13?
opt1: As an eagle fluttereth over its young and beareth them upon its wings, so will the Lord carry Jacob
opt2: As a shepherd gently leadeth the ewes with young, so shall the Holy One guide his flock in peace
opt3: Ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees. As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem
opt4: As a father pitieth his children when they weep, so the Lord of hosts will wipe away your tears
correct: Ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees. As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem
explanation: God expresses His boundless compassion through maternal imagery: holding His children on His hip, dandling them on His lap, and comforting them as a tender mother comforts her child. Isaiah 66:12-13 (KJV) - "Then shall ye suck, ye shall be borne upon her sides, and be dandled upon her knees. As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem."

question: How does the LORD arrive to execute judgment by fire upon all ungodly flesh in Isaiah 66:15-16?
opt1: He shall march from Mount Paran with ten thousand holy angels, and his sword shall divide the waters
opt2: He shall descend upon Mount Sinai with thick darkness, and his arrows of lightning shall scatter the kings
opt3: He shall send a destroying pestilence through the four corners of the earth, and the oceans shall burn with sulfur
opt4: For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many
correct: For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many
explanation: Yahweh arrives in apocalyptic majesty with whirlwind chariots and consuming fire, executing worldwide judicial retribution ('plead with all flesh') by fire and sword. Isaiah 66:15-16 (KJV) - "For, behold, the LORD will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will the LORD plead with all flesh: and the slain of the LORD shall be many."

question: To what distant Gentile coastlands and nations will surviving Jewish missionaries be sent to declare God's glory in Isaiah 66:19?
opt1: Unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles
opt2: To Babylon, Media, Persia, and the provinces of the east bordering the great river
opt3: To Egypt, Pathros, Cush, and the desert cities of Sheba and Dedan
opt4: To Damascus, Hamath, Arpad, and the maritime ports of Tyre and Sidon
correct: Unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles
explanation: God commissions rescued witnesses as global missionaries to remote Gentile lands: Tarshish (Spain), Pul/Lud (North Africa), Tubal (Asia Minor/Black Sea), Javan (Greece), and distant islands to proclaim His glory. Isaiah 66:19 (KJV) - "And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, that draw the bow, to Tubal, and Javan, to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles."

question: What astonishing inclusion allows Gentiles to be consecrated into the sacred Levitical priesthood in Isaiah 66:20-21?
opt1: They shall be circumcised according to the law of Moses, and minister as porters in the outer court
opt2: They shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD out of all nations ... and I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD
opt3: They shall offer ten thousand talents of silver to support the sons of Aaron at the bronze altar
opt4: They shall be designated honorary proselytes, and worship on the high feast days in Jerusalem
correct: They shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD out of all nations ... and I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD
explanation: A revolutionary prophecy shattering Old Covenant tribal boundaries: God will select consecrated ministers from among Gentile converts ('take of them') to serve as priests and Levites before Him! Isaiah 66:20-21 (KJV) - "And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the LORD out of all nations ... to my holy mountain Jerusalem, saith the LORD, as the children of Israel bring an offering in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD. And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites, saith the LORD."

question: What unceasing cosmic worship schedule will unite all flesh in perpetual adoration before God in Isaiah 66:22-23?
opt1: From the Feast of Passover unto the Feast of Tabernacles shall all the kings of the earth bring tribute unto Zion
opt2: Throughout the seven thousand years of the kingdom shall the righteous rejoice before the throne of glory
opt3: For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD
opt4: Every morning and every evening shall the angels and the saints offer the incense of praise in the temple
correct: For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD
explanation: Just as the New Heavens and New Earth endure forever, redeemed humanity will gather in perpetual, rhythmic worship from Sabbath to Sabbath and New Moon to New Moon before Yahweh. Isaiah 66:22-23 (KJV) - "For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the LORD, so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the LORD."

question: What chilling, undying punishment of transgressors concludes the entire Book of Isaiah in Isaiah 66:24?
opt1: They shall be cast into the outer darkness, where there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth forever
opt2: The memory of the wicked shall rot in the dust, and their names shall be blotted out from the book of life
opt3: The ungodly shall sink like lead into the bottomless pit, and the smoke of their torment shall ascend for ever
opt4: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh
correct: And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh
explanation: Quoted by Jesus three times in Mark 9:44, 46, 48 regarding Gehenna (Hell), the Book of Isaiah concludes with the eternal judgment of rebels: their consuming worm never dies, their tormenting fire is never extinguished, and their fate is an abhorrence to all flesh. Isaiah 66:24 (KJV) - "And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh."
